If you are her parent, brother or sister, say it out loud: you can come home whenever you need to. A woman who believes that door is closed may stay in a home that is not safe. Call when her husband's family is not listening. Ask specific questions: are you sleeping, do you have money of your own, is anyone hurting you.

If you are worried, ask directly whether she has thought about suicide. A calm, direct question tells her someone noticed.

Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline on 14416, offers counselling to anyone in need [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. She can call for herself; you can call to ask how to help. Nobody is punished for surviving an attempt: the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 presumes severe stress and obliges the government to provide care [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. If the home itself is the danger, treat it as violence, not as a mood, and call 112 in an emergency.

A housewife is not a category. She is a person doing unpaid work in a house that may or may not be safe for her. The data cannot see her. The people around her can.
housewives-suicide-india-ncrb-data.hg:
2022 mein India mein 25,309 auratein, jinhe police ne housewife ke roop mein darj kiya, suicide se mari. Yeh us saal suicide se mari 48,172 auraton ka 52.5% tha, aur saare suicides ka 14.8% [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Student suicides, jin pe kahin zyada headlines banti hain, usi saal 13,044 the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Housewives ki ginti iski lagbhag do guna thi. Phir bhi in pe koi national baatcheet nahi hoti, shayad isliye ki yeh maut us ek jagah hoti hain jise India private maanta hai.

## Har saat mein se ek suicide: NCRB ki table mein housewives kahan hain

Yeh figures Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India se aate hain, woh saalana report jo National Crime Records Bureau police records se banata hai. Isne 2022 mein 1,70,924 suicides gine [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Inmein 71.8% mard the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]], aur us pe alag se dhyaan dena zaroori hai.

Dekho ki table logon ko kaise baantti hai. Mardon mein sabse bada group daily wage earners ka tha. Auraton mein sabse bada group housewives ka tha [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Daily wage earners, jo zyada tar mard hain, 45,185 the, yaani total ka 26.4%; housewives lagbhag har saat mein se ek thi [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Mard is hisaab se darj hote hain ki woh kaise kamaate hain. Auratein us ghar ke hisaab se jise woh sambhaalti hain.

Yeh counts hain, rates nahi. Indian auraton ka bahut bada hissa homemaker ke roop mein darj hota hai, isliye bada count kuch had tak bada group bhi dikhata hai. Table yeh dikhati hai ki auraton ki sabse zyada maut kahan hain, aur isliye bachaav ko kahan pahunchna hai.

NCRB ki baad ki reports ke hisaab se total suicides 2023 mein 1,71,418 the aur 2024 mein 1,70,746 [[theprint-ncrb-adsi-2024]]. Un saalon ke liye housewives ki ginti kisi doosre source se confirm nahi ho paayi, isliye yeh story 2022 ki tables pe hi tiki hai.

## "Family problems" ka matlab kya-kya ho sakta hai

Har maut ke liye police ek cause darj karti hai. 2022 mein shaadi se judi problems ke alawa baaki family problems saare suicides ka 31.7% thi, illness 18.4% aur shaadi se judi problems 4.8% [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. Yeh hisse sab logon ke hain, sirf auraton ke nahi. Jiski maut hui, woh khud yeh cause nahi bata sakti, isliye entry is pe tiki hoti hai ki baad mein police ko kya bataya gaya. Jab ek shaadi-shuda aurat apne pati ke ghar mein marti hai, toh uski maut ke baare mein batane wale wahi log ho sakte hain jinke saath woh rehti thi.

"Housewife" utna hi chhupata hai jitna "family problems". Yeh occupation wale column mein likha jaata hai, lekin iske saath na tankhwah aati hai, na fixed ghante, na chhutti, na colleagues. Bahut si auratein is kaam mein tab aati hain jab woh apne maa-baap aur doston se door kisi doosri family ke ghar mein rehne jaati hain. Paisa, phone aur baahar jaane ki ijaazat, sab kisi aur ke haath mein ho sakta hai. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook "housewife" ki jagah "homemaker" likhne ko kehti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Surveys jo cheez record karte hain, woh hai hinsa. NFHS-5 mein 31.9% ever-married auraton ne kaha ki unhone pati ki taraf se physical, sexual ya emotional violence jheli hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jin auraton ne kisi ki bhi taraf se physical ya sexual violence jheli, unmein se 77.2% ne kabhi madad nahi maangi aur kisi ko bataya bhi nahi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 ne lagbhag 1% adults ko high suicidal risk pe paaya, aur auraton mein 1.14% ko [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Iski summary yeh bhi kehti hai ki high risk wale logon mein se aadhon ko koi aur mental disorder nahi tha. Takleef hamesha kisi ek insaan ke andar ki beemari nahi hoti. Kabhi-kabhi woh uske aas-paas ki zindagi ka jawab hoti hai.

Ek situation socho. Kanpur ki ek 28 saal ki aurat, jiski shaadi ko paanch saal ho gaye hain, apne pati ki family ke saath rehti hai. Uske paas ek degree hai jo kabhi kaam nahi aayi, aur apne naam ka koi bank account nahi. Jab usne apni maa ko bataya ki pati haath uthata hai, toh jawab mila ki har shaadi mein adjust karna padta hai, toh usne batana hi chhod diya. Uske hafte ka kuch bhi kisi record mein nahi aayega. Aur uska har hissa aisa hai jise koi doosra insaan badal sakta hai.

## Abetment cases: jab kanoon maut aur cruelty ke beech ka rishta dekhta hai

Kabhi-kabhi police ek aurat ki maut ko is baat se jodti hai ki uske saath kaisa bartaav hua. 2024 mein police ne auraton ke suicide ke liye uksaane (abetment) ke 4,220 cases darj kiye, jinmein 4,284 victims thi, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Sections 107 aur 108 ke tahat ya, 1 July 2024 se pehle ke offences ke liye, IPC ke Sections 305 aur 306 ke tahat. 2022 mein yeh ginti 4,963 thi aur 2023 mein 4,825 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

2022 mein, jab 48,172 auratein suicide se mari, police ne lagbhag har das maut pe ek abetment case darj kiya. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki har das mein se ek maut ke peeche cruelty thi; suicide ki shayad hi kabhi ek akeli wajah hoti hai. Iska matlab yeh hai ki lagbhag har das maut mein se ek pe police ne criminal case khola. Dono ginti NCRB ki alag-alag reports se hain, isliye is anupaat ko sirf mota andaaza samjho.

Kanoon maut se pehle bhi kaam kar sakta hai. BNS ke Sections 85 aur 86 pati ya uske rishtedaaron ki cruelty pe 3 saal tak ki jail aur jurmaane ki saza dete hain, aur cruelty ki definition mein woh jaan-boojh ke kiya gaya bartaav bhi aata hai jo aurat ko suicide ki taraf dhakel sakta ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police ne 2024 mein cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Akelapan kismat nahi hai: kya kaam aata hai

World Health Organization saaf kehta hai ki suicide roke ja sakte hain [[who-suicide]]. Ghar mein rehne wali aurat ke liye bachaav ka matlab zyada tar yahi hai: roz ka aam rishta, aur baahar nikalne ka ek asli raasta.

Agar tum uske maa-baap, bhai ya behen ho, toh yeh baat bol ke kaho: tum jab chaaho ghar aa sakti ho. Jis aurat ko lagta hai ki woh darwaza band ho chuka hai, woh ek unsafe ghar mein ruki reh sakti hai. Tab call karo jab pati ki family sun na rahi ho. Seedhe sawaal poochho: neend aa rahi hai, tumhare paas apne paise hain, koi tumhe takleef toh nahi de raha.

Agar fikar ho rahi hai, toh seedha poochho ki kya usne suicide ke baare mein socha hai. Shaanti se seedha poochha gaya sawaal use batata hai ki kisi ne dhyaan diya.

Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free aur din-raat chalne wali helpline 14416, har us insaan ko counselling deti hai jise zaroorat ho [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Woh khud ke liye call kar sakti hai; tum yeh poochhne ke liye call kar sakte ho ki madad kaise karein. Attempt ke baad bach jaane pe kisi ko saza nahi hoti: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 maanta hai ki aisa insaan severe stress mein tha aur sarkar ki zimmedari banata hai ki use care de [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Agar khatra ghar hi hai, toh use hinsa samjho, mood nahi, aur emergency mein 112 pe call karo.

Housewife koi category nahi hai. Woh ek insaan hai jo bina tankhwah ka kaam ek aise ghar mein kar rahi hai jo uske liye safe ho bhi sakta hai aur nahi bhi. Data use nahi dekh sakta. Uske aas-paas ke log dekh sakte hain.

intersex-rights-india-2026-law.en:
Imagine a baby born in a district hospital in Nashik. The nurse pauses before saying "boy" or "girl". By evening an uncle is asking how soon an operation can "settle it". Now imagine the same person at 26: raised as a girl, living as a woman, never once having thought of herself as transgender. India's transgender law, as amended in 2026, writes people like her into the definition of a "transgender person" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. This explainer is about that mismatch, and about what the law still leaves to relatives and surgeons. It is general information, not legal advice.

## What intersex means, and what it does not

Some people are born with sex characteristics, such as chromosomes, hormone patterns, internal organs or genitals, that do not fit the typical definitions of male or female. These are called intersex variations [[unesco-itgse]]. Some are noticed at birth, some only at puberty, some never. They are natural differences between bodies, not an illness and nobody's fault.

Intersex is about how a body developed. Transgender is about gender identity: a person's own sense of who they are, when it differs from the sex recorded at birth. Sexual orientation, meaning whom a person is attracted to, is a third thing. An intersex person may be a man or a woman, may be transgender or non-binary, may be straight, gay or asexual. Being intersex decides none of that.

India has no official count of intersex people that we could find. Census 2011 offered one box beyond male and female: "other". 4,87,803 people chose it, and the government still uses that figure as the transgender population [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. The census did not ask about intersex variations.

## Inside the transgender definition: the 2026 change

The amended Section 2(k) says a "transgender person" means a person with socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta, or a eunuch, or "a person with intersex variations", along with people compelled to assume a transgender identity. A proviso adds that the term shall not include "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

The list names communities, and it names a kind of body. What it shuts out is self-perception. Trans-men, trans-women and genderqueer persons, who were named in the 2019 definition, no longer are [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

> An intersex woman who has never called herself transgender is inside the definition. A trans man who has lived by that word for years is no longer named in it.

The test has moved from who you say you are to what kind of body or community you come from. It moved fast: the bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 13 March 2026 and passed by both houses within 12 days [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. It has been in force since 25 May 2026 [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Surgery on babies: the consent question

For many intersex people the first rights question arrives in the first weeks of life. A baby whose genitals look different needs a prompt check by a specialist children's team, because a few of the underlying conditions need medical treatment quickly.

That check cannot wait. Surgery done only to make a body look typical can. It cannot be undone, it can affect how the body feels and functions for the rest of the person's life, and the child may grow up to identify differently from the sex a surgeon chose. The one person who has to live with the result is the one person nobody asked.

On 16 April 2024, following the Supreme Court's Supriyo judgment, the Centre set up a six-member committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary. Its terms include measures so that queer persons are not subjected to "involuntary medical treatments, surgeries, etc." [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. More than two and a half years later, we could not find any report from it.

## From NALSA's self-identification to medical boards

On 15 April 2014, in NALSA v. Union of India, the Supreme Court recognised transgender persons as a "third gender" and upheld their right to self-identify their gender [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Section 4(2) of the 2019 Act then gave a person recognised as transgender "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

The 2026 amendment deletes that sub-section. A District Magistrate now issues a transgender certificate only after examining the recommendation of a medical board headed by a Chief Medical Officer or a deputy [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

For an intersex adult whose body may have been a hospital file since birth, the law now offers a document under a label many of them do not use, on the say of one more panel of doctors.

The certificate reached few people even under self-identification. A petition filed in the Supreme Court on 15 June 2026 cites Ministry of Social Justice data showing 33,189 certificates issued nationwide, about 7% of the Census 2011 count [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. The amendment is under challenge. On 17 August 2026 the Union told the Supreme Court that identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act would continue to operate while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

## What families and intersex adults can do

If a baby in your family is born with a variation, get the medical check first. Go to hospital at once if the baby vomits, feeds poorly, is very sleepy or cannot pass urine. Then ask each doctor two questions: what is medically necessary now, and what can wait until the child can take part in the decision? Get the diagnosis and test results in writing, and keep the file for the child. A relative's hurry is not a medical reason.

As the child grows, tell them the truth about their body in words they can handle. Secrecy teaches shame faster than any diagnosis.

If you are an intersex adult, ask the hospitals that treated you for your childhood records. You do not have to call yourself transgender to be treated with respect by a doctor, a school or an employer. If you hold a certificate, or want one, keep every document safe and follow the Supreme Court case. Free legal aid is available on the National Legal Services Authority's helpline [[nalsa]], and Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and open round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
intersex-rights-india-2026-law.hg:
Sochiye, Nashik ke ek district hospital mein ek baby paida hota hai. Nurse "ladka" ya "ladki" bolne se pehle ruk jaati hai. Shaam tak ek chacha pooch rahe hote hain ki operation kitni jaldi ho sakta hai, taaki baat "settle" ho jaye. Ab usi insaan ko 26 saal ki umar mein sochiye: ladki ki tarah pali-badhi, aurat ki tarah jee rahi hai, aur usne khud ko kabhi transgender nahi samjha. India ka transgender law, jaisa 2026 mein amend hua, us jaise logon ko "transgender person" ki definition ke andar likhta hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Yeh explainer isi mismatch ke baare mein hai, aur us sawaal ke baare mein jo law aaj bhi rishtedaaron aur surgeons par chhod deta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Intersex ka matlab kya hai, aur kya nahi

Kuch log aise sex characteristics ke saath paida hote hain, jaise chromosomes, hormone patterns, internal organs ya genitals, jo male ya female ki typical definitions mein fit nahi hote. Inhe intersex variations kehte hain [[unesco-itgse]]. Kuch variations birth par dikh jaate hain, kuch sirf puberty mein pata chalte hain, aur kuch kabhi pata hi nahi chalte. Yeh bodies ke beech ke natural differences hain, koi bimari nahi, aur kisi ki galti nahi.

Intersex is baare mein hai ki body kaise develop hui. Transgender gender identity ke baare mein hai: insaan ki apni samajh ki woh kaun hai, jab woh birth par darj kiye gaye sex se alag ho. Sexual orientation, yaani insaan kis ki taraf attract hota hai, ek teesri cheez hai. Ek intersex insaan aadmi ho sakta hai ya aurat, transgender ho sakta hai ya non-binary, straight, gay ya asexual ho sakta hai. Intersex hona inme se kuch bhi tay nahi karta.

India mein intersex logon ki koi official ginti humein nahi mili. Census 2011 mein male aur female ke alawa sirf ek box tha: "other". 4,87,803 logon ne use chuna, aur sarkar aaj bhi isi figure ko transgender population maanti hai [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Census ne intersex variations ke baare mein poocha hi nahi.

## Transgender definition ke andar: 2026 ka badlaav

Amended Section 2(k) kehta hai ki "transgender person" ka matlab hai aisa insaan jiski socio-cultural identity kinner, hijra, aravani ya jogta jaisi ho, ya eunuch, ya "a person with intersex variations", aur saath mein woh log jinhe transgender identity apnane par majboor kiya gaya. Ek proviso yeh bhi jodta hai ki is term mein "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" shaamil nahi honge [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Yeh list communities ke naam leti hai, aur ek tarah ki body ka naam leti hai. Jo cheez bahar kar di gayi hai, woh hai self-perception. Trans-men, trans-women aur genderqueer log, jinka naam 2019 ki definition mein tha, ab usme nahi hain [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

> Jis intersex aurat ne khud ko kabhi transgender nahi kaha, woh definition ke andar hai. Jo trans man barson se isi shabd ke saath jee raha hai, uska naam ab usme nahi hai.

Test ab yeh nahi raha ki aap khud ko kya kehte hain. Test yeh ho gaya hai ki aapki body kis tarah ki hai ya aap kis community se aate hain. Aur yeh sab bahut tezi se hua: bill 13 March 2026 ko Lok Sabha mein introduce hua aur 12 days ke andar dono houses se pass ho gaya [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. 25 May 2026 se yeh lagu hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Babies par surgery: consent ka sawaal

Bahut se intersex logon ke liye rights ka pehla sawaal zindagi ke pehle kuch hafton mein hi aa jaata hai. Jis baby ke genitals alag dikhte hain, use specialist children's team ko jaldi dikhana zaroori hai, kyunki kuch underlying conditions ka ilaaj jaldi shuru karna padta hai.

Yeh check ruk nahi sakta. Jo surgery sirf body ko typical dikhane ke liye ki jaati hai, woh ruk sakti hai. Woh wapas nahi ho sakti, woh poori zindagi body ke mehsoos karne aur kaam karne ke tareeke par asar daal sakti hai, aur ho sakta hai bachcha bada hokar khud ko us sex se alag samjhe jo surgeon ne chuna tha. Jis ek insaan ko is nateeje ke saath poori zindagi jeeni hai, usi ek insaan se kisi ne poocha nahi.

16 April 2024 ko, Supreme Court ke Supriyo judgment ke baad, Centre ne Cabinet Secretary ki chairmanship mein six-member committee banayi. Uske terms mein aise measures shaamil hain jinse queer logon par "involuntary medical treatments, surgeries, etc." na thope jaayein [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. Dhaai saal se zyada beet chuke hain, aur humein us committee ki koi report nahi mili.

## NALSA ke self-identification se medical boards tak

15 April 2014 ko NALSA v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne transgender persons ko "third gender" maana aur apna gender khud identify karne ke unke haq ko upheld kiya [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Phir 2019 Act ke Section 4(2) ne transgender ke roop mein recognised har insaan ko "a right to self-perceived gender identity" diya [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

2026 ka amendment yeh sub-section hata deta hai. Ab District Magistrate transgender certificate tabhi issue karta hai jab woh us medical board ki recommendation dekh le jiska head Chief Medical Officer ya unka deputy hota hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Jis intersex adult ki body shayad paida hote hi hospital ki file ban gayi thi, use law ab ek document deta hai, ek aise label ke neeche jo unme se bahut log khud use nahi karte, aur woh bhi doctors ke ek aur panel ke kehne par.

Certificate self-identification ke daur mein bhi bahut kam logon tak pahuncha. 15 June 2026 ko Supreme Court mein file hui ek petition Ministry of Social Justice ke data ka hawala deti hai: poore desh mein 33,189 certificates issue hue, jo Census 2011 ki ginti ka lagbhag 7% hai [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. Amendment ko court mein challenge kiya gaya hai. 17 August 2026 ko Union ne Supreme Court ko bataya ki 2019 Act ke under jo identity cards pehle se issue ho chuke hain, woh case pending rehne tak chalte rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

## Families aur intersex adults kya kar sakte hain

Agar aapki family mein koi baby variation ke saath paida hua hai, toh sabse pehle medical check karwaiye. Agar baby ulti kare, feed theek se na le, bahut sust rahe ya urine pass na kar paye, toh turant hospital jaiye. Phir har doctor se do sawaal poochiye: abhi medically kya zaroori hai, aur kya tab tak ruk sakta hai jab tak bachcha khud faisle mein shaamil ho sake? Diagnosis aur test results likhit mein lijiye, aur yeh file bachche ke liye sambhaal kar rakhiye. Kisi rishtedaar ki jaldbaazi koi medical reason nahi hai.

Jaise-jaise bachcha bada ho, use uski body ke baare mein sach bataiye, aise shabdon mein jo woh samajh sake. Chhupana kisi bhi diagnosis se zyada tezi se sharam sikhata hai.

Agar aap intersex adult hain, toh jin hospitals mein aapka ilaaj hua, unse apne bachpan ke records maangiye. Doctor, school ya employer se respect paane ke liye aapko khud ko transgender kehne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Agar aapke paas certificate hai, ya aap banwana chahte hain, toh har document sambhaal kar rakhiye aur Supreme Court ke case par nazar rakhiye. Free legal aid National Legal Services Authority ki helpline par milti hai [[nalsa]], aur Tele-MANAS 14416 free hai aur chaubees ghante khula rehta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

lgbtq-rights-india-timeline-2009-2026.en:
Line up the dates that changed life for LGBTQ+ Indians since 2009 and a pattern shows quickly. Nearly every gain is a judgment. The sharpest recent loss is an Act of Parliament, passed in March 2026 within 12 days of its introduction [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. This timeline covers 17 years and notes, each time, who acted: a court, a regulator or the legislature.

| Date | What happened | Who acted |
|---|---|---|
| 2 July 2009 | Consensual gay sex decriminalised (Naz Foundation) | Delhi High Court |
| 11 December 2013 | That verdict reversed (Koushal) | Supreme Court |
| 15 April 2014 | Right to self-identify gender recognised (NALSA) | Supreme Court |
| 6 September 2018 | Section 377 read down (Navtej Singh Johar) | Supreme Court |
| 17 October 2023 | Same-sex marriage left to Parliament (Supriyo) | Supreme Court |
| 25 March 2026 | Amendment ending self-identification passed | Parliament |

## 2009-2013: decriminalised, then criminal again

On 2 July 2009 the Delhi High Court ruled in Naz Foundation that Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code could not be used to punish sex between consenting adults. On 11 December 2013 the Supreme Court reversed that verdict in Suresh Kumar Koushal, and consensual gay sex was a crime again for nearly five years [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Imagine a gay man who turned 18 in Delhi that July. At 18 the law left him alone. At 22 he was, on paper, a criminal again, though nothing about him had changed. Through all of it the section sat in the statute book, unamended.

## 2014-2018: NALSA and Navtej

Four months after Koushal, the Supreme Court moved the other way on gender identity. On 15 April 2014, in NALSA v. Union of India, it recognised transgender persons as a "third gender", upheld their right to self-identify their gender and extended them protection under Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 and 21 [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Then, on 6 September 2018, five judges in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India unanimously read down Section 377. Consensual sex between adults of the same sex was no longer a crime; non-consensual acts and bestiality stayed offences [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. The man in our example was 27.

Parliament added one narrow protection in these years. Section 21 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 bars discrimination in mental health care on any basis and names sexual orientation among the grounds [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## 2019-2022: a transgender law and a conversion-therapy ban

The statute that followed NALSA took more than five years. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 came into force on 10 January 2020. Its Rules were notified on 25 September 2020, and a national portal for certificates and identity cards opened on 25 November 2020 [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Section 4(2) of the Act put NALSA's core idea into law: "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

On conversion therapy, the push again came from a court. In June 2021 the Madras High Court directed that any attempt to medically "cure" or change a person's sexual orientation or gender identity be prohibited, with action up to withdrawal of the professional's licence [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

The regulator moved only after the court directed it to: in a letter dated 25 August 2022 to all state medical councils, the National Medical Commission declared conversion therapy professional misconduct [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

## 2023-2025: the marriage case and a committee

On 17 October 2023, five Supreme Court judges in Supriyo v. Union of India unanimously held that there is no fundamental right to marry and declined to recognise same-sex marriage, leaving it to Parliament. On civil unions the bench split 3:2 against. It did hold that a transgender person in a heterosexual relationship can marry under existing laws [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]].

Parliament has not legislated on it. What came instead was a committee: on 16 April 2024 the Centre set up a six-member panel chaired by the Cabinet Secretary to recommend measures against discrimination, violence and involuntary medical treatment of queer persons [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. We could find no published report from it. On 9 January 2025 the Supreme Court dismissed the petitions asking it to review Supriyo [[barandbench-supriyo-review-dismissed-2025]].

Parliament did act once in this period, by subtraction. When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024, it dropped Section 377 and added no replacement [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Its own Standing Committee on Home Affairs had warned on 10 November 2023 that this would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. The part of Section 377 that Navtej had kept to protect people went with the rest.

## 2026: the amendment and the challenge

The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 13 March 2026, passed there on 24 March and cleared the Rajya Sabha on 25 March [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. It received the President's assent on 30 March and came into force on 25 May 2026 [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

The amendment omits Section 4(2), the right to self-perceived gender identity. A District Magistrate may now issue a transgender certificate only after examining the recommendation of a medical board. The new definition says the term does not include "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. The Supreme Court recognised self-identification in 2014. Parliament wrote it into law in 2019 and wrote it out in 2026, in 12 days.

On 17 August 2026 a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant heard petitions challenging the amendment, and the Union said identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act would continue to operate while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

Three lessons sit in these dates. A right that rests on one judgment can be undone by a later bench, as 2013 showed. A right written into a statute can be deleted in under two weeks, as 2026 showed. And when Parliament stays silent, as on marriage, the silence is the decision.

The man who turned 18 in 2009 is 35 now, and the law still does not let him marry his partner. This is general information, not legal advice. If the back-and-forth wears you down, Tele-MANAS offers free counselling round the clock on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
lgbtq-rights-india-timeline-2009-2026.hg:
2009 se ab tak jin dates ne LGBTQ+ Indians ki zindagi badli, unhe ek line mein rakhiye, pattern turant dikh jaata hai. Lagbhag har jeet ek judgment hai. Haal ki sabse badi haar Parliament ka ek Act hai, jo March 2026 mein introduce hone ke 12 din ke andar pass ho gaya [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. Yeh timeline 17 saal cover karti hai aur har baar note karti hai ki kadam kisne uthaya: court ne, regulator ne ya legislature ne.

| Date | Kya hua | Kisne kiya |
|---|---|---|
| 2 July 2009 | Consensual gay sex decriminalise hua (Naz Foundation) | Delhi High Court |
| 11 December 2013 | Woh verdict palat diya gaya (Koushal) | Supreme Court |
| 15 April 2014 | Apna gender khud identify karne ka right maana gaya (NALSA) | Supreme Court |
| 6 September 2018 | Section 377 read down hua (Navtej Singh Johar) | Supreme Court |
| 17 October 2023 | Same-sex marriage Parliament par chhod di gayi (Supriyo) | Supreme Court |
| 25 March 2026 | Self-identification khatam karne wala amendment pass hua | Parliament |

## 2009-2013: decriminalise hua, phir dobara crime

2 July 2009 ko Delhi High Court ne Naz Foundation case mein kaha ki Indian Penal Code ka Section 377 consenting adults ke beech sex ko punish karne ke liye use nahi ho sakta. 11 December 2013 ko Supreme Court ne Suresh Kumar Koushal case mein yeh verdict palat diya, aur consensual gay sex lagbhag paanch saal ke liye phir se crime ban gaya [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Sochiye ek gay ladka jo usi July mein Delhi mein 18 ka hua. 18 ki umar mein law ne use akela chhod diya. 22 ki umar mein woh kaagaz par phir se criminal tha, jabki usme kuch nahi badla tha. Is poore time mein yeh section statute book mein waise ka waisa pada raha, bina kisi amendment ke.

## 2014-2018: NALSA aur Navtej

Koushal ke chaar mahine baad Supreme Court gender identity par ulti disha mein gaya. 15 April 2014 ko NALSA v. Union of India mein usne transgender persons ko "third gender" maana, apna gender khud identify karne ka unka right upheld kiya aur unhe Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 aur 21 ki protection di [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Phir 6 September 2018 ko Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India mein paanch judges ne ek-rai se Section 377 ko read down kiya. Same sex ke adults ke beech consensual sex ab crime nahi tha; non-consensual acts aur bestiality offence bane rahe [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Hamare example wala ladka tab 27 ka tha.

In saalon mein Parliament ne ek hi chhoti si protection jodi. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ka Section 21 mental health care mein kisi bhi basis par discrimination ko rokta hai, aur grounds mein sexual orientation ka naam leta hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## 2019-2022: ek transgender law aur conversion therapy par ban

NALSA ke baad jo statute aaya, usme paanch saal se zyada lage. Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, 10 January 2020 ko lagu hua. Uske Rules 25 September 2020 ko notify hue, aur certificates aur identity cards ke liye national portal 25 November 2020 ko khula [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Act ke Section 4(2) ne NALSA ka core idea law mein likh diya: "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

Conversion therapy par bhi dhakka ek court se hi aaya. June 2021 mein Madras High Court ne direction di ki kisi ki sexual orientation ya gender identity ko medically "cure" ya change karne ki har koshish prohibit ki jaaye, aur professional ka licence wapas lene tak ka action ho [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

Regulator tabhi hila jab court ne use direct kiya: 25 August 2022 ki ek letter mein, jo saare state medical councils ko bheji gayi, National Medical Commission ne conversion therapy ko professional misconduct declare kiya [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

## 2023-2025: marriage case aur ek committee

17 October 2023 ko Supriyo v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ke paanch judges ne ek-rai se kaha ki marry karne ka koi fundamental right nahi hai, aur same-sex marriage ko recognise karne se mana karke mamla Parliament par chhod diya. Civil unions par bench 3:2 se khilaaf rahi. Court ne yeh zaroor maana ki heterosexual relationship mein rehne wala transgender insaan existing laws ke tahat shaadi kar sakta hai [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]].

Parliament ne is par koi law nahi banaya. Uski jagah ek committee aayi: 16 April 2024 ko Centre ne Cabinet Secretary ki chairmanship mein chhe members ka panel banaya, jo queer persons ke saath hone wale discrimination, violence aur involuntary medical treatment ke khilaaf measures recommend kare [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. Hamein uski koi published report nahi mili. 9 January 2025 ko Supreme Court ne Supriyo ke review ki petitions dismiss kar din [[barandbench-supriyo-review-dismissed-2025]].

Is dauraan Parliament ne ek baar kadam uthaya, lekin kuch ghata kar. 1 July 2024 ko jab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ne IPC ki jagah li, toh usne Section 377 hata diya aur uski jagah kuch nahi rakha [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Uski apni Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne 10 November 2023 ko warning di thi ki isse men aur transgender persons ke against non-consensual sexual offences ki koi saza nahi bachegi [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Section 377 ka jo hissa Navtej ne logon ki protection ke liye bachaya tha, woh bhi baaki ke saath chala gaya.

## 2026: amendment aur challenge

Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, 13 March 2026 ko Lok Sabha mein introduce hua, 24 March ko wahan pass hua aur 25 March ko Rajya Sabha se bhi pass ho gaya [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. 30 March ko use President ki assent mili aur 25 May 2026 se woh lagu ho gaya [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Amendment Section 4(2) ko, yaani self-perceived gender identity ke right ko, hata deta hai. Ab District Magistrate transgender certificate tabhi issue kar sakta hai jab woh ek medical board ki recommendation examine kar le. Nayi definition kehti hai ki is term mein "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" shaamil nahi hain [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Supreme Court ne 2014 mein self-identification ko maana. Parliament ne 2019 mein use law mein likha aur 2026 mein law se kaat diya, 12 din mein.

17 August 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ki lead wali Supreme Court bench ne amendment ko challenge karne wali petitions suni, aur Union ne kaha ki 2019 Act ke tahat pehle se issue hue identity cards case pending rehne tak chalte rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

In dates mein teen sabak hain. Jo right ek judgment par tika ho, use baad ki koi bench palat sakti hai, jaisa 2013 ne dikhaya. Jo right statute mein likha ho, woh do hafte se kam mein kaata ja sakta hai, jaisa 2026 ne dikhaya. Aur jab Parliament chup rehti hai, jaise marriage par, toh woh chuppi hi faisla hoti hai.

Jo ladka 2009 mein 18 ka hua tha, woh ab 35 ka hai, aur law ab bhi use apne partner se shaadi nahi karne deta. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar yeh aage-peeche aapko thaka raha hai, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 par free counselling deta hai, 24x7 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

lgbtqia-basics-orientation-identity-law.en:
Imagine a Class 11 student in Pune. A classmate is called "gay" because he is soft-spoken. A news clip calls a trans woman "a hijra". A relative, talking about a newborn with an intersex variation, says the baby "is a transgender". Three different things have been treated as one.

Since 2026, India's transgender law makes a version of the same mistake. To see how, start with the three questions the letters LGBTQIA+ answer.

## Three different questions: attraction, identity, body

| The question | The term | Some answers |
|---|---|---|
| Whom are you attracted to? | Sexual orientation | heterosexual, gay, lesbian, bisexual, asexual |
| Who are you? | Gender identity | man, woman, non-binary; cisgender or transgender |
| How did your body develop? | Sex characteristics | typically male, typically female, intersex variations |

The answers are independent. A trans woman can be straight, lesbian or bisexual. A gay man is a man. A person born with an intersex variation may be a man, a woman or neither, straight or gay. Being intersex does not make someone transgender.

People also confuse all three with gender expression: clothes, voice, hair, manner. A gentle boy or a short-haired girl has told you nothing about attraction, identity or body.

None of these answers is an illness. None needs a cure.

## L, G, B, T, Q, I, A: each letter in plain words

- **L, lesbian:** a woman attracted to women.
- **G, gay:** a man attracted to men.
- **B, bisexual:** attracted to more than one gender.
- **T, transgender:** gender identity differs from the sex recorded at birth. This includes trans men, trans women and non-binary people, and communities such as hijra, kinner, aravani and jogta; not every transgender person belongs to one.
- **Q, queer or questioning:** an umbrella word many use for themselves, or "I am still working it out".
- **I, intersex:** born with chromosomes, hormones or anatomy that do not fit the typical male or female pattern. It is about the body.
- **A, asexual:** little or no sexual attraction; not the same as choosing celibacy.

So L, G, B and A answer the attraction question, T the identity question and I the body question. Official data has never kept them apart. Census 2011 had one gender category beyond male and female, "other", and counted 4,87,803 people in it. The government still treats that as the transgender population, although anyone could choose "other" and many transgender people were recorded as male or female [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

## What the courts recognised: NALSA and Navtej

The Supreme Court dealt with the questions one at a time, and kept them distinct.

**Identity.** On 15 April 2014, in *NALSA v. Union of India*, the court recognised transgender persons as a "third gender" and upheld their right to self-identify their gender [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. The test was the person's own sense of self, not a medical examination.

**Orientation.** On 6 September 2018, in *Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India*, a five-judge bench unanimously read down Section 377 of the IPC, so that consensual sex between adults of the same sex is no longer a crime [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Parliament has kept the categories apart too. Section 21 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 bars discrimination in mental health care "on any basis including gender, sex, sexual orientation", listing each as its own ground [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. And in 2023 the Supreme Court held that a transgender person in a heterosexual relationship is entitled to marry under existing marriage laws [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. That ruling treats who you are and whom you love as two separate facts.

## What the 2026 amendment says, and what it conflates

The 2019 transgender law gave every transgender person "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. The Amendment Act of 2026, in force from 25 May 2026, deleted that right and rewrote the definition. A "transgender person" now means a person with socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta, a "eunuch" (the Act's word), a person with intersex variations, or a person forced into a transgender identity. The definition ends with a proviso [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]:

> "Provided that it shall not include, nor shall ever have been so included, persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities."

Set against the three questions, this mixes the categories in three ways.

**Body is filed under identity.** Intersex persons are placed inside "transgender", though an intersex variation is about how a body developed, not about who a person is.

**Identity is blurred with orientation.** The proviso excludes people with "different sexual orientations", but orientation was never what made anyone transgender. The phrase "self-perceived sexual identities" does not say whether it means gender or sexuality. Trans men, trans women and genderqueer persons, who were named in the 2019 definition, are no longer listed.

**A community is treated as the whole category.** Hijra, kinner, aravani and jogta communities are part of the transgender population, not all of it. A trans man who has never belonged to any such community has no clear place in the new wording.

The amendment also makes a District Magistrate issue a transgender certificate only after examining the recommendation of a medical board [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. That turns a question of identity back into an inspection of the body. The law is under challenge in the Supreme Court. At a hearing on 17 August 2026, the Union said identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act would continue to operate while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Talking about it respectfully

Five habits cover most situations.

- Use the name and pronoun a person asks for.
- Do not ask about bodies, surgery or sex lives.
- Never "out" anyone. Who they tell, and when, is their decision.
- Hijra and kinner are names of communities. Do not use them as insults, or as a label for every transgender person.
- If you get a word wrong, correct yourself and move on.

If these questions are about you, there is no deadline for answering them. Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free, open round the clock, and its counselling is for anyone in need, including transgender persons [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
lgbtqia-basics-orientation-identity-law.hg:
Socho, Pune ka ek Class 11 ka student. Ek classmate ko "gay" kaha jaata hai kyunki woh dheere bolta hai. Ek news clip ek trans woman ko "hijra" kehti hai. Ek rishtedaar, intersex variation ke saath paida hue ek newborn ke baare mein baat karte hue, kehta hai ki bachcha "transgender hai". Teen alag cheezon ko ek maan liya gaya.

2026 se India ka transgender law bhi isi galti ka ek version karta hai. Kaise, yeh samajhne ke liye un teen sawaalon se shuru karo jinka jawab LGBTQIA+ ke letters dete hain.

## Teen alag sawaal: attraction, identity, body

| Sawaal | Term | Kuch jawab |
|---|---|---|
| Tum kiski taraf attract hote ho? | Sexual orientation | heterosexual, gay, lesbian, bisexual, asexual |
| Tum kaun ho? | Gender identity | man, woman, non-binary; cisgender ya transgender |
| Tumhari body kaise develop hui? | Sex characteristics | typically male, typically female, intersex variations |

Yeh jawab ek-doosre se independent hain. Ek trans woman straight, lesbian ya bisexual ho sakti hai. Ek gay man, man hi hai. Intersex variation ke saath paida hua insaan man ho sakta hai, woman ho sakta hai ya dono mein se koi nahi, straight ho sakta hai ya gay. Intersex hone se koi transgender nahi ho jaata.

Log in teeno ko gender expression ke saath bhi mila dete hain: kapde, awaaz, baal, andaaz. Ek naram-mizaaj ladke ya chhote baalon wali ladki ne tumhe attraction, identity ya body ke baare mein kuch nahi bataya.

Inme se koi bhi jawab bimaari nahi hai. Kisi ko ilaaj ki zaroorat nahi.

## L, G, B, T, Q, I, A: har letter seedhe shabdon mein

- **L, lesbian:** woh aurat jo auraton ki taraf attract hoti hai.
- **G, gay:** woh mard jo mardon ki taraf attract hota hai.
- **B, bisexual:** jo ek se zyada gender ki taraf attract ho.
- **T, transgender:** jiski gender identity janam par record hue sex se alag hai. Isme trans men, trans women aur non-binary log aate hain, aur hijra, kinner, aravani aur jogta jaisi communities bhi; har transgender insaan kisi community ka hissa nahi hota.
- **Q, queer ya questioning:** ek umbrella word jo bahut log apne liye use karte hain, ya "main abhi samajh raha hoon".
- **I, intersex:** aise chromosomes, hormones ya anatomy ke saath paida hona jo male ya female ke typical pattern mein fit nahi hote. Yeh body ke baare mein hai.
- **A, asexual:** jise sexual attraction bahut kam ya bilkul nahi hota; yeh celibacy chunne jaisa nahi hai.

Yaani L, G, B aur A attraction wale sawaal ka jawab hain, T identity wale ka aur I body wale ka. Official data ne inhe kabhi alag nahi rakha. Census 2011 mein male aur female ke alawa ek hi gender category thi, "other", aur usme 4,87,803 log gine gaye. Government aaj bhi isi ko transgender population maanti hai, jabki "other" koi bhi chun sakta tha aur bahut se transgender log male ya female mein darj hue [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

## Courts ne kya maana: NALSA aur Navtej

Supreme Court ne in sawaalon ko ek-ek karke dekha, aur alag-alag rakha.

**Identity.** 15 April 2014 ko *NALSA v. Union of India* mein court ne transgender logon ko "third gender" ke roop mein maanyata di aur apna gender khud pehchaanne ke unke right ko barkaraar rakha [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Test insaan ka apna ehsaas tha ki woh kaun hai, koi medical examination nahi.

**Orientation.** 6 September 2018 ko *Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India* mein paanch judges ki bench ne ek-rai se IPC ki Section 377 ko read down kiya, jisse same sex ke adults ke beech consensual sex ab crime nahi hai [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Parliament ne bhi categories ko alag rakha hai. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ki Section 21 mental health care mein discrimination par rok lagati hai, "on any basis including gender, sex, sexual orientation", aur har ek ko alag ground ki tarah ginati hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Aur 2023 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki heterosexual relationship mein rehne wala transgender insaan maujooda marriage laws ke under shaadi karne ka haqdaar hai [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. Yeh faisla "tum kaun ho" aur "tum kisse pyaar karte ho" ko do alag facts maanta hai.

## 2026 ka amendment kya kehta hai, aur kya mila deta hai

2019 ke transgender law ne har transgender insaan ko "a right to self-perceived gender identity" diya tha [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. 2026 ke Amendment Act ne, jo 25 May 2026 se lagu hai, woh right hata diya aur definition dobara likh di. Ab "transgender person" ka matlab hai: kinner, hijra, aravani aur jogta jaisi socio-cultural identities wala insaan, "eunuch" (yeh Act ka apna word hai), intersex variations wala insaan, ya woh insaan jise zabardasti transgender identity mein dhakela gaya. Definition ek proviso par khatam hoti hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]:

> "Provided that it shall not include, nor shall ever have been so included, persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities."

Teen sawaalon ke saamne rakh kar dekho, toh yeh categories ko teen tarah se mila deta hai.

**Body ko identity ke khaate mein daal diya gaya.** Intersex logon ko "transgender" ke andar rakha gaya hai, jabki intersex variation is baare mein hai ki body kaise develop hui, is baare mein nahi ki insaan kaun hai.

**Identity ko orientation ke saath dhundhla kar diya gaya.** Proviso "different sexual orientations" wale logon ko bahar rakhta hai, lekin kisi ko transgender banane wali cheez orientation kabhi thi hi nahi. "Self-perceived sexual identities" wala phrase yeh nahi batata ki uska matlab gender hai ya sexuality. Trans men, trans women aur genderqueer log, jinka naam 2019 ki definition mein tha, ab list mein nahi hain.

**Ek community ko poori category maan liya gaya.** Hijra, kinner, aravani aur jogta communities transgender population ka hissa hain, poori population nahi. Jo trans man kabhi aisi kisi community ka hissa nahi raha, uske liye naye shabdon mein koi saaf jagah nahi hai.

Amendment yeh bhi kehta hai ki District Magistrate transgender certificate tabhi issue karega jab woh ek medical board ki recommendation dekh le [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Isse identity ka sawaal phir se body ki jaanch ban jaata hai. Is law ko Supreme Court mein challenge kiya gaya hai. 17 August 2026 ki hearing mein Union ne kaha ki 2019 Act ke under pehle se issue hue identity cards case pending rehne tak chalte rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Is baare mein izzat se baat kaise karein

Paanch aadatein zyada tar situations sambhal leti hain.

- Insaan jo naam aur pronoun bataye, wahi use karo.
- Body, surgery ya sex life ke baare mein mat poochho.
- Kisi ko kabhi "out" mat karo. Woh kisko batayein aur kab, yeh unka faisla hai.
- Hijra aur kinner communities ke naam hain. Inhe gaali ki tarah use mat karo, na har transgender insaan ke label ki tarah.
- Agar koi word galat bol do, toh khud ko correct karo aur aage badho.

Agar yeh sawaal tumhare apne baare mein hain, toh jawab dene ki koi deadline nahi hai. Tele-MANAS 14416 free hai, din-raat khuli hai, aur iski counselling har zaroorat-mand ke liye hai, transgender logon ke liye bhi [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

love-affairs-murders-possessive-violence.en:
Every year the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) sorts India's murders by motive: dowry, witchcraft, political reasons, class conflict. One column is headed "love affairs". In 2024 it held 1,391 murders. The column beside it, "honour killing", held 36 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is more than 38 times as many killings filed under love as under honour, and the table does not explain what kind of love ends this way.

## The motive column nobody reads: 1,391 'love affairs' murders

"Love affairs" is not an offence. It is a label police attach to a murder case when they report it. NCRB only compiles what state police send, and says it is not responsible for the authenticity of the information [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The honour column has been tiny for years: 25 in 2020, 33 in 2021, 18 in 2022, 38 in 2023 and 36 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. The volume sits next door, under "love affairs" and the even larger "illicit relationship" column.

## What sits inside the category, and what slips out

At least three different killings can be filed under "love affairs":

- a person killed by a partner, an ex or a rejected admirer who would not accept a no;
- a person killed by a rival;
- a couple, or one of them, killed by relatives who opposed the relationship.

The third is what most people mean by an honour killing. The official honour count is widely regarded as a large under-count, because honour killing is not a separate offence and many such murders are logged under "love affairs" or other motives [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The table does not say whether the person killed was a woman or a man, or who the accused was.

Some killings never reach the table, because motive data cover only cases registered as murder [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In April 2025 the Supreme Court set aside orders that had let an alleged honour killing in Uttar Pradesh be tried as culpable homicide instead of murder, called it "a clear case of honour killing" and ordered a murder charge [[barandbench-honour-killing-lesser-charge-2025]].

## Possessiveness, stalking, threats: the slide to violence

Consider a hypothetical. A 23-year-old in Nagpur ends a two-year relationship. He calls through the night, then starts waiting outside her office. He tells her that if she will not be his, she will not be anyone's. Her friends call it heartbreak. Her family never knew about the relationship, so she cannot tell them. Nobody treats that sentence as what it is: a threat to kill.

The law has a name for the middle of that story. Following a woman and repeatedly contacting her after she has clearly shown she is not interested is stalking under Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), punishable with up to three years in prison, or five on a repeat conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 9,865 stalking cases in 2024. Courts convicted in 25.2% of the stalking trials they completed that year, and 92.8% of the stalking cases before them were still pending when it ended [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

What the data cannot do is join the stages. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. When stalking and a killing are in the same FIR, the case is counted as a murder and the stalking drops out of the statistics. NCRB's tables do not show how many of the 1,391 killings came after a stalking complaint, a threat or an earlier FIR.

Data from France, South Africa and Colombia show that between 22% and 37% of women killed by their intimate partners had earlier reported violence by that partner, which UNODC and UN Women say suggests many such killings are preventable [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. We found no comparable figure for India.

## The global pattern: 137 women and girls a day

Around 50,000 women and girls were killed by intimate partners or other family members worldwide in 2024. That is about 60% of the roughly 83,000 women and girls killed intentionally that year, an average of 137 a day [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Men and boys were 80% of all homicide victims, but only 11% of male victims were killed by a partner or relative [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Men are mostly killed by people outside the family. Women are mostly killed by people inside it.

Who inside it varies. On the data available for 2023, 64% of such victims in Europe were killed by partners. Outside Europe and the Americas, 59% were killed by other family members and 41% by intimate partners [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

> The partner who cannot bear to be left and the family that cannot bear her choice sit in the same column.

India's "love affairs" column holds both without telling them apart. Both treat another person's decision as something they own. Men can be in this column too, such as a boyfriend killed by a woman's relatives, and possessive violence is not limited to straight couples. The table records none of it.

## When love sounds like ownership: taking threats seriously

"You are mine." "I cannot live without you." "If not me, then no one." Films and songs have made these lines sound like devotion. Said after a refusal or a breakup, they are information about risk.

- **Believe the threat and save it.** Screenshot it, or note the date, time and exact words.
- **Tell two people,** including one adult who can act. If you are under 18, the Child Helpline is 1098.
- **Report it.** Take the saved threat to the police with the rest of your record. Stalking can be reported at any police station, wherever it happened, or electronically, and a woman officer must record a woman's complaint [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. In immediate danger, call 112.
- **If he threatens to hurt himself,** that is pressure too, and it is not yours to manage alone. Tell his family or a friend, and pass on Tele-MANAS, the free round-the-clock mental health helpline, on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

A murder filed under "love affairs" is recorded as though love were the cause. It was not. Love can hear a no.
love-affairs-murders-possessive-violence.hg:
Har saal National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) India ke murders ko motive ke hisaab se baantta hai: dowry, witchcraft, political reasons, class conflict. Ek column ka heading hai "love affairs". 2024 mein is column mein 1,391 murders the. Uske bagal wale column "honour killing" mein 36 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani honour ke naam par jitni killings darj hui, pyaar ke naam par usse 38 guna se bhi zyada, aur table yeh nahi batati ki yeh kaisa pyaar hai jo is tarah khatam hota hai.

## Woh motive column jo koi nahi padhta: 1,391 'love affairs' murders

"Love affairs" koi offence nahi hai. Yeh ek label hai jo police murder case report karte waqt us par laga deti hai. NCRB sirf wahi compile karta hai jo state police bhejti hai, aur kehta hai ki information ki authenticity ki zimmedari uski nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Honour wala column saalon se chhota hi raha hai: 2020 mein 25, 2021 mein 33, 2022 mein 18, 2023 mein 38 aur 2024 mein 36 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Asli volume bagal mein baitha hai, "love affairs" mein aur usse bhi bade "illicit relationship" column mein.

## Is category ke andar kya hai, aur kya bahar chhoot jaata hai

"Love affairs" ke neeche kam se kam teen alag tarah ki killings darj ho sakti hain:

- koi insaan jise uske partner, ex ya reject kiye gaye admirer ne maara, kyunki woh 'na' maanne ko tayyar nahi tha;
- koi insaan jise kisi rival ne maara;
- koi couple, ya unme se ek, jise un rishtedaron ne maara jo is rishte ke khilaf the.

Teesri type wahi hai jise zyada tar log honour killing kehte hain. Official honour count ko bahut bada under-count maana jaata hai, kyunki honour killing koi alag offence nahi hai aur aise kai murders "love affairs" ya doosre motives mein darj ho jaate hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Table yeh nahi batati ki maara gaya insaan aurat tha ya aadmi, ya accused kaun tha.

Kuch killings table tak pahunchti hi nahi, kyunki motive data sirf un cases ka hota hai jo murder ke roop mein register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. April 2025 mein Supreme Court ne woh orders radd kiye jinhone Uttar Pradesh ki ek alleged honour killing ko murder ki jagah culpable homicide ke roop mein chalne diya tha. Court ne ise "a clear case of honour killing" kaha aur murder ka charge lagane ka order diya [[barandbench-honour-killing-lesser-charge-2025]].

## Possessiveness, stalking, dhamkiyan: violence ki taraf phislan

Ek hypothetical socho. Nagpur ki ek 23 saal ki ladki do saal purana relationship khatam karti hai. Ladka raat bhar call karta hai, phir uske office ke bahar intezaar karne lagta hai. Woh kehta hai ki agar woh uski nahi hui, toh kisi ki nahi hogi. Uske dost ise heartbreak kehte hain. Family ko relationship ke baare mein kabhi pata hi nahi tha, isliye woh unhe bata nahi sakti. Koi us sentence ko woh nahi maanta jo woh asal mein hai: jaan se maarne ki dhamki.

Is kahani ke beech wale hisse ka law mein ek naam hai. Kisi aurat ka peecha karna aur uske saaf dikha dene ke baad bhi, ki use interest nahi hai, use baar-baar contact karna Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 78 ke under stalking hai. Saza teen saal tak ki jail hai, aur dobara conviction par paanch saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2024 mein police ne stalking ke 9,865 cases register kiye. Us saal courts ne stalking ke jitne trials poore kiye unme se 25.2% mein conviction hui, aur unke saamne ke 92.8% stalking cases saal khatam hone par bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Data jo nahi kar sakta, woh hai in stages ko jodna. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke neeche [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Jab stalking aur killing ek hi FIR mein hon, toh case murder mein gina jaata hai aur stalking statistics se gayab ho jaati hai. NCRB ki tables yeh nahi dikhati ki un 1,391 killings mein se kitni kisi stalking complaint, kisi dhamki ya kisi pehle ki FIR ke baad hui.

France, South Africa aur Colombia ka data dikhata hai ki intimate partner ke haathon maari gayi women mein se 22% se 37% pehle hi us partner ki violence report kar chuki thi. UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik iska matlab hai ki aisi kai killings roki ja sakti hain [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. India ke liye hume aisa koi comparable figure nahi mila.

## Global pattern: har din 137 women aur girls

2024 mein duniya bhar mein kareeb 50,000 women aur girls apne intimate partners ya doosre family members ke haathon maari gayi. Yeh us saal jaan-boojh kar maari gayi lagbhag 83,000 women aur girls ka kareeb 60% hai, yaani average 137 har din [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Saare homicide victims mein 80% men aur boys the, lekin male victims mein se sirf 11% ko kisi partner ya rishtedaar ne maara [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Aadmi zyada tar family ke bahar ke logon ke haathon maare jaate hain. Auratein zyada tar family ke andar ke logon ke haathon.

Andar ka kaun, yeh jagah ke hisaab se badalta hai. 2023 ke available data ke mutabik Europe mein aise 64% victims ko partners ne maara. Europe aur Americas ke bahar 59% ko doosre family members ne maara aur 41% ko intimate partners ne [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

> Woh partner jo chhode jaana bardasht nahi kar sakta, aur woh family jo ladki ki choice bardasht nahi kar sakti, dono ek hi column mein baithe hain.

India ka "love affairs" column dono ko rakhta hai, bina alag kiye. Dono kisi doosre insaan ke faisle ko apni milkiyat samajhte hain. Is column mein aadmi bhi ho sakte hain, jaise woh boyfriend jise ladki ke rishtedaron ne maara, aur possessive violence sirf straight couples tak limited nahi hai. Table isme se kuch bhi record nahi karti.

## Jab pyaar maalikana haq jaisa sunayi de: dhamki ko seriously lo

"Tum meri ho." "Main tumhare bina jee nahi sakta." "Meri nahi toh kisi ki nahi." Films aur gaanon ne in lines ko devotion jaisa bana diya hai. Kisi refusal ya breakup ke baad boli jaayein, toh yeh risk ki information hain.

- **Dhamki par yakeen karo aur use save karo.** Screenshot lo, ya date, time aur exact shabd likh lo.
- **Do logon ko batao,** jinme ek aisa adult ho jo kuch kar sake. Agar aap 18 se kam ho, toh Child Helpline 1098 hai.
- **Report karo.** Save ki hui dhamki baaki record ke saath police ke paas le jao. Stalking ki report kisi bhi police station mein ho sakti hai, incident chahe kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronically bhi; aur aurat ki complaint woman officer ko hi record karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Turant khatra ho toh 112 par call karo.
- **Agar woh khud ko nuksaan pahunchane ki dhamki de,** toh woh bhi pressure hai, aur use akele sambhalna aapki zimmedari nahi hai. Uski family ya kisi dost ko batao, aur Tele-MANAS ka number do: free, round-the-clock mental health helpline, 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

"Love affairs" ke neeche darj murder aise record hota hai jaise wajah pyaar tha. Wajah pyaar nahi tha. Pyaar 'na' sun sakta hai.

love-or-control-relationship-self-check.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Bhopal. Her boyfriend wants her live location "so I know you're safe". He asks why she was online at 1 am. Every time she meets her college friends, he goes silent for a day. He has never raised a hand, so none of it looks like violence, which is exactly why it is hard to name.

It is also common. WHO's latest estimates find that 23.3% of ever-married or partnered girls aged 15 to 19 worldwide have already faced physical or sexual violence from a partner, and 16% faced it in the past year alone [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Very often, it starts as control.

## Why abuse is hard to see from the inside

Abuse rarely arrives as a stranger. It arrives as someone you chose, who was kind at first and now calls every rule "for your own good". Each act alone can be explained away; the pattern is the problem.

Young women carry the highest risk. WHO's earlier 2018 estimates, made with a different method, found that 1 in 4 women aged 15 to 24 who had been in a relationship had faced partner violence by their mid-twenties, with the highest past-year rate of any age group [[who-vaw-estimates-2021]].

In India, it stays hidden. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Among never-married women who reported sexual violence, 16% named a current or former boyfriend [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Silence lets a relationship like this run for years.

## The 12 questions

They apply to any relationship, straight or queer, whatever your gender. Answer for the last three months, not just the good days.

1. Do they check your phone, or ask for your passwords because "couples have no secrets"?
2. Do they need to know where you are and who you are with, and get angry when you reply late?
3. Have you stopped meeting some friends or family because it starts a fight?
4. Do they decide what you wear, what you post or whom you follow?
5. Do they accuse you of cheating, or get jealous of classmates, colleagues, even cousins?
6. Do they mock your looks, your mind or your family, then say "just joking"?
7. After arguments, do you doubt your own memory, or apologise for things you did not do?
8. Do you change what you say or do to avoid their anger?
9. Have they pressured you into sex or into sending photos, or said "if you loved me, you would"?
10. Have they threatened to share your photos or chats, or to tell your family about the relationship?
11. Have they said they will hurt themselves, or die, if you leave?
12. Have they ever pushed, grabbed, slapped or blocked you, or broken things in anger?

## Control dressed up as care

Almost every sign comes with a loving explanation. "I just worry about you" justifies the tracking. "I'm jealous because I love you" justifies the accusations. "Your friends are a bad influence" justifies the distance. Translate each sentence and look at what is left: less freedom, fewer people around you, more fear.

That fear is information. In NFHS-5, 59% of women afraid of their husband most of the time had faced spousal violence, against 15% of those never afraid of him [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey asked wives, but the lesson travels: if you plan your words around someone's temper, take it seriously.

Marriage will not fix it. Nearly one in three ever-married women in India (31.9%) have faced physical, sexual or emotional violence from a husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Among currently married women married only once, 11.2% first faced spousal physical or sexual violence within two years of the wedding [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## If you answered yes to several

This is not a medical test and there is no magic score. But several yes answers to questions 1 to 8 describe a pattern of control, which tends to grow, not fade. One yes to questions 9 to 12 is serious on its own.

Some of it is also a crime. Under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), sharing a woman's private image without her consent is voyeurism even if she agreed to the photo: 1 to 3 years in prison on first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A man who keeps following or contacting a woman after a clear no can be charged with stalking under Section 78, with up to 3 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 66E of the IT Act covers every gender: capturing or sharing an image of someone's private area without consent carries up to 3 years [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. If you are under 18, you are a child under the POCSO Act, and any sexual act with you is an offence whatever the "consent" [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]; the Child Helpline 1098 can help [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

This is general information, not legal advice. Our myth-check of five dating scripts against Section 63 covers consent itself.

## Leaving safely and finding support

You do not have to decide everything today. Start by telling one person you trust. In NFHS-5, women who did seek help most often went to their own family (60.9%), and only 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A friend, sibling or teacher counts.

Then protect yourself quietly. Save screenshots of threats where your partner cannot reach them. Change passwords they know, switch off location sharing and log out of shared devices. End things by phone or in a public place, and do not agree to meet "one last time" alone.

If someone threatens to leak your images, do not pay or send more. Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images within two hours of your complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

If a partner says they will hurt themselves, take it seriously, but do not carry it alone. Call 112 if they are in immediate danger [[mha-erss]], or Tele-MANAS on 14416, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock mental health helpline, which you can also call for yourself [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Their safety matters, but it is not a reason you must stay.

For face-to-face help, 926 One Stop Centres (Sakhi) were open across India in March 2026, having helped over 13 lakh women [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]].
love-or-control-relationship-self-check.hg:
Imagine karo, Bhopal mein ek 19 saal ki ladki hai. Uska boyfriend uski live location maangta hai, "bas isliye ki pata rahe tum safe ho." Woh poochta hai ki raat 1 baje woh online kyun thi. Jab bhi woh college ke doston se milti hai, woh poore ek din baat nahi karta. Usne kabhi haath nahi uthaya, isliye yeh sab violence jaisa nahi dikhta. Aur isi wajah se ise pehchaanna mushkil hai.

Aur yeh bahut common hai. WHO ke latest estimates kehte hain ki duniya bhar mein 15 se 19 saal ki jin ladkiyon ki shaadi hui hai ya koi partner raha hai, unme se 23.3% partner ki physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki hain, aur 16% ne toh pichhle ek saal mein hi jheli [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Aksar iski shuruaat control se hoti hai.

## Andar reh kar yeh dikhta kyun nahi

Abuse kisi stranger ki shakal mein nahi aata. Woh us insaan ke roop mein aata hai jise tumne khud chuna, jo shuru mein bahut achha tha aur jo ab har rok-tok ko "tumhare bhale ke liye" bolta hai. Har baat ko alag se dekho toh koi na koi bahana mil jaata hai. Asli problem poora pattern hai.

Sabse zyada risk young women ko hai. WHO ke 2018 wale purane estimates alag method se bane the. Unke hisaab se 15 se 24 saal ki jo ladkiyan kisi relationship mein rahi, unme se har 4 mein se 1 mid-twenties tak partner ki violence jhel chuki thi, aur pichhle ek saal ka rate bhi isi age group mein sabse zyada tha [[who-vaw-estimates-2021]].

India mein yeh chuppi ke peeche chhupa rehta hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein jin women ne physical ya sexual violence jheli thi, unme se 77% ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jin women ki kabhi shaadi nahi hui aur jinhone sexual violence report ki, unme se 16% ne current ya ex-boyfriend ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yahi chuppi aise rishte ko saalon tak chalne deti hai.

## 12 sawaal

Yeh sawaal har rishte pe laagu hote hain, straight ho ya queer, tumhara gender kuch bhi ho. Sirf achhe dinon ke baare mein mat socho. Pichhle teen mahine yaad karke jawaab do.

1. Kya woh tumhara phone check karte hain, ya yeh bol ke password maangte hain ki "couples mein koi secret nahi hota"?
2. Kya unhe har waqt jaanna hota hai ki tum kahan ho, kiske saath ho, aur late reply pe woh gussa ho jaate hain?
3. Kya tumne kuch doston ya family se milna chhod diya hai, kyunki us pe ladai hoti hai?
4. Tum kya pehnoge, kya post karoge, kise follow karoge, kya yeh woh decide karte hain?
5. Kya woh tum pe cheating ka ilzaam lagate hain, ya classmates, colleagues, yahan tak ki cousins se bhi jealous hote hain?
6. Kya woh tumhari shakal, tumhari samajh ya tumhari family ka mazaak udaate hain, aur phir bolte hain "arre, joke tha"?
7. Ladai ke baad kya tumhe apni hi yaaddasht pe shak hone lagta hai, ya tum un baaton ke liye sorry bolte ho jo tumne ki hi nahi?
8. Kya unke gusse se bachne ke liye tum apni baat ya behaviour badal lete ho?
9. Kya unhone sex ya photos bhejne ke liye pressure daala, ya bola "pyaar hai toh itna toh kar hi sakte ho"?
10. Kya unhone tumhari photos ya chats share karne ki, ya family ko rishte ke baare mein bata dene ki dhamki di?
11. Kya unhone kaha ki tum chhod ke gaye toh woh khud ko hurt karenge ya jaan de denge?
12. Kya unhone kabhi dhakka diya, kas ke pakda, thappad maara, raasta roka, ya gusse mein cheezein todi?

## Care ke naam pe control

Lagbhag har sign ke saath ek pyaar bhari wajah judi hoti hai. "Mujhe bas tumhari fikar hai" se location tracking justify hoti hai. "Jealous hoon kyunki pyaar karta hoon" se ilzaam justify hote hain. "Tumhare dost theek nahi hain" se doston se doori justify hoti hai. Har line ka asli matlab nikaalo aur dekho kya bacha: kam azaadi, aas-paas kam log, aur zyada darr.

Yeh darr khud ek signal hai. NFHS-5 mein jo women zyada tar time apne pati se darti thi, unme se 59% spousal violence jhel chuki thi, jabki kabhi na darne wali women mein yeh 15% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh sawaal wives se poocha gaya tha, par lesson har rishte ka hai: agar tum kisi ka gussa dekh ke apne words tolte ho, toh ise halke mein mat lo.

Shaadi se yeh theek nahi hota. India mein married rahi lagbhag har teen mein se ek woman (31.9%) pati ki physical, sexual ya emotional violence jhel chuki hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jo women abhi married hain aur jinki ek hi shaadi hui, unme se 11.2% ne shaadi ke do saal ke andar hi pehli baar pati ki physical ya sexual violence jheli [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Agar kai jawaab "haan" hain

Yeh koi medical test nahi hai, aur koi magic score bhi nahi hai. Lekin agar sawaal 1 se 8 mein kai jawaab "haan" hain, toh yeh control ka pattern hai, jo time ke saath kam nahi hota, badhta hai. Sawaal 9 se 12 mein ek bhi "haan" apne aap mein serious hai.

Inme se kuch cheezein crime bhi hain. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 77 ke under kisi woman ki private photo uski consent ke bina share karna voyeurism hai, chahe photo khinchwane ke liye usne haan kaha ho. First conviction pe 1 se 3 saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Agar koi aadmi saaf "na" ke baad bhi kisi woman ka peecha kare ya baar-baar contact kare, toh Section 78 ke under stalking ka case ban sakta hai, jisme 3 saal tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. IT Act ka Section 66E har gender pe laagu hota hai: kisi ke private parts ki image bina consent ke lena ya share karna, isme 3 saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Agar tumhari umar 18 se kam hai, toh POCSO Act ke under tum child ho, aur tumhare saath koi bhi sexual act offence hai, "consent" ho ya na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]; Child Helpline 1098 madad kar sakti hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Consent pe poori baat hamare us article mein hai, jisme dating ke paanch myths ko Section 63 pe parkha gaya hai.

## Safely nikalna aur support paana

Tumhe aaj hi sab kuch decide nahi karna. Shuruaat kisi ek bharosemand insaan ko batane se karo. NFHS-5 mein jin women ne help maangi, unme se zyada tar (60.9%) apni family ke paas gayi, aur sirf 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Dost, bhai-behen ya teacher, koi bhi chalega.

Phir chupchaap apni safety karo. Dhamkiyon ke screenshots aisi jagah rakho jahan partner na pahunch sake. Jo passwords unhe pata hain, badal do, location sharing band karo aur shared devices se log out karo. Rishta khatam karne ki baat phone pe ya kisi public jagah pe karo, aur "last time" akele milne ke liye haan mat bolo.

Agar koi tumhari photos leak karne ki dhamki de, toh na paise do, na aur photos bhejo. cybercrime.gov.in pe complaint karo ya 1930 pe call karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. 20 February 2026 se rule hai ki platforms tumhari complaint ke do ghante ke andar nude, sexual ya morphed images hatayein [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].

Agar partner bole ki woh khud ko hurt karega, toh ise seriously lo, par iska bojh akele mat uthao. Unki jaan ko turant khatra ho toh 112 pe call karo [[mha-erss]], ya Tele-MANAS 14416 pe, jo Health Ministry ki free, 24x7 mental health helpline hai; tum apne liye bhi call kar sakte ho [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Unki safety zaroori hai, lekin iski wajah se tumhe rishte mein rukna pade, aisa nahi hai.

Face-to-face help ke liye, March 2026 tak poore India mein 926 One Stop Centres (Sakhi) chal rahe the, aur tab tak 13 lakh se zyada women ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]].

male-survivors-sexual-assault-questions.en:
A man who has been sexually assaulted in India rarely says it aloud. More often he types it into a search bar late at night. Here are straight answers to five of the questions he is likely to ask, for men, for boys, and for anyone a man might one day tell. On the law, this is general information, not legal advice.

## Does it count if it happened to a man?

Yes. Any sexual act done to you without your consent is sexual violence. Your gender, size and strength do not change that, and neither does who did it: a man or a woman, a stranger, a senior, a relative or a partner.

UNICEF estimates that 240 million to 310 million boys and men alive today, around 1 in 11, were raped or sexually assaulted in childhood, and says the range is wide because data on boys are thin [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. For adult men, India's crime statistics keep no count at all.

If you froze instead of fighting, that was fear, not agreement. For women, Indian law already says that a person who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The section does not cover you. The reasoning does.

## My body reacted. Does that mean I wanted it?

No. A physical response, even an erection or ejaculation, can happen without any wanting. Bodies react to touch, fear and stress in ways the mind does not choose. A reaction is not a decision, and consent is a decision.

Someone who abuses may point to this reaction so that a boy or man feels he "took part" and stays quiet. The confusion and shame it leaves can keep a man silent for years. A doctor or counsellor has heard it before. It also says nothing about your sexuality: being assaulted by a man does not make you gay, and being gay does not make an assault any less an assault.

## What does the law offer an adult man today, and what does it not?

Less than it should, and you deserve to know that before you walk into a police station. Since 1 July 2024, Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines rape as an act by "a man" against "a woman", so an adult man cannot legally be a victim of rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 377 of the old IPC, which the Supreme Court kept in force for non-consensual acts in 2018 [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]], has no counterpart in the new code, and no specific offence replaced it [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

This was not an oversight. In November 2023 Parliament's Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned that dropping Section 377 would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping it; the government did not accept this [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Police registered 888 cases under Section 377 in 2023; the 2024 data have no such head [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

What remains are general offences such as hurt, grievous hurt or wrongful confinement, depending on the facts. Voluntarily causing hurt carries at most 1 year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For transgender survivors, the Transgender Persons Act punishes sexual abuse with six months to two years [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

You can still go to the police. Anyone can report a cognizable offence at any police station, wherever it happened, and the victim must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
