The charges depend on the facts, so write everything down: injuries, threats, being held against your will, any recording. NALSA's legal aid helpline can tell you whether you qualify for free legal aid [[nalsa]].

## What if it happened before I turned 18?

Then the law is far stronger. The POCSO Act, in force since 14 November 2012, defines a child as anyone under 18 and protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Under it, a child's "consent" is not a question at all.

Boys are still nearly invisible in its records. In 2024 police recorded 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault under POCSO: 43,675 girls and 892 boys [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yet in the government's own 2007 Study on Child Abuse, boys were 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. That study's sample was not nationally representative, but the distance between it and the police count shows how rarely anyone asks boys.

If you are under 18 now, tell an adult you trust or call the Child Helpline 1098. Know one thing first: POCSO makes reporting mandatory for anyone who knows of abuse, so a doctor, teacher or counsellor cannot promise to keep it secret [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. If you are an adult and it happened years ago, a lawyer can tell you what legal options remain after the delay, and you can get counselling whether or not you ever report.

## Where do I get medical care, PEP and mental-health support?

Start with a hospital, and with the clock. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) must begin as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure, and is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. Ask for it by name at a government hospital's emergency department; the NACO helpline 1097 can direct you [[naco]]. Ask about testing for other infections too, since many STIs cause no symptoms [[who-sti]].

An honest warning: the law that orders every hospital to treat survivors free of cost names rape, acid attack and POCSO offences [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], so an adult man is not expressly covered. Go anyway. You can ask for treatment before you have decided anything about the police.

Then the mind. Sleeplessness, anger, flashbacks, drinking more and avoiding touch are common after sexual violence, and they respond to care. Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline on 14416, offers counselling to anyone in need [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. You can open with one sentence: "Something sexual was done to me that I did not want." If you ever feel you cannot go on, call 14416 or 112 straight away.

The gap in the penal code is Parliament's failure. It is not a verdict on what happened to you.
male-survivors-sexual-assault-questions.hg:
India mein jis aadmi par sexual assault hua ho, woh ise shayad hi kabhi zor se kehta hai. Zyada tar woh ise raat ko der se search bar mein type karta hai. Yahan un paanch sawaalon ke seedhe jawaab hain jo woh shayad poochhega, men ke liye, boys ke liye, aur har us insaan ke liye jise koi aadmi kabhi yeh baat bata sakta hai. Law ke maamle mein yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Agar yeh ek aadmi ke saath hua, toh kya yeh count hota hai?

Haan. Aapki consent ke bina aapke saath kiya gaya koi bhi sexual act sexual violence hai. Aapka gender, size ya taakat ise nahi badalte, aur yeh bhi nahi ki karne wala kaun tha: aadmi ya aurat, stranger, senior, rishtedaar ya partner.

UNICEF ka estimate hai ki aaj zinda 240 million se 310 million boys aur men, yaani kareeb 1 in 11, bachpan mein rape ya sexual assault ka shikaar hue, aur UNICEF kehta hai ki range isliye badi hai kyunki boys par data kam hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Adult men ke liye India ke crime statistics mein koi ginti hi nahi hai.

Agar aap ladne ki jagah freeze ho gaye, toh woh darr tha, agreement nahi. Women ke liye Indian law pehle hi kehta hai ki jo insaan physically resist nahi karta, use sirf is wajah se consenting nahi maana jaayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh section aapko cover nahi karta. Iski reasoning aap par bhi lagu hoti hai.

## Meri body ne react kiya. Kya iska matlab hai ki main yeh chahta tha?

Nahi. Physical response, erection ya ejaculation bhi, bina chaahe ho sakta hai. Body touch, darr aur stress par aise react karti hai jo mann tay nahi karta. Reaction koi decision nahi hai, aur consent ek decision hota hai.

Abuse karne wala insaan isi reaction ki taraf ishaara kar sakta hai, taaki ladke ya aadmi ko lage ki woh bhi "shaamil" tha aur woh chup rahe. Isse jo confusion aur sharm paida hoti hai, woh kisi aadmi ko saalon tak chup rakh sakti hai. Doctor ya counsellor yeh baat pehle sun chuke hain. Yeh aapki sexuality ke baare mein bhi kuch nahi kehta: kisi aadmi ke haathon assault hone se aap gay nahi ho jaate, aur gay hone se assault kam assault nahi ho jaata.

## Aaj law ek adult man ko kya deta hai, aur kya nahi?

Jitna dena chahiye usse kam, aur police station mein kadam rakhne se pehle yeh jaanna aapka haq hai. 1 July 2024 se Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 rape ko "a man" ka "a woman" ke against kiya gaya act batata hai, isliye ek adult man legally rape victim nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Purane IPC ka Section 377, jise Supreme Court ne 2018 mein non-consensual acts ke liye lagu rakha tha [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]], naye code mein kahin nahi hai, aur uski jagah koi specific offence nahi aaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh koi bhool nahi thi. November 2023 mein Parliament ki Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne warn kiya tha ki Section 377 hatane se men aur transgender persons ke against non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur ise rakhne ki recommendation di; government ne yeh nahi maana [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. 2023 mein police ne Section 377 ke tahat 888 cases register kiye; 2024 ke data mein yeh head hai hi nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Jo bacha hai, woh hurt, grievous hurt ya wrongful confinement jaise general offences hain, facts ke hisaab se. Voluntarily causing hurt par zyada se zyada 1 year ki jail, Rs 10,000 tak ka fine, ya dono hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Transgender survivors ke liye Transgender Persons Act sexual abuse par chhah mahine se do saal ki saza deta hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Aap phir bhi police ke paas ja sakte hain. Koi bhi insaan kisi bhi police station mein cognizable offence report kar sakta hai, chahe woh kahin bhi hua ho, aur victim ko FIR ki free copy milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Charges facts par depend karte hain, isliye sab kuch likh lijiye: injuries, dhamkiyan, aapko zabardasti rok kar rakhna, koi recording. NALSA ki legal aid helpline bata sakti hai ki aap free legal aid ke liye qualify karte hain ya nahi [[nalsa]].

## Agar yeh mere 18 ka hone se pehle hua ho toh?

Tab law kahin zyada mazboot hai. POCSO Act, jo 14 November 2012 se lagu hai, 18 se kam ke har insaan ko child maanta hai aur boys aur girls ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Iske tahat child ki "consent" ka sawaal uthta hi nahi.

Phir bhi iske records mein ladke lagbhag dikhte hi nahi. 2024 mein police ne POCSO ke tahat penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims darj kiye: 43,675 girls aur 892 boys [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jabki government ki apni 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Us study ka sample nationally representative nahi tha, lekin uske aur police ki ginti ke beech ka faasla dikhata hai ki ladkon se kitna kam poochha jaata hai.

Agar aap abhi 18 se kam ke hain, toh kisi bharosemand adult ko bataiye ya Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye. Pehle ek baat jaan lijiye: POCSO ke tahat abuse ke baare mein jaanne wale har insaan ke liye report karna mandatory hai, isliye doctor, teacher ya counsellor ise secret rakhne ka waada nahi kar sakte [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Agar aap ab adult hain aur yeh saalon pehle hua tha, toh lawyer bata sakta hai ki itni der ke baad kaun se legal options bache hain, aur report karein ya na karein, aap counselling le sakte hain.

## Medical care, PEP aur mental-health support kahan milega?

Hospital se shuru kijiye, aur ghadi par nazar rakhiye. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) jitni jaldi ho sake aur exposure ke 72 hours ke andar shuru honi chahiye, aur 28 days tak li jaati hai [[who-pep]]. Kisi government hospital ke emergency department mein iska naam lekar maangiye; NACO helpline 1097 aapko raasta bata sakti hai [[naco]]. Doosre infections ki testing ke baare mein bhi poochhiye, kyunki kai STIs ke koi symptoms nahi hote [[who-sti]].

Ek imaandaar warning: jo law har hospital ko survivors ka free ilaaj karne ka order deta hai, usme rape, acid attack aur POCSO offences ka naam hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], isliye ek adult man saaf taur par cover nahi hota. Phir bhi jaiye. Police ke baare mein kuch tay karne se pehle bhi aap treatment maang sakte hain.

Phir mann ki baat. Neend na aana, gussa, flashbacks, zyada peena aur touch se bachna sexual violence ke baad common hain, aur care se inme sudhaar hota hai. Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free, round-the-clock helpline 14416, kisi bhi zarooratmand ko counselling deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Aap ek sentence se shuru kar sakte hain: "Mere saath kuch sexual kiya gaya jo main nahi chahta tha." Agar kabhi lage ki ab aage nahi chal paayenge, toh turant 14416 ya 112 par call kijiye.

Penal code ka yeh gap Parliament ki naakaami hai. Yeh is baat ka faisla nahi hai ki aapke saath kya hua.

men-mental-health-help-seeking-gap.en:
"Men don't talk" is usually said with a shrug, as if it were a fact of nature. India's only national mental health survey suggests something more uncomfortable. In 2015-16 it found a mental disorder in 13.9% of men against 7.5% of women, and alcohol use disorder in 9% of men against 0.5% of women [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Men's distress is not missing. It is showing up under other names, and the system that is supposed to catch it is mostly not built for the way men live.

## The 150-million gap

The National Mental Health Survey, run by NIMHANS for the Health Ministry across 12 states, found that 10.6% of Indian adults had a mental disorder at the time of the survey and 13.7% had had one at some point in their lives [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. It estimated that nearly 150 million Indians need mental health care, and that fewer than 30 million seek it [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]].

For individual conditions the treatment gap, the share of people who need care but do not get it, ran from 28% to 83%, and reached 86% for alcohol use disorders [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Every disorder except epilepsy had a gap above 60%. In plain words: in India, untreated is the normal state of most mental illnesses, for women and men alike.

Men sit at a particular point in that gap. The disorder that most separates them from women in the survey, alcohol use, is also the one least likely to be treated.

## What men's distress looks like in the data

The survey found depression and anxiety disorders more common in women, while the widest gap between the sexes was in alcohol use disorder; men aged 30 to 49 were the most affected group [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Those are the years when many Indian men are expected to support children, ageing parents and often a loan, all at once.

One reading of that pattern is that many men's sadness and fear never get called depression at all. They get called drinking, temper, overwork or "tension". A man who cannot sleep may be told to have a peg. A man who is snapping at his children may be told he has a short fuse. Neither is sent to a doctor.

The cost of that silence shows up elsewhere. Men were 71.8% of the people who died by suicide in India in 2022, according to police records [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. Our data story on that figure looks at the breadwinner pressure behind it.

## Rigid masculinity and the cost of 'be strong'

In 2014, researchers from ICRW and UNFPA surveyed 9,205 men and 3,158 women in seven Indian states [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. They grouped men by their views and behaviour on gender roles: 32% showed "rigid" masculinity, 45% were moderate, and only 23% were gender-equitable [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

That study measured attitudes to women and power, not help-seeking. But the logic of rigid masculinity explains a lot about why help feels impossible. If a man's worth rests on being in control and providing for everyone, then admitting he cannot cope is not a health event. It is a demotion.

Imagine a 41-year-old shop owner in Indore whose business has been sinking for a year. He sleeps four hours a night and drinks most evenings. His wife has asked him twice to "see someone". To him, sitting in a waiting room would announce to the whole market that he has failed, so he tells her he is fine and goes back to the shop.

The good news sits in the same table. Nearly half of the men surveyed were moderate, not rigid. Most Indian men are not locked into "be strong at any cost". They can be reached.

## Why clinics lose men

For many men the problem is practical before it is emotional. A daily wage earner who spends a morning in a hospital queue loses that day's income. A salaried man may not want to explain a psychiatry appointment to his manager. A young man in a small town may know the receptionist. Families worry about izzat and marriage prospects. Alcohol is treated as a moral weakness to be scolded, not a condition to be treated.

The law has moved further than many families have. The Mental Healthcare Act 2017 bars discrimination in mental health care on any basis, naming gender, sex and sexual orientation among the protected grounds, which matters for gay, bisexual and trans men who fear judgement as well as stigma [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. The same Act presumes that a person who attempts suicide is under severe stress and bars trying or punishing them for it [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## Making help usable: what works for men

Help reaches more men when it fits around their lives instead of demanding they rearrange them. A phone line removes the waiting room. Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock tele-mental-health helpline on 14416, has offered counselling to anyone who needs it since October 2022 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. A man can call from a parked bike or a night shift. He does not need to say the word "depression".

The other part of the answer is people. Men are more likely to open up when another man goes first: a father who admits he once struggled, a friend who asks twice, a boss who treats a counselling appointment like any other medical visit. If you are the one struggling, start with one honest sentence to one person, or one call to 14416. If drinking has become your way of coping, say that to a doctor in exactly those words.

"Men don't talk" is not destiny. It is what happens when talking costs too much. Lower the cost, and men talk.
men-mental-health-help-seeking-gap.hg:
"Mard baat nahi karte" aksar kandhe uchka ke kaha jaata hai, jaise yeh koi kudrati sach ho. India ka iklauta national mental health survey isse zyada uncomfortable baat kehta hai. 2015-16 mein isne 13.9% mardon mein mental disorder paaya, jabki auraton mein 7.5%, aur alcohol use disorder 9% mardon mein tha, auraton mein sirf 0.5% [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Mardon ki takleef gayab nahi hai. Woh doosre naamon se saamne aa rahi hai, aur jis system ko use pakadna chahiye, woh zyada tar mardon ki zindagi ke hisaab se bana hi nahi hai.

## 150 million ka gap

National Mental Health Survey, jo NIMHANS ne Health Ministry ke liye 12 states mein kiya, usne paaya ki survey ke waqt 10.6% Indian adults ko mental disorder tha aur 13.7% ko zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi hua tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Iska andaaza tha ki lagbhag 150 million Indians ko mental health care chahiye, aur 30 million se bhi kam log madad dhoondhte hain [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]].

Alag-alag conditions ke liye treatment gap, yaani jinhe care chahiye par milti nahi unka hissa, 28% se 83% tak tha, aur alcohol use disorders mein 86% tak pahunch gaya [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Epilepsy ko chhod ke har disorder ka gap 60% se upar tha. Seedhe shabdon mein: India mein zyada tar mental illnesses ka normal haal hai ki unka ilaaj nahi hota, auraton aur mardon dono ke liye.

Is gap mein mard ek khaas jagah pe khade hain. Survey mein jo disorder unhe auraton se sabse zyada alag karta hai, yaani sharaab ki lat, wahi sabse kam ilaaj paane wala bhi hai.

## Data mein mardon ki takleef kaisi dikhti hai

Survey mein depression aur anxiety disorders auraton mein zyada common the, jabki mardon aur auraton ke beech sabse bada fark alcohol use disorder mein tha; 30 se 49 saal ke mard sabse zyada affected group the [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Yeh woh saal hain jab bahut se Indian mardon se ummeed ki jaati hai ki woh bachchon, boodhe maa-baap aur aksar ek loan ko, sab ek saath sambhalein.

Is pattern ko padhne ka ek tareeka yeh hai ki bahut se mardon ki udaasi aur darr ko kabhi depression kaha hi nahi jaata. Use peena, gussa, zyada kaam ya "tension" kaha jaata hai. Jis mard ko neend nahi aati, use ek peg lene ki salaah mil sakti hai. Jo mard bachchon pe chillata hai, use bas "gusse wala" maan liya jaata hai. Dono mein se kisi ko doctor ke paas nahi bheja jaata.

Is chuppi ki keemat kahin aur dikhti hai. Police records ke mutabik 2022 mein India mein suicide se marne walon mein 71.8% mard the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. Is figure pe hamari data story uske peeche ke 'ghar chalaane wale' pressure ko dekhti hai.

## Rigid masculinity aur 'strong bano' ki keemat

2014 mein ICRW aur UNFPA ke researchers ne saat Indian states mein 9,205 mardon aur 3,158 auraton ka survey kiya [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. Unhone mardon ko gender roles pe unke views aur behaviour ke hisaab se groups mein baanta: 32% mein "rigid" masculinity thi, 45% moderate the, aur sirf 23% gender-equitable the [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Us study ne auraton aur power ke baare mein soch ko naapa tha, madad maangne ko nahi. Lekin rigid masculinity ka logic samjhaata hai ki madad maangna itna namumkin kyun lagta hai. Agar mard ki keemat is pe tiki hai ki sab uske control mein ho aur woh sabka pet bhare, toh yeh maanna ki woh sambhal nahi pa raha, sehat ka mamla nahi rehta. Woh demotion ban jaata hai.

Socho, Indore mein ek 41 saal ke dukaandaar ka business saal bhar se doob raha hai. Woh raat ko chaar ghante sota hai aur zyada tar shaamon ko peeta hai. Uski wife do baar keh chuki hai ki "kisi ko dikha lo". Uske liye waiting room mein baithna poore bazaar ko bata dena hai ki woh haar gaya, isliye woh kehta hai sab theek hai aur wapas dukaan chala jaata hai.

Achhi khabar usi table mein hai. Survey kiye gaye mardon mein se lagbhag aadhe moderate the, rigid nahi. Zyada tar Indian mard "har haal mein strong bano" mein kaid nahi hain. Unn tak pahuncha ja sakta hai.

## Clinic mardon ko kyun kho dete hain

Bahut se mardon ke liye problem emotional se pehle practical hai. Daily wage earner agar subah hospital ki line mein bitaye, toh us din ki kamaai gayi. Salary wala mard shayad apne manager ko psychiatry appointment samjhaana nahi chahta. Chhote shehar ka young ladka shayad receptionist ko jaanta ho. Families ko izzat aur rishton ki fikr hoti hai. Sharaab ko ek naitik kamzori maana jaata hai jispe daanta jaaye, aisi condition nahi jiska ilaaj ho.

Kanoon kai families se aage nikal chuka hai. Mental Healthcare Act 2017 mental health care mein kisi bhi aadhaar pe bhedbhaav rokta hai, aur protected grounds mein gender, sex aur sexual orientation ka naam leta hai, jo gay, bisexual aur trans mardon ke liye maayne rakhta hai jinhe stigma ke saath judgement ka bhi darr hota hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Wahi Act maanta hai ki suicide attempt karne wala severe stress mein hai, aur us pe case chalane ya saza dene pe rok lagata hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## Madad ko kaam ka banana: mardon ke liye kya kaam karta hai

Madad zyada mardon tak tab pahunchti hai jab woh unki zindagi mein fit ho, na ki unse apni zindagi badalne ki maang kare. Phone line waiting room hata deti hai. Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free aur din-raat chalne wali tele-mental-health helpline 14416, October 2022 se kisi ko bhi counselling de rahi hai jise zaroorat ho [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Mard park ki hui bike pe baithe ya night shift ke beech call kar sakta hai. Use "depression" shabd bolne ki bhi zaroorat nahi.

Jawab ka doosra hissa log hain. Mard tab zyada khulte hain jab koi doosra mard pehle bole: papa jo maanein ki woh bhi kabhi struggle kar chuke hain, dost jo do baar poochhe, boss jo counselling appointment ko kisi bhi doosre medical visit jaisa maane. Agar struggle tum kar rahe ho, toh ek insaan se ek sachcha sentence bolo, ya 14416 pe ek call karo. Agar peena tumhara sambhalne ka tareeka ban gaya hai, toh doctor ko bilkul yahi shabd bolo.

"Mard baat nahi karte" koi kismat nahi hai. Yeh tab hota hai jab baat karne ki keemat bahut zyada ho. Keemat ghatao, aur mard baat karenge.

men-say-husband-may-force-sex-nfhs.en:
India's National Family Health Survey puts a blunt question to men aged 15 to 49. If a wife refuses to have sex with her husband, does he have the right to get angry and reprimand her, to refuse her financial support, to use force to have sex, or to have sex with another woman? In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 12.2% of men, about one in eight, said he has the right to use force [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In a group of 40 men, that is about five.

## The question NFHS asks men about a wife's "no"

Each of the four responses is a way of making a refusal cost something: anger, money, force, or another woman. The report compares the answers with the previous round, NFHS-4 (2015-16).

These are opinions, not a count of what men do. A man answering an interviewer has every reason to give the respectable answer, so the figures are more likely a floor than a ceiling. The survey also asks only about husbands and wives; pressure and force in other relationships, including against men and queer people, are outside it.

The women's side of the same survey shows these opinions are not idle. Among ever-married women aged 18 to 49, 6.3% reported sexual violence by their husband, and 4.6% said he had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Among ever-married women who had ever faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband as the person responsible [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 12.2%, 19.2% and a shrinking 72%

Force was not the most common answer. 19.2% of men said a husband has the right to get angry and reprimand a wife who refuses [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The same table shows 13% backing a cut in financial support and 12.6% saying he may have sex with another woman, while 5.5% agreed with all four [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The number that matters most is the group that said no to everything: 72% of men in NFHS-5, down from 77% in NFHS-4 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Between two rounds, the share of men who think a wife's refusal should cost her nothing fell by five percentage points.

Anger sounds mild beside force. It is not harmless. A wife who knows that "no" will be followed by shouting, a week of silence or a stopped allowance is not choosing freely the next time she says "yes". Agreement given to avoid punishment is compliance, not consent.

## Women's views moved forward, men's moved back

The same split appears on violence in general. NFHS asks both sexes whether a husband is justified in beating his wife in any of seven situations. Among women, agreement fell from 52% in NFHS-4 to 45% in NFHS-5. Among men, it rose from 42% to 44% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Refusing sex was the reason least often accepted for a beating, by 10% of men and 11% of women; disrespect to in-laws was the most accepted, by 31% of men and 32% of women [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. So about one man in ten approves of hitting a wife who refuses, and about one in eight approves of forcing her.

> Women are being told they can say no. Far fewer men are being told they have to hear it.

The survey records the shift; it does not explain it. One honest observation: much of the public messaging on violence at home speaks to women (know your rights, call this number). Very little of it speaks to the husband.

## Punjab 21%, Karnataka 45%: where most men accept some coercion

The national figure hides wide gaps. The share of men rejecting all four responses was below half in four places: Punjab (21%), Chandigarh (28%), Karnataka (45%) and Ladakh (46%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. There, most men interviewed accepted at least one way of punishing a wife's refusal.

"At least one" includes getting angry, so these are not the shares of men who back force, and state samples are smaller than the national one. The list still breaks a comfortable assumption. Chandigarh's men were the least likely in the country to say wife-beating can be justified, while Karnataka's were the most likely, at 82% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A man can reject hitting and still believe sex is owed to him.

## The law exempts husbands. The 72% decide what happens next

Criminal law does not draw this line for men. Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 says sexual intercourse by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The exception does not cover a wife under 18. On 9 September 2026 a three-judge Supreme Court bench posted the challenge to it for final hearing; no verdict had been reported when this story was written [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

Forced sex in marriage is still not lawful. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts sexual abuse as domestic violence, and a wife can ask a court for a protection order [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

Until the rape law changes, what a husband believes is, for many wives, the only protection in the room. That is why the 72% matter more than the 12.2%. Most Indian men already reject every one of these responses. What they rarely do is say so.

Consider this situation. A 27-year-old in Indore is at a friend's pre-wedding party. Someone jokes that the groom should "not take no for an answer" on the first night, and everyone laughs. Going by the survey, most of the men laughing do not believe it. The joke survives because none of them says so.

Attitudes are learned early. A 2014 ICRW-UNFPA study in seven states found that men raised in families where fathers did household chores were two times more likely to hold gender-equitable attitudes [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. Prevention starts with what a boy sees his father do, and with what the majority is willing to say out loud: a wife's "no" needs no permission and earns no penalty.
men-say-husband-may-force-sex-nfhs.hg:
India ka National Family Health Survey 15 se 49 saal ke mardon se ek seedha sawaal poochhta hai. Agar patni apne pati ke saath sex se mana kar de, toh kya pati ko haq hai ki woh gussa kare aur use daante, uska kharcha rok de, zabardasti sex kare, ya kisi doosri aurat ke saath sex kare? NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 12.2% mardon ne, yaani lagbhag har aath mein se ek ne, kaha ki pati ko zabardasti karne ka haq hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 40 mardon ke group mein yeh lagbhag paanch hote hain.

## Patni ki "na" pe NFHS mardon se kya poochhta hai

Chaaron jawabon mein se har ek mana karne ki keemat vasoolne ka tareeka hai: gussa, paisa, zabardasti, ya doosri aurat. Report in jawabon ki tulna pichhle round, NFHS-4 (2015-16), se karti hai.

Yeh raay hai, is baat ki ginti nahi ki mard asal mein kya karte hain. Interviewer ke saamne baitha mard wahi jawab dena chahega jo sunne mein theek lage, isliye asli figures in se kam nahi, zyada hi ho sakte hain. Survey sirf pati aur patni ke baare mein poochhta hai; doosre rishton mein hone wala dabaav aur zabardasti, jo mardon aur queer logon ke saath bhi hoti hai, iske daayre se baahar hai.

Usi survey ka auraton wala hissa dikhata hai ki yeh raay sirf baatein nahi hain. 18 se 49 saal ki ever-married auraton mein se 6.3% ne pati ki taraf se sexual violence report kiya, aur 4.6% ne kaha ki unki marzi ke bina pati ne zabardasti intercourse kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jin ever-married auraton ne kabhi sexual violence jhela, unmein se 82% ne apne current pati ko hi zimmedar bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 12.2%, 19.2% aur sikudta hua 72%

Zabardasti sabse common jawab nahi tha. 19.2% mardon ne kaha ki mana karne wali patni pe gussa karna aur use daantna pati ka haq hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Usi table ke hisaab se 13% ne kharcha rokne ko sahi kaha aur 12.6% ne kaha ki pati doosri aurat ke saath sex kar sakta hai, jabki 5.5% chaaron baaton se sehmat the [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Sabse zaroori number us group ka hai jisne har baat ko mana kiya: NFHS-5 mein 72% mard, jabki NFHS-4 mein 77% the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Do rounds ke beech un mardon ka hissa paanch percentage points ghat gaya jo maante hain ki patni ke mana karne ki use koi keemat nahi chukani chahiye.

Zabardasti ke saamne gussa halka lagta hai. Lekin woh bekasoor nahi hai. Jis patni ko pata hai ki "na" ke baad chillaana, hafte bhar ki chuppi ya kharcha band hona tay hai, woh agli baar "haan" azaadi se nahi keh rahi hoti. Saza se bachne ke liye di gayi haan majboori hai, consent nahi.

## Auraton ki soch aage badhi, mardon ki peeche gayi

Yahi fark aam hinsa ke sawaal pe bhi dikhta hai. NFHS dono se poochhta hai ki kya saat situations mein se kisi mein bhi pati ka patni ko peetna sahi hai. Auraton mein sehmati NFHS-4 ke 52% se ghat ke NFHS-5 mein 45% ho gayi. Mardon mein yeh 42% se badh ke 44% ho gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Peetne ki sabse kam maani gayi wajah sex se mana karna thi, jise 10% mardon aur 11% auraton ne sahi kaha; sabse zyada maani gayi wajah sasuraal walon ki beizzati thi, 31% mard aur 32% auratein [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani lagbhag das mein se ek mard mana karne wali patni ko maarna sahi maanta hai, aur lagbhag aath mein se ek uske saath zabardasti karna.

> Auraton ko bataya ja raha hai ki woh na keh sakti hain. Mardon ko bahut kam bataya ja raha hai ki unhe woh na sunni padegi.

Survey yeh badlaav darj karta hai; iski wajah nahi batata. Ek baat imaandaari se kahi ja sakti hai: ghar ki hinsa pe kaafi public messaging auraton se baat karti hai (apne haq jaano, is number pe call karo). Pati se baat karne wali messaging bahut kam hai.

## Punjab 21%, Karnataka 45%: jahan zyada tar mard kisi na kisi dabaav ko sahi maante hain

National figure ke peeche bade fark chhupe hain. Chaaron jawab reject karne wale mardon ka hissa chaar jagah aadhe se kam tha: Punjab (21%), Chandigarh (28%), Karnataka (45%) aur Ladakh (46%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Wahan interview kiye gaye zyada tar mardon ne patni ke mana karne pe saza ka kam se kam ek tareeka sahi maana.

"Kam se kam ek" mein gussa karna bhi shaamil hai, toh yeh un mardon ka hissa nahi hai jo zabardasti ko sahi kehte hain, aur state ke samples national sample se chhote hote hain. Phir bhi yeh list ek aaraamdeh soch ko todti hai. Chandigarh ke mard poore desh mein sabse kam the jinhone patni ko peetna sahi kaha, jabki Karnataka ke mard sabse zyada the, 82% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ek mard maar-peet ko galat maan sakta hai aur phir bhi yeh maan sakta hai ki sex uska haq hai.

## Kanoon pati ko chhoot deta hai. Aage kya hoga, yeh 72% tay karenge

Criminal law mardon ke liye yeh line nahi kheenchta. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar patni 18 ya usse zyada ki hai, toh pati ka apni patni ke saath sexual intercourse rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 18 se kam umar ki patni pe yeh exception laagu nahi hota. 9 September 2026 ko Supreme Court ki teen judges ki bench ne is exception ke khilaaf challenge ko final hearing ke liye post kiya; jab yeh story likhi gayi, tab tak koi faisla report nahi hua tha [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

Shaadi mein zabardasti sex phir bhi kanooni nahi hai. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 sexual abuse ko domestic violence maanta hai, aur patni court se protection order maang sakti hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Jab tak rape law nahi badalta, bahut si patniyon ke liye kamre mein akela bachaav yahi hai ki pati kya maanta hai. Isiliye 72% ki ahmiyat 12.2% se zyada hai. Zyada tar Indian mard pehle se hi in chaaron jawabon ko galat maante hain. Bas woh yeh baat bolte bahut kam hain.

Ek situation socho. Indore ka ek 27 saal ka ladka apne dost ki shaadi se pehle ki party mein hai. Koi mazaak karta hai ki pehli raat dulhe ko "na sunni hi nahi chahiye", aur sab hans dete hain. Survey ke hisaab se hansne wale zyada tar mard yeh baat maante hi nahi. Mazaak isliye zinda rehta hai kyunki unmein se koi kehta nahi.

Soch bachpan mein banti hai. 2014 ki ICRW-UNFPA study ne saat states mein paaya ki jin gharon mein papa ghar ka kaam karte the, wahan bade hue mardon ke gender-equitable soch rakhne ke chances do guna zyada the [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. Bachaav wahan se shuru hota hai jo ek ladka apne papa ko karte dekhta hai, aur us baat se jo majority khul ke kehne ko taiyaar ho: patni ki "na" ko kisi ijaazat ki zaroorat nahi, aur us pe koi saza nahi banti.

men-suicide-india-breadwinner-trap.en:
In 2024, police in India recorded 1,70,746 suicides, slightly fewer than the 1,71,418 recorded in 2023 [[theprint-ncrb-adsi-2024]]. Behind the totals sits a pattern that barely moves from year to year: most of the people who die are men. In 2022, the latest year for which we could verify the breakdown by sex, men were 71.8% of suicide victims, and about 68% of those men were married [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. This is not a story about men being weaker, or about women suffering less. It is a story about what Indian men are expected to carry, and how rarely they are allowed to put it down.

## Seven in ten: what NCRB's data show

The figures come from Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India (ADSI), an annual report the National Crime Records Bureau builds from police records. In 2022 it counted 1,70,924 suicides, a rate of 12.4 per lakh people [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Of those, 1,22,724 were men [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. The 2023 total of 1,71,418 worked out to 12.3 per lakh [[theprint-pti-ncrb-adsi-2023]]. The numbers shift by fractions; the shape stays the same.

Detailed 2024 breakdowns had not been independently confirmed when this story was written, so the profile below uses NCRB's 2022 tables.

That profile cuts against a familiar image. The typical man in these records is not a lonely young drifter with no ties. He is married. In most Indian homes, being a married man also means being the one expected to earn, to repay, to arrange, and to keep quiet when any of it goes wrong.

## Married, working, under pressure: daily wage earners

In 2022, daily wage earners were the largest group among men who died by suicide: 41,433 of the 1,22,724 men, about one in three [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Across all suicides that year, daily wage earners numbered 45,185, or 26.4%, which means more than nine in ten of them were men [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. In 2023 the group grew to 47,170 deaths, 27.5% of all suicides, and was again the largest single category [[business-standard-adsi-2023-daily-wage]].

The women's side of the same table is just as gendered. Among women, the largest group was housewives: 25,309 in 2022, which was 52.5% of the 48,172 women who died by suicide [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. NCRB's occupation columns read like a summary of Indian gender roles. Men are recorded as earners, women as homemakers, and each group is boxed in by what the family expects of it.

One caution matters here. These are counts, not rates. Daily wage work employs a very large number of Indian men, so a big count partly reflects a big group. What the numbers do show is where the pressure lands: on men whose income can stop any day, with no salary to fall back on.

Consider this situation. A 38-year-old painter in Surat has found four days of work this month. School fees are due, there is a loan from a relative, and his father's medicines cost money every week. At home he says work is slow. With friends he jokes. Nobody asks how he is, because he is the one who is supposed to have the answers. None of that pressure appears in any official record, which is exactly why the people around him have to notice it.

## What police-recorded causes cannot tell us

NCRB also records a cause for each suicide. In 2022, family problems other than marriage-related ones accounted for 31.7%, illness for 18.4% and marriage-related problems for 4.8%: together, 54.9% [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. These boxes are filled in by the police, usually from what relatives say after a death. "Family problems" can hide debt, unemployment, alcohol, violence or years of untreated depression. A single category cannot hold a life.

India's National Mental Health Survey of 2015-16 shows part of what police files miss. It found a mental disorder in 13.9% of men against 7.5% of women, and alcohol use disorder in 9% of men against 0.5% of women; men aged 30 to 49 were the most affected group [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. In many Indian homes, a man's distress is not called depression. It is called drinking, temper or "tension", and it is handled, if at all, as a flaw in his character rather than a problem with his health.

> The data do not show that men break more easily. They show that men are rarely allowed to say they are breaking.

The World Health Organization is clear that suicides are preventable [[who-suicide]]. Prevention starts long before a crisis: in whether a man has anyone he can tell, and whether telling them feels safe.

## Reaching out: Tele-MANAS 14416 and other first steps

Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock tele-mental-health helpline on 14416, has been running since October 2022 and offers counselling to anyone who needs it [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. A man does not have to be in crisis to call, and he does not need a medical name for what he is feeling. Friends and family can call too, to ask how to help.

The law is no longer a reason to stay silent. Under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017, a person who attempts suicide is presumed, unless proved otherwise, to be under severe stress and is not to be tried or punished for it, and the government is obliged to provide care and rehabilitation [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, in force since 1 July 2024, has no general offence of attempted suicide [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. No family should avoid a hospital out of fear of the police.

If a man around you calls himself a burden, stops talking about the future or starts giving his things away, ask him plainly whether he is thinking about suicide. Then listen. Help him call 14416, or call it yourself first. In an emergency, call 112.

And change the script at home. A lost job, a failed crop or a debt is a family problem to solve together, not a test of one man's worth. The breadwinner is allowed to say he is tired.
men-suicide-india-breadwinner-trap.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne 1,70,746 suicides record kiye, jo 2023 ke 1,71,418 se thode kam the [[theprint-ncrb-adsi-2024]]. In totals ke peeche ek pattern hai jo saal dar saal mushkil se hilta hai: marne walon mein zyada tar mard hote hain. 2022 mein, jo latest saal hai jiska male-female breakdown hum verify kar paaye, suicide victims mein 71.8% mard the, aur inmein se lagbhag 68% mard shaadi-shuda the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. Yeh kahani is baare mein nahi hai ki mard kamzor hote hain, ya auraton ki takleef kam hai. Yeh kahani is baare mein hai ki Indian mardon se kya-kya uthaane ki ummeed ki jaati hai, aur unhe use neeche rakhne ki ijaazat kitni kam milti hai.

## Das mein saat: NCRB ka data kya dikhata hai

Yeh figures Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India (ADSI) se aate hain, ek saalana report jo National Crime Records Bureau police records se banata hai. 2022 mein isne 1,70,924 suicides gine, yaani har lakh logon pe 12.4 ka rate [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Inmein se 1,22,724 mard the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. 2023 ka total 1,71,418 tha, jo har lakh pe 12.3 banta hai [[theprint-pti-ncrb-adsi-2023]]. Numbers thoda-bahut upar-neeche hote hain; shape wahi rehti hai.

Jab yeh story likhi gayi, tab tak 2024 ke detailed breakdowns independently confirm nahi hue the, isliye neeche ki profile NCRB ki 2022 tables pe based hai.

Yeh profile ek jaani-pehchaani image ko todti hai. In records ka typical mard koi akela, bina rishton wala young ladka nahi hai. Woh shaadi-shuda hai. Zyada tar Indian gharon mein shaadi-shuda mard hone ka matlab yeh bhi hai ki kamaana, karza chukaana, sab arrange karna usi ka kaam hai, aur kuch bhi galat ho toh chup rehna bhi.

## Shaadi-shuda, kaam pe, pressure mein: daily wage earners

2022 mein suicide se marne wale mardon mein sabse bada group daily wage earners ka tha: 1,22,724 mardon mein se 41,433, yaani lagbhag har teen mein se ek [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. Us saal saare suicides mein daily wage earners 45,185 the, yaani 26.4%, jiska matlab hai ki inmein das mein se nau se zyada mard the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. 2023 mein yeh group badh ke 47,170 deaths tak pahunch gaya, saare suicides ka 27.5%, aur phir se sabse badi single category bana [[business-standard-adsi-2023-daily-wage]].

Usi table ka auraton wala hissa bhi utna hi gendered hai. Auraton mein sabse bada group housewives ka tha: 2022 mein 25,309, jo suicide se mari 48,172 auraton ka 52.5% tha [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]]. NCRB ke occupation columns Indian gender roles ka summary lagte hain. Mard earners ke roop mein record hote hain, auratein homemakers ke roop mein, aur dono groups family ki ummeedon ke dabbe mein band hain.

Yahan ek baat dhyaan mein rakhni zaroori hai. Yeh counts hain, rates nahi. Daily wage kaam mein Indian mardon ki bahut badi sankhya lagi hai, isliye bada count kuch had tak bada group bhi dikhata hai. Lekin numbers yeh zaroor dikhate hain ki pressure kahan girta hai: un mardon pe jinki kamaai kisi bhi din ruk sakti hai, aur peeche koi salary nahi hoti.

Ek situation socho. Surat mein 38 saal ke ek painter ko is mahine sirf chaar din ka kaam mila hai. School ki fees deni hai, ek rishtedaar ka loan chal raha hai, aur papa ki dawaiyon ka kharcha har hafte aata hai. Ghar pe woh kehta hai kaam thanda hai. Doston ke saath mazaak karta hai. Koi nahi poochhta ki woh kaisa hai, kyunki saare jawab toh usi ke paas hone chahiye. Is pressure ka koi bhi hissa kisi official record mein nahi dikhta, aur isi wajah se uske aas-paas ke logon ko ise notice karna padega.

## Police ke likhe 'causes' kya nahi bata sakte

NCRB har suicide ka ek cause bhi record karta hai. 2022 mein shaadi se judi problems ke alawa baaki family problems 31.7%, illness 18.4% aur shaadi se judi problems 4.8% thi: kul mila ke 54.9% [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. Yeh boxes police bharti hai, aksar maut ke baad rishtedaaron ki baaton se. "Family problems" ke peeche karza, berozgaari, sharaab, hinsa ya saalon ka bina ilaaj wala depression chhupa ho sakta hai. Ek category mein poori zindagi nahi samaa sakti.

India ka National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 dikhata hai ki police files kya miss karti hain. Isne 13.9% mardon mein mental disorder paaya, jabki auraton mein 7.5%, aur alcohol use disorder 9% mardon mein tha, auraton mein sirf 0.5%; 30 se 49 saal ke mard sabse zyada affected group the [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Bahut se Indian gharon mein mard ki takleef ko depression nahi kaha jaata. Use peena, gussa ya "tension" kaha jaata hai, aur agar kuch kiya bhi jaata hai toh use uske character ki kami maana jaata hai, sehat ki problem nahi.

> Data yeh nahi dikhata ki mard jaldi toot jaate hain. Yeh dikhata hai ki mardon ko yeh kehne ki ijaazat shayad hi milti hai ki woh toot rahe hain.

World Health Organization saaf kehta hai ki suicide roke ja sakte hain [[who-suicide]]. Bachaav crisis se bahut pehle shuru hota hai: is baat se ki kya mard ke paas koi hai jisse woh baat kar sake, aur kya baat karna safe lagta hai.

## Haath badhao: Tele-MANAS 14416 aur pehle kadam

Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free aur din-raat chalne wali tele-mental-health helpline 14416, October 2022 se chal rahi hai aur kisi ko bhi counselling deti hai jise zaroorat ho [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Call karne ke liye crisis mein hona zaroori nahi, aur apni feeling ko koi medical naam dena bhi zaroori nahi. Dost aur family bhi call karke poochh sakte hain ki madad kaise karein.

Ab kanoon chup rehne ki wajah nahi hai. Mental Healthcare Act 2017 ke tahat, suicide attempt karne wale ke baare mein maana jaata hai ki woh severe stress mein tha (jab tak ulta saabit na ho), us pe na case chal sakta hai na saza ho sakti hai, aur sarkar ki zimmedari hai ki use care aur rehabilitation de [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. 1 July 2024 se laagu Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita mein attempted suicide ka koi general offence nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Kisi bhi family ko police ke darr se hospital jaane se nahi bachna chahiye.

Agar tumhare aas-paas koi mard khud ko bojh kehta hai, future ki baat karna band kar deta hai, ya apni cheezein dena shuru kar deta hai, toh usse seedha poochho ki kya woh suicide ke baare mein soch raha hai. Phir suno. Use 14416 pe call karne mein madad karo, ya pehle khud call kar lo. Emergency mein 112 pe call karo.

Aur ghar ka script badlo. Naukri chhootna, fasal kharab hona ya karza, yeh poori family ki problem hai jo milke suljhani hai, kisi ek mard ki keemat ka test nahi. Ghar chalaane wala bhi keh sakta hai ki woh thak gaya hai.

myths-about-queer-indians.en:
Imagine a 22-year-old in Kanpur who tells his parents he is gay. Within a week he has heard four sentences. From his father: this is all Western. From his mother: it will be fine after marriage. From an uncle: it is against the law. And from a cousin, a question meant as an insult: is he now "a hijra"?

Each sentence is a claim about facts, so each can be checked against the Gazette, the Supreme Court, the Census and the medical regulator. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Myth: it is a Western import

Start with what is written down. The punishment is the old part: Section 377, the provision used to criminalise same-sex relations, sat in the Indian Penal Code of 1860 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. India's own Supreme Court read it down on 6 September 2018 [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Indian law does not treat gender diversity as foreign either. The definition of "transgender person" in the 2026 amendment to the transgender law lists "socio-cultural identities" by name: kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Those are words from Indian languages. When Census 2011 offered a gender category beyond male and female, 4,87,803 people were counted in it [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Why the myth survives: the English words are new. "Gay", "queer" and "LGBTQIA+" reached most homes through films, news and social media, so the vocabulary gets mistaken for the people. The people were already here.

## Myth: it is a phase that marriage will fix

Being lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or asexual is not an illness, so there is nothing to cure. In a letter dated 25 August 2022 to all state medical councils, the National Medical Commission declared that conducting "conversion therapy" on LGBTQIA+ persons is professional misconduct [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]]. It acted after the Madras High Court, in June 2021, directed that any attempt to medically "cure" or change a person's sexual orientation or gender identity be prohibited [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

Marriage is the home-remedy version of the same idea. A wedding does not change whom a person is attracted to. It pulls a second person into the harm: a spouse who was never told the truth, married to someone who was often given no real choice either.

Why it survives: some young people do take time to understand their feelings, and families hold on to that uncertainty as hope. Taking time to know yourself is not the same as being curable.

## Myth: it is illegal in India

On 6 September 2018, in *Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India*, a five-judge Supreme Court bench unanimously read down Section 377. Consensual sex between adults of the same sex stopped being a crime; non-consensual acts stayed punishable [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

The confusion has a real history. The Delhi High Court decriminalised consensual gay sex on 2 July 2009. The Supreme Court reversed that verdict on 11 December 2013, and it was a crime again for nearly five years [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. A relative who insists "the court said it is illegal" may be remembering 2013.

What is true today is much narrower. On 17 October 2023 the Supreme Court held that there is no fundamental right to marry and declined to recognise same-sex marriage, leaving the question to Parliament [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. "The state will not register your marriage" and "you are a criminal" are different sentences. Two adults of the same sex in a consensual relationship commit no offence. Parliament itself, in the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, names sexual orientation among the grounds on which mental health care must not discriminate [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## Myth: transgender means hijra

Hijra, kinner, aravani and jogta are names of specific communities with their own histories and customs. "Transgender" is wider: it describes anyone whose gender identity differs from the sex recorded at their birth. That includes trans men, trans women and non-binary people who never belonged to any of those communities. It is also separate from being gay, which is about attraction, not identity.

The Supreme Court took the wider view. On 15 April 2014, in the NALSA judgment, it recognised transgender persons as a "third gender" and upheld their right to self-identify their gender [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. The 2019 transgender law then gave every transgender person "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

Then the record turns. The 2026 amendment deleted that right and rewrote the definition around the socio-cultural identities, intersex persons and people forced into a transgender identity. It adds that the term does not include "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Trans men, trans women and genderqueer persons, who were named in the 2019 definition, are no longer listed. On paper, Parliament has moved the law towards the myth. The amendment is under challenge in the Supreme Court, which heard the petitions on 17 August 2026 [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

> A statute can narrow a definition. It cannot make trans men and trans women stop existing.

## Why these myths survive, and what they cost

Each myth does a job for the person saying it. "Western" turns a family member into an outsider. "A phase" lets parents postpone the conversation. "Illegal" works as a threat. "Hijra", thrown as an insult, wounds twice: the person it is aimed at, and the communities whose name is being used as abuse.

India does not count the costs. We found no official figure for how many queer Indians are taken to a "healer", pushed into a marriage or put out of the house. The record does show how thin official recognition is. The Census figure is widely seen as an undercount, and by December 2024 only 24,015 transgender certificates had been issued nationwide, about 5% of even that count [[pib-mosje-transgender-parliament-reply-2024]].

If you are the one hearing these four sentences at home: none of them is true, and you do not have to win the argument tonight. Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and open round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. If anyone confines or hurts you, call 112. If you are the one saying them, check the record first.
myths-about-queer-indians.hg:
Socho, Kanpur ka ek 22 saal ka ladka apne parents ko batata hai ki woh gay hai. Ek hafte ke andar use chaar baatein sunne ko milti hain. Papa se: yeh sab Western hai. Mummy se: shaadi ke baad sab theek ho jayega. Ek chacha se: yeh kanoon ke khilaaf hai. Aur ek cousin se ek sawaal, jo gaali ki tarah poocha gaya: toh kya ab woh "hijra" hai?

Har baat facts ke baare mein ek claim hai, isliye har ek ko Gazette, Supreme Court, Census aur medical regulator ke record se check kiya ja sakta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Myth: yeh West se aaya hai

Shuru karo us cheez se jo likhi hui hai. Purani cheez toh saza hai: Section 377, jis provision se same-sex relations ko crime banaya jaata tha, 1860 ke Indian Penal Code mein thi [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. India ke apne Supreme Court ne 6 September 2018 ko ise read down kiya [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Indian law gender diversity ko bhi videshi nahi maanta. Transgender law ke 2026 ke amendment mein "transgender person" ki definition "socio-cultural identities" ko naam lekar ginati hai: kinner, hijra, aravani aur jogta [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Yeh Indian languages ke shabd hain. Jab Census 2011 mein male aur female ke alawa ek gender category di gayi, toh usme 4,87,803 log gine gaye [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Yeh myth kyun zinda hai: English ke words naye hain. "Gay", "queer" aur "LGBTQIA+" zyada tar gharon mein films, news aur social media se pahunche, isliye log vocabulary ko hi insaan samajh lete hain. Log toh pehle se yahin the.

## Myth: yeh ek phase hai jo shaadi se theek ho jayega

Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender ya asexual hona koi bimaari nahi hai, isliye ilaaj karne ko kuch hai hi nahi. 25 August 2022 ko saari state medical councils ko bheje ek letter mein National Medical Commission ne declare kiya ki LGBTQIA+ logon par "conversion therapy" karna professional misconduct hai [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]]. Usne yeh tab kiya jab Madras High Court ne June 2021 mein order diya ki kisi ke sexual orientation ya gender identity ko medically "cure" karne ya badalne ki har koshish par rok lage [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

Shaadi isi soch ka gharelu nuskha hai. Shaadi se yeh nahi badalta ki insaan kiski taraf attract hota hai. Isse bas ek doosra insaan nuksaan mein kheench liya jaata hai: ek spouse jise sach kabhi bataya hi nahi gaya, aur jiski shaadi aise insaan se hui jise khud bhi aksar koi asli choice nahi di gayi.

Yeh kyun zinda hai: kuch young logon ko apni feelings samajhne mein sach mein time lagta hai, aur families usi uncertainty ko umeed bana kar pakde rehti hain. Khud ko samajhne mein time lagna aur "theek ho sakna" ek baat nahi hai.

## Myth: yeh India mein illegal hai

6 September 2018 ko *Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India* mein Supreme Court ki paanch judges ki bench ne ek-rai se Section 377 ko read down kiya. Same sex ke adults ke beech consensual sex crime nahi raha; bina consent wale acts punishable bane rahe [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Is confusion ki ek asli history hai. Delhi High Court ne 2 July 2009 ko consensual gay sex ko decriminalise kiya. Supreme Court ne 11 December 2013 ko woh faisla palat diya, aur kareeb paanch saal tak yeh phir se crime raha [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Jo rishtedaar zor dekar kehta hai "court ne kaha tha yeh illegal hai", use shayad 2013 yaad hai.

Aaj jo sach hai, woh isse kaafi chhota hai. 17 October 2023 ko Supreme Court ne kaha ki shaadi karne ka koi fundamental right nahi hai, same-sex marriage ko recognise karne se mana kiya aur yeh sawaal Parliament par chhod diya [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. "State tumhari shaadi register nahi karega" aur "tum criminal ho" do alag baatein hain. Same sex ke do adults, jo consensual relationship mein hain, koi offence nahi karte. Khud Parliament ne Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 mein sexual orientation ko un grounds mein gina hai jin par mental health care mein discrimination nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## Myth: transgender ka matlab hijra hai

Hijra, kinner, aravani aur jogta khaas communities ke naam hain, jinki apni history aur apne riwaaz hain. "Transgender" isse bada word hai: yeh har us insaan ke liye hai jiski gender identity us sex se alag hai jo uske janam par record hua tha. Isme trans men, trans women aur non-binary log bhi aate hain, jo kabhi in communities ka hissa nahi rahe. Yeh gay hone se bhi alag hai, kyunki gay hona attraction ke baare mein hai, identity ke baare mein nahi.

Supreme Court ne yahi bada nazariya apnaya. 15 April 2014 ko NALSA judgment mein usne transgender logon ko "third gender" ke roop mein maanyata di aur apna gender khud pehchaanne ke unke right ko barkaraar rakha [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Phir 2019 ke transgender law ne har transgender insaan ko "a right to self-perceived gender identity" diya [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

Phir record palat jaata hai. 2026 ke amendment ne woh right hata diya aur definition ko socio-cultural identities, intersex logon aur un logon ke ird-gird dobara likha jinhe zabardasti transgender identity mein dhakela gaya. Usme yeh bhi joda gaya ki is term mein "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" shaamil nahi hain [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Trans men, trans women aur genderqueer log, jinka naam 2019 ki definition mein tha, ab list mein nahi hain. Kaagaz par, Parliament ne law ko myth ki taraf khiska diya hai. Is amendment ko Supreme Court mein challenge kiya gaya hai, jisne 17 August 2026 ko petitions suni [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

> Ek law definition ko chhota kar sakta hai. Woh trans men aur trans women ka wajood khatam nahi kar sakta.

## Yeh myths kyun zinda hain, aur inki keemat kya hai

Har myth bolne wale ke liye ek kaam karta hai. "Western" ghar ke hi insaan ko bahar wala bana deta hai. "Phase" parents ko baat taalne ka mauka deta hai. "Illegal" dhamki ka kaam karta hai. Aur "hijra", jab gaali ki tarah phenka jaata hai, do baar chot karta hai: us insaan ko jis par nishana hai, aur un communities ko jinke naam ko gaali banaya ja raha hai.

India is keemat ko ginta hi nahi. Humein koi official figure nahi mila ki kitne queer Indians ko "healer" ke paas le jaaya jaata hai, shaadi mein dhakela jaata hai ya ghar se nikaal diya jaata hai. Record yeh zaroor dikhata hai ki official recognition kitni patli hai. Census ke figure ko aam taur par undercount maana jaata hai, aur December 2024 tak poore desh mein sirf 24,015 transgender certificates issue hue the, yaani us count ka bhi kareeb 5% [[pib-mosje-transgender-parliament-reply-2024]].

Agar ghar par yeh chaar baatein tum sun rahe ho: inme se ek bhi sach nahi hai, aur tumhe aaj raat hi behes jeetni zaroori nahi. Tele-MANAS 14416 free hai aur din-raat khula hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Agar koi tumhe band kare ya chot pahunchaye, toh 112 par call karo. Aur agar yeh baatein tum bol rahe ho, toh pehle record check kar lo.

parents-guide-when-child-comes-out.en:
Imagine it is a Sunday night in Kanpur. The plates are cleared, and your 17-year-old says, "I need to tell you something. I'm gay." Or: "I'm not a boy. I'm a girl." What you say in the next five minutes will stay with your child for years. Many Indian parents reach for the same three answers: it's a phase, we'll see a doctor, don't tell anyone. All three do damage.

## The first five minutes: what to say and what not to

Your child has probably rehearsed this for months. They are watching your face more than listening to your words. Start with the two sentences that matter most: "Thank you for telling me." And: "I love you. That has not changed."

You do not have to understand everything tonight. It is honest to say, "I need time to take this in, but I am not going anywhere." Then ask about them, not about you. How long have you known? Who else knows? Is anyone at school or online troubling you?

Avoid the sentences that close the door. "It's a phase" says you did not believe them. "Who put this in your head?" blames a friend, a film or the internet. "What will people say?" says your reputation comes first. And do not tell relatives without your child's permission. Coming out is their story to tell, at their pace.

Remember, too: coming out tells you who your child is, or whom they are drawn to. It does not tell you what they have done.

## It is not an illness, and it is not illegal

If you remember gay sex being a crime, you remember right. The Delhi High Court decriminalised consensual gay sex in 2009, and the Supreme Court reversed that in December 2013 [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Then, on 6 September 2018, a five-judge Supreme Court bench in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India unanimously read down Section 377 of the IPC. Consensual sex between adults of the same sex is no longer a crime [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Health law protects your child too. Section 21 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 bars discrimination in mental health care on any basis, naming sexual orientation among the protected grounds [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. If your child ever needs help for anxiety or low mood, that is what gets treated, not their sexuality.

If your child is transgender, the law is in flux. The Supreme Court recognised the right to self-identify one's gender in NALSA (2014) [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]], but a 2026 amendment, now under challenge, makes a transgender certificate depend on a medical board's recommendation [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The 'cure' trap: doctors, babas and conversion practices

Fear sends parents looking for a fix, and someone is always selling one: a doctor with pills or hormones, a counsellor promising "correction", a baba with rituals. None of them can change your child's sexual orientation or gender identity. Trying only deepens the shame and breaks your child's trust in you.

In June 2021, in S. Sushma v. Commissioner of Police, a case brought by a lesbian couple, the Madras High Court ordered a ban on any attempt to medically "cure" or change the sexual orientation or gender identity of LGBTQIA+ people, with action against professionals involved, up to withdrawing their licence [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]]. In a letter dated 25 August 2022, the National Medical Commission told all state medical councils that "conversion therapy" on LGBTQIA+ persons is professional misconduct [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

Even the Centre has named the problem: in April 2024 it set up a committee, chaired by the Cabinet Secretary, to recommend measures against discrimination, violence and involuntary medical treatment of queer persons [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. We could find no report from it yet.

Notice the gap: the NMC rule binds registered doctors, but a baba or an unlicensed "healer" has no licence to lose and no regulator watching. Refuse anyone who offers a cure, and report a doctor who does to your state medical council.

## Marriage will not fix it: why pressure backfires

The most common Indian "cure" is not a clinic. It is a wedding: once he is married, it will settle. It will not. Marriage does not change whom a person is attracted to. It drags a second person, the spouse, into the harm, and often children too.

On 17 October 2023, in Supriyo v. Union of India, the Supreme Court declined to recognise same-sex marriage and left the question to Parliament [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. So your child may not be able to marry the person they love. That is a reason for patience, not for forcing a wedding they do not want.

A child pushed to "change" learns to hide. They stop telling you where they are and whom they are with, and stop calling when they are in trouble. A queer teenager who can still talk to their parents is a safer teenager.

## Protecting your child's mental health

We could find no reliable national data on the mental health of LGBTQIA+ young people in India, and that silence is itself a failure. You do not need a statistic to know what rejection, bullying and forced secrecy do to a teenager.

Watch for changes that do not pass: pulling away from friends, skipping classes, not sleeping or eating, giving things away, or saying everyone would be better off without them. Do not wait for your child to bring it up. Ask directly and calmly, and listen.

Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock mental-health helpline on 14416, offers counselling to anyone in need [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Call together if your child agrees, or call for yourself: parents need support too. If you look for a therapist, ask one question first: do you see being gay or transgender as something to treat? Anything but a clear no means keep looking.

Your child took a risk by telling you. Make sure they never regret it.
parents-guide-when-child-comes-out.hg:
Imagine kijiye, Kanpur mein Sunday ki raat hai. Khaane ki plates uth chuki hain, aur aapka 17 saal ka bachcha kehta hai, "Mujhe aapko kuch batana hai. Main gay hoon." Ya phir: "Main ladka nahi hoon. Main ladki hoon." Agle paanch minute mein aap jo kahenge, woh aapke bachche ko barson yaad rahega. Bahut se Indian parents ke munh se wahi teen jawaab nikalte hain: yeh ek phase hai, doctor ko dikhayenge, kisi ko batana mat. Teeno nuksaan karte hain.

## Pehle paanch minute: kya kahein aur kya nahi

Aapke bachche ne shayad mahino tak is pal ki rehearsal ki hai. Woh aapke shabdon se zyada aapka chehra dekh raha hai. Shuruaat un do sentences se kijiye jo sabse zyada maayne rakhte hain: "Mujhe batane ke liye thank you." Aur: "Main tumse pyaar karta/karti hoon. Woh nahi badla."

Aaj raat hi sab kuch samajh lena zaroori nahi hai. Yeh kehna imaandari hai: "Mujhe yeh samajhne mein time lagega, lekin main tumhare saath hoon aur rahunga/rahungi." Phir apne baare mein nahi, uske baare mein poochiye. Tumhe kab se pata hai? Aur kise pata hai? Kya school mein ya online koi tumhe pareshaan kar raha hai?

Un sentences se bachiye jo darwaaza band kar dete hain. "Yeh ek phase hai" ka matlab hai ki aapne uski baat par yakeen nahi kiya. "Yeh tumhare dimaag mein kisne daala?" kisi dost, film ya internet par ilzaam daalta hai. "Log kya kahenge?" batata hai ki aapki izzat pehle aati hai. Aur bachche ki permission ke bina rishtedaaron ko mat bataiye. Come out karna uski apni kahani hai, jo woh apni raftaar se batayega.

Ek baat aur yaad rakhiye: come out karna aapko batata hai ki aapka bachcha kaun hai, ya woh kiski taraf attract hota hai. Yeh nahi batata ki usne kya kiya hai.

## Yeh bimari nahi hai, aur illegal bhi nahi

Agar aapko yaad hai ki gay sex crime hua karta tha, toh aapko sahi yaad hai. Delhi High Court ne 2009 mein consent wale gay sex ko decriminalise kiya tha, aur Supreme Court ne December 2013 mein woh faisla palat diya [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Phir 6 September 2018 ko Supreme Court ke paanch judges ki bench ne Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India mein IPC ke Section 377 ko unanimously read down kiya. Same-sex adults ke beech consent wala sex ab crime nahi hai [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Health law bhi aapke bachche ko protect karta hai. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ka Section 21 mental health care mein kisi bhi basis par discrimination rokta hai, aur protected grounds mein sexual orientation ka naam leta hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Agar aapke bachche ko kabhi anxiety ya low mood ke liye help chahiye, toh ilaaj usi ka hoga, uski sexuality ka nahi.

Agar aapka bachcha transgender hai, toh law abhi badal raha hai. Supreme Court ne NALSA (2014) mein apna gender khud identify karne ka right maana tha [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]], lekin 2026 ka ek amendment, jo abhi court mein challenge ho raha hai, transgender certificate ko medical board ki recommendation par tika deta hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 'Cure' ka jaal: doctors, babas aur conversion practices

Darr parents ko kisi "ilaaj" ki talaash mein bhejta hai, aur koi na koi use bechne ke liye hamesha taiyaar milta hai: goliyon ya hormones wala doctor, "correction" ka vaada karne wala counsellor, rituals wala baba. Inme se koi bhi aapke bachche ki sexual orientation ya gender identity nahi badal sakta. Koshish karne se bas sharm gehri hoti hai aur bachche ka aap par se bharosa toot jaata hai.

June 2021 mein, S. Sushma v. Commissioner of Police mein, jo ek lesbian couple ka case tha, Madras High Court ne LGBTQIA+ logon ki sexual orientation ya gender identity ko medically "cure" karne ya badalne ki har koshish par rok ka order diya, aur kaha ki isme shaamil professionals par action ho, jo unka licence withdraw karne tak ja sakta hai [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]]. 25 August 2022 ki ek chitthi mein National Medical Commission ne sabhi state medical councils ko bataya ki LGBTQIA+ logon par "conversion therapy" karna professional misconduct hai [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

Centre ne bhi is problem ka naam liya hai: April 2024 mein usne Cabinet Secretary ki chairmanship mein ek committee banayi, jise queer logon ke saath discrimination, violence aur zabardasti medical treatment ke khilaaf upaay suggest karne hain [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. Humein ab tak uski koi report nahi mili.

Gap par dhyaan dijiye: NMC ka rule registered doctors par lagu hota hai, lekin kisi baba ya bina licence wale "healer" ke paas khone ke liye koi licence nahi hai, aur us par nazar rakhne wala koi regulator nahi hai. Jo bhi cure offer kare, use mana kijiye, aur aisa karne wale doctor ko apni state medical council mein report kijiye.

## Shaadi se yeh theek nahi hoga: pressure ulta kyun padta hai

India ka sabse aam "cure" koi clinic nahi hai. Woh ek shaadi hai: ek baar shaadi ho jaaye, sab settle ho jaayega. Aisa nahi hoga. Shaadi se yeh nahi badalta ki koi insaan kiski taraf attract hota hai. Woh ek doosre insaan ko, yaani spouse ko, is nuksaan mein ghaseet leti hai, aur aksar bachchon ko bhi.

17 October 2023 ko Supriyo v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne same-sex marriage ko recognise karne se mana kiya aur yeh sawaal Parliament par chhod diya [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. Yaani ho sakta hai ki aapka bachcha us insaan se shaadi na kar paaye jisse woh pyaar karta hai. Yeh sabr rakhne ki wajah hai, uski marzi ke khilaaf shaadi thopne ki nahi.

Jis bachche par "badalne" ka pressure daala jaata hai, woh chhupana seekh jaata hai. Woh aapko batana band kar deta hai ki woh kahan hai aur kiske saath hai, aur mushkil mein phasne par aapko call karna bhi band kar deta hai. Jo queer teenager apne parents se ab bhi baat kar sakta hai, woh zyada safe teenager hai.

## Apne bachche ki mental health ki hifazat

India mein LGBTQIA+ young logon ki mental health par humein koi bharosemand national data nahi mila, aur yeh khamoshi apne aap mein ek failure hai. Rejection, bullying aur zabardasti ka secret ek teenager ke saath kya karte hain, yeh jaanne ke liye aapko kisi statistic ki zaroorat nahi hai.

Un badlaavon par nazar rakhiye jo guzarte nahi: doston se door ho jaana, classes chhodna, na sona, na khaana, apni cheezein baant dena, ya yeh kehna ki uske bina sab behtar rahenge. Is intezaar mein mat rahiye ki bachcha khud baat chhede. Seedhe aur shaant hokar poochiye, phir suniye.

Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free, round-the-clock mental-health helpline, 14416 par har zarooratmand ko counselling deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Agar bachcha raazi ho toh saath mein call kijiye, ya apne liye call kijiye: parents ko bhi support chahiye. Agar aap therapist dhoondh rahe hain, toh pehle ek sawaal poochiye: kya aap gay ya transgender hone ko ilaaj ki cheez maante hain? Saaf "nahi" ke alawa koi bhi jawaab mile, toh kisi aur ko dhoondhiye.

Aapke bachche ne aapko batakar ek risk liya hai. Yeh pakka kijiye ki use is par kabhi pachtaana na pade.

partner-violence-world-india-numbers.en:
Global statistics on violence against women usually reach us as one line: "one in three". Behind that line sit separate counts with different age groups, time frames and definitions. Here are six of them, with what each one measures and where India sits. The short version: by WHO's estimate, more than one in five Indian women aged 15-49 who have ever had a husband or partner faced physical or sexual violence from him in a single year [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

| Number | What it counts |
|---|---|
| 840 million | women and girls who have ever faced partner violence, non-partner sexual violence or both |
| 31% | women in Southern Asia who have ever faced partner violence |
| 22.4% | partnered women in India who faced partner violence in the past 12 months |
| 137 a day | women and girls killed by a partner or family member in 2024 |
| 0.2% a year | average fall in partner violence over 20 years |
| 0.2% | share of global development aid spent on prevention in 2022 |

## 840 million: the lifetime count

About 840 million women and girls, nearly 1 in 3, have faced physical or sexual violence from an intimate partner, or sexual violence from someone else, at least once in their lives, by WHO's 2023 estimates [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. That is 30.4% of women aged 15 and older, and 31.6% of those aged 15-49 [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Partner violence alone accounts for about 682 million women aged 15 and older, or 24.7% of those who have ever been married or partnered [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. About 263 million women have been sexually assaulted by someone who was not their partner [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. Some women are in both groups.

Two caveats. The partner-violence indicator covers physical and sexual violence only; psychological abuse and controlling behaviour are left out. And WHO says all surveys are likely to underestimate violence, because many women never disclose it [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Treat 840 million as a floor.

## 31% and 22.4%: South Asia and India

Among ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49 worldwide, 25.8% have faced physical or sexual violence from a husband or male partner at least once. In Southern Asia, the UN region that includes India, the figure is 31%, among the highest of any region [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

WHO also models an estimate for each country. For India it is 29.9% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49 over a lifetime, and 22.4% in the past 12 months. The past-year figure places India among the 33 countries and territory with the highest rates. Afghanistan is the only other South Asian country in that group. The global past-year average for the same age group is 13.7% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

The past-year number is the more telling one. A lifetime figure includes violence that ended years ago. A 12-month figure describes homes where it is happening now. Imagine a lane with nine married women under 50 in any Indian town. On WHO's estimate, about two of them, on average, faced physical or sexual violence from their husbands in the last year.

The caveats: this is the output of a statistical model built on survey data, so it will not exactly match India's NFHS reports, and its uncertainty range runs from 17.4% to 27.7%. It also cannot be compared with WHO's earlier estimate for India [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Most never reach anyone official. In NFHS-5, only 14% of Indian women who had faced physical or sexual violence had ever sought help, and 77% had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 137 a day: the deadliest end

Around 50,000 women and girls were killed by intimate partners or other family members in 2024. That is about 60% of all women and girls killed intentionally that year, or an average of 137 a day [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]].

Men and boys were 80% of the world's homicide victims in 2024, but only 11% of male victims were killed by a partner or family member [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. A murdered man was usually killed by someone outside his family. A murdered woman was usually killed by someone inside hers.

One caveat: the 2024 figure is lower than the 51,100 estimated for 2023, but the report says the difference reflects which countries supplied data, not a real decline [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]].

Where countries do not report such killings, the UN builds its estimate from related offences such as dowry death and honour killing, where national law defines them [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Indian law defines dowry death, and police recorded 5,737 such cases in 2024, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 0.2% a year: the speed of change

Partner violence against women has fallen by an average of only about 0.2% a year over the past 20 years, and the "one in three" figure has stagnated. WHO says this makes it very unlikely that the world will meet its target of eliminating violence against women and girls by 2030 [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

WHO's previous round, using data up to 2018, counted about 736 million women [[who-vaw-estimates-2021]], against 840 million now. That gap is not a measured rise: WHO states that the 2023 estimates are not comparable with the 2018 and 2010 rounds, because methods and data changed [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. The trend finding is the 0.2%, an almost flat line.

## 0.2% of aid: what the world spends on prevention

In 2022, only 0.2% of global development aid went to programmes focused on preventing violence against women, and WHO reported that the funding fell further in 2025 [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]].

In some countries, violence against women costs between 1% and 6% of GDP through police, justice, social protection and health services, a range drawn from selected country studies, not a global estimate [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. Partner violence is also the fourth leading cause of poor health among women worldwide [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. Put the two 0.2% figures side by side: one is the money, the other is the speed.

Numbers this large are made of single homes. Of the Indian women who did seek help after violence, 60.9% turned to their own family and only 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]], so the first response usually comes from a mother, a brother or a friend. If someone tells you, believe her and ask what she needs. If she is in danger now, call 112.
partner-violence-world-india-numbers.hg:
Auraton par violence ke global statistics aksar ek hi line mein hum tak pahunchte hain: "teen mein se ek". Us line ke peeche alag-alag ginti hain, jinke age groups, time frames aur definitions alag hain. Yahan unme se chhe hain: har ek kya naapta hai, aur India usme kahan hai. Short version: WHO ke estimate ke hisaab se, 15-49 saal ki jin Indian auraton ka kabhi pati ya partner raha hai, unme se paanch mein se ek se zyada ne ek hi saal mein usse physical ya sexual violence jheli [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

| Number | Yeh kya ginta hai |
|---|---|
| 840 million | auratein aur ladkiyan jinhone kabhi partner violence, non-partner sexual violence ya dono jheli |
| 31% | Southern Asia ki auratein jinhone kabhi partner violence jheli |
| 22.4% | India ki partnered auratein jinhone pichhle 12 mahinon mein partner violence jheli |
