| 2024 | 9,865 |

Yeh rows NCRB ki Crime in India report ke teen editions se li gayi hain [[ncrb-cii-2018]] [[ncrb-cii-2021]] [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 ka figure har ek lakh auraton par 1.4 cases banta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

2024 ki giravat ka matlab yeh nahi hai ki kam auraton ka peecha hua. NCRB FIRs ginta hai, incidents nahi, aur har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke neeche [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis FIR mein stalking ke baad assault ya killing hui ho, woh us bade crime mein gini jaati hai.

Zyada tar harassment toh FIR tak pahunchta hi nahi. 2005 mein 12% households ne India Human Development Survey ko bataya tha ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko "sometimes" ya "often" harass kiya jaata hai, jabki police records ke hisaab se yeh sirf 0.06% households banta tha: kareeb 200 guna ka gap [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Jo file karti hain, unke hisse intezaar aata hai. 2024 mein courts ne stalking ke jitne trials poore kiye, unme se 25.2% mein conviction hui, aur 52,273 stalking cases, yaani courts ke saamne maujood cases ke 92.8%, saal khatam hone par bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Imagine karo Kanpur ki ek 19 saal ki ladki, jo roz subah ek hi shared auto se coaching jaati hai. Ek aadmi stop par uska intezaar karne lagta hai. Ladki keh deti hai ki use interest nahi hai. Woh ek classmate se uska number le leta hai, har raat message karta hai, phir uske gate ke bahar khada rehne lagta hai. Ghar walon ka jawab: coaching band. Ladki ke mana karne ke baad us aadmi ne jo kuch kiya, Section 78 wahi describe karta hai. Zindagi sirf ladki ki badli.

## Law kise protect karta hai: BNS ke shabd aur uske gaps

Section 78 ke shabdon ke hisaab se stalking sirf ek aadmi kar sakta hai, aur sirf ek aurat ke khilaf [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Text aaj bhi yahi hai, jabki Home Ministry ne July 2024 mein kaha tha ki BNS mein women aur children ke khilaf kai offences gender-neutral kar diye gaye hain, "covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender" [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Jis aadmi ke peeche uski ex-partner padi ho, ya jis aurat ka peecha koi doosri aurat kar rahi ho, woh is section mein cover nahi hote.

Kuch protection doosri jagah milti hai. 18 saal se kam umar ke har insaan ko POCSO protect karta hai, gender chahe jo ho [[pocso-act-2012]]. Transgender person Transgender Persons Act ke Section 18(d) ka sahara le sakte hain, jo unki safety ya well-being ko khatre mein daalne wale abuse par saza deta hai, lekin sirf chhe mahine se do saal tak ki [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Agar koi aapka peecha kar raha hai: pehle steps

Ek saaf 'na' kaafi hai. Message mein bheji gayi 'na' us "clear indication" ka record bhi ban jaati hai jo law maangta hai.

- **Likh lo.** Date, time, jagah, usne kya kiya, kisne dekha. Messages ki copies kisi dost ke paas rakho.
- **Bharose ke logon ko batao.** Stalking us insaan par sabse zyada chalti hai jo ise akele jhel raha ho.
- **Report karo.** Aap kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte ho, incident chahe kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronically bhi; aur jab koi aurat stalking ki complaint deti hai toh use woman officer ko hi record karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Online stalking ke liye cybercrime.gov.in ya 1930 bhi use karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Turant khatra ho toh 112 par call karo.
- **Agar aap uske dost ho,** toh ladki ka number ya uska route aage mat do. Use batao ki jawab 'na' tha.

Film ladki ki aakhri 'na' se seedha shaadi par cut ho jaati hai. Asli zindagi mein aisa koi cut nahi hota. Jab woh 'na' kehti hai, kahani wahin khatam ho jaati hai. Uske baad peecha karne ka ek section number hota hai.

student-suicides-india-decade-rise.en:
In 2024, 14,488 students in India died by suicide, about 80% more than a decade earlier, according to NCRB data [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]. That is about 40 students a day. Over the eleven years from 2014 to 2024, the total was 1,23,918 [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]. The usual explanation is two words long: exam pressure. The records behind these numbers do not support so simple a story, and they are silent on most of what a student's life contains.

## About 80% in a decade, while the national total stood still

The figures come from Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India, the annual report the National Crime Records Bureau builds from police records. The last three years show the pattern.

| Year | Student suicides | All suicides |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 13,044 | 1,70,924 |
| 2023 | 13,892 | 1,71,418 |
| 2024 | 14,488 | 1,70,746 |

Sources: student counts for 2022 and 2023 [[careers360-ncrb-adsi-2023-students]] and 2024 [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]; totals for 2022 [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]], 2023 [[theprint-pti-ncrb-adsi-2023]] and 2024 [[theprint-ncrb-adsi-2024]].

The national total barely moved. The student count rose in each of these years. Students were 7.6% of all suicides in 2022 and 8.1% in 2023, described at the time as the highest count in a decade [[careers360-ncrb-adsi-2023-students]]. In 2024 it went higher still, to roughly one in twelve of all suicides.

India has more young people in schools and colleges than a decade ago, so part of the rise may reflect a bigger group; NCRB publishes counts for students, not rates. And police records are widely believed to under-count suicides.

Men were 71.8% of all those who died by suicide in 2022 [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. But the familiar image of a boy cracking under an entrance exam is not the whole picture. Girls and young women are in the student count too, and they rarely appear in the story adults tell about it.

## What a police entry can and cannot say

NCRB's tables sort each death by the cause police recorded. That entry is written after the death, by people other than the student, and it cannot hold a whole life. Some of its boxes are very wide: across all suicides in 2022, family problems other than marriage-related ones accounted for 31.7% [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]].

A cause on a police form is not a finding about why someone died. An exam result may be the last thing that happened, not the reason.

The exam explanation is also the comfortable one. It blames boards, coaching and cut-offs. It asks nothing of the adults in the room.

## What the records leave out

A police entry holds only what police are told. Being bullied in a hostel, a relationship the family forbade, being outed, sexual abuse by someone at home, watching one parent hit the other: if the student never told anyone, none of it can reach the record.

Silence about abuse is the rule, not the exception. India's 2007 national Study on Child Abuse found that most children who faced sexual abuse told no one, and that only 26.8% of young adults who had been sexually assaulted in childhood had ever told anyone [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Its sample was not nationally representative, so the share is indicative. What a young person has never said aloud cannot reach a police form.

> An adult who asks only about marks will hear only about marks.

Imagine a 17-year-old in a hostel far from home, preparing for an entrance exam. Her mock-test rank has slipped, and that is the part every adult can see. What they cannot see: a relative who sexually abused her years ago still comes to family functions; a classmate is passing around a private photo of her; her parents borrowed money for the fees and mention it on every call. Every item on that list is something an adult could ask about.

## What schools, hostels and families can do

Ask the direct question, calmly and in private: are you thinking about suicide? It tells them the subject is allowed, and then listen.

Wardens and teachers are often the first to notice changes: missed meals, skipped classes, withdrawal from friends, talk of being a burden. Treat these as a reason for a private conversation the same day, not for a complaint to parents about discipline. Every school and hostel needs a counsellor students can reach in private.

Be honest about the limits of secrecy. If a student under 18 tells an adult about sexual abuse, the adult cannot promise to keep it secret: Sections 19 and 21 of the POCSO Act make reporting to the police mandatory for anyone who knows of it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Say so plainly, and stay beside the child through what follows.

Parents: tell your child before the result, not after, that no mark changes their place at home.

## If you are struggling: first steps

Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free, runs round the clock and offers counselling to anyone in need [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. You do not need a diagnosis, or a reason that sounds big enough. If you are under 18, the Child Helpline on 1098 is also for you. In an emergency, call 112.

Tell one person today: a friend, a sibling, a teacher you trust. "I am not okay and I need help" is enough.

If you have already tried to end your life, you will not be punished for it. The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 presumes that a person who attempts suicide is under severe stress and obliges the government to provide care [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Go to a hospital, and take someone with you if you can.

The World Health Organization is clear that suicides are preventable [[who-suicide]]. An exam can be retaken, a course can be changed, a hostel can be left. None of that feels true at two in the morning, which is why the first step is the same every time: tell someone, and let them stay.
student-suicides-india-decade-rise.hg:
NCRB data ke hisaab se 2024 mein India mein 14,488 students suicide se mare, jo ek dashak pehle se lagbhag 80% zyada hai [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]. Yaani roz lagbhag 40 students. 2014 se 2024 ke gyaarah saalon mein total 1,23,918 raha [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]. Iski aam wajah do shabdon mein bata di jaati hai: exam pressure. In numbers ke peeche ke records itni seedhi kahani ka saath nahi dete, aur ek student ki zindagi mein jo kuch hota hai, uske zyada tar hisse pe woh chup hain.

## Ek dashak mein lagbhag 80%, jabki national total wahin khada raha

Yeh figures Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India se aate hain, woh saalana report jo National Crime Records Bureau police records se banata hai. Pichhle teen saal pattern dikha dete hain.

| Saal | Student suicides | Saare suicides |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 13,044 | 1,70,924 |
| 2023 | 13,892 | 1,71,418 |
| 2024 | 14,488 | 1,70,746 |

Sources: 2022 aur 2023 ke student counts [[careers360-ncrb-adsi-2023-students]] aur 2024 ka [[thewire-student-suicides-2014-2024]]; totals 2022 ke liye [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-ch2]], 2023 ke liye [[theprint-pti-ncrb-adsi-2023]] aur 2024 ke liye [[theprint-ncrb-adsi-2024]].

National total mushkil se hila. Student count in teeno saalon mein har saal badha. 2022 mein students saare suicides ka 7.6% the aur 2023 mein 8.1%, jise us waqt ek dashak ki sabse oonchi ginti bataya gaya [[careers360-ncrb-adsi-2023-students]]. 2024 mein yeh aur upar gayi, saare suicides mein lagbhag har baarah mein se ek tak.

India mein ek dashak pehle ke muqaable ab zyada young log schools aur colleges mein hain, toh badhat ka kuch hissa bade group ki wajah se ho sakta hai; NCRB students ke counts chhaapta hai, rates nahi. Aur police records ke baare mein aam taur pe maana jaata hai ki yeh suicides ko kam ginte hain.

2022 mein suicide se marne walon mein 71.8% mard the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]]. Lekin entrance exam ke bojh tale tootte ladke wali jaani-pehchaani image poori tasveer nahi hai. Student count mein ladkiyan aur young auratein bhi hain, aur bade log is baare mein jo kahani sunaate hain usmein woh shayad hi dikhti hain.

## Police ki ek entry kya bata sakti hai aur kya nahi

NCRB ki tables har maut ko us cause ke hisaab se baantti hain jo police ne darj kiya. Woh entry maut ke baad likhi jaati hai, student ke alawa doosre log batate hain, aur ek poori zindagi usmein nahi sama sakti. Kuch dabbe bahut bade hain: 2022 ke saare suicides mein shaadi se judi problems ke alawa baaki family problems ka hissa 31.7% tha [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]].

Police form pe likha cause is baat ki jaanch ka nateeja nahi hota ki kisi ki maut kyun hui. Exam ka result aakhri cheez ho sakti hai jo hui, wajah nahi.

Exam wali wajah sabse aaraamdeh bhi hai. Yeh boards, coaching aur cut-offs ko dosh deti hai. Kamre mein baithe bade logon se yeh kuch nahi maangti.

## Records kya chhod dete hain

Police ki entry mein sirf wahi hota hai jo police ko bataya gaya. Hostel mein bully hona, woh relationship jise family ne mana kar diya, out kar diya jaana, ghar ke kisi insaan ke haathon sexual abuse, ek parent ko doosre pe haath uthate dekhna: agar student ne kabhi kisi ko nahi bataya, toh inmein se kuch bhi record tak nahi pahunch sakta.

Abuse pe chuppi aam baat hai, kabhi-kabhaar ki nahi. India ki 2007 ki national Study on Child Abuse ne paaya ki sexual abuse jhelne wale zyada tar bachchon ne kisi ko nahi bataya, aur jin young adults ke saath bachpan mein sexual assault hua tha unmein se sirf 26.8% ne kabhi kisi ko bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Iska sample nationally representative nahi tha, isliye yeh hissa sirf ek andaaza deta hai. Jo ek young insaan ne kabhi bol ke kaha hi nahi, woh police form tak nahi pahunch sakta.

> Jo bada sirf marks ke baare mein poochhta hai, use sirf marks ke baare mein hi sunne ko milega.

Socho, ek 17 saal ki ladki ghar se door ek hostel mein entrance exam ki taiyaari kar rahi hai. Uski mock-test rank gir gayi hai, aur yahi woh hissa hai jo har bade ko dikhta hai. Jo unhe nahi dikhta: ek rishtedaar jisne saalon pehle uska sexual abuse kiya tha, ab bhi family functions mein aata hai; ek classmate uski ek private photo idhar-udhar bhej raha hai; maa-baap ne fees ke liye udhaar liya hai aur har call pe iska zikr karte hain. Is list ki har cheez ke baare mein koi bada poochh sakta hai.

## Schools, hostels aur families kya kar sakte hain

Seedha sawaal poochho, shaanti se aur akele mein: kya tum suicide ke baare mein soch rahe ho? Isse use pata chalta hai ki is baare mein baat ki ja sakti hai, aur phir suno.

Wardens aur teachers aksar sabse pehle badlaav notice karte hain: khaana chhodna, classes miss karna, doston se door hona, khud ko bojh kehna. Inhe usi din akele mein baat karne ki wajah samjho, parents se discipline ki shikayat karne ki nahi. Har school aur hostel mein ek aisa counsellor hona chahiye jis tak students akele mein pahunch sakein.

Secrecy ki hadon ke baare mein imaandaar raho. Agar 18 se kam ka student kisi bade ko sexual abuse ke baare mein batata hai, toh woh bada ise secret rakhne ka waada nahi kar sakta: POCSO Act ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke tahat jise bhi iski jaankari ho, uske liye police ko report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh baat saaf bata do, aur aage jo bhi ho usmein bachche ke saath khade raho.

Parents: result ke baad nahi, pehle hi apne bachche se kaho ki koi bhi mark ghar mein uski jagah nahi badalta.

## Agar tum mushkil mein ho: pehle kadam

Tele-MANAS 14416 pe free hai, din-raat chalta hai aur har us insaan ko counselling deta hai jise zaroorat ho [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Tumhe kisi diagnosis ki zaroorat nahi, na hi kisi aisi wajah ki jo sunne mein kaafi badi lage. Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh Child Helpline 1098 bhi tumhare liye hai. Emergency mein 112 pe call karo.

Aaj hi kisi ek insaan ko batao: koi dost, bhai-behen, ya koi teacher jis pe bharosa ho. "Main theek nahi hoon aur mujhe madad chahiye" kaafi hai.

Agar tum pehle hi apni jaan lene ki koshish kar chuke ho, toh tumhe iske liye saza nahi milegi. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 maanta hai ki suicide attempt karne wala insaan severe stress mein hai, aur sarkar ki zimmedari banata hai ki use care de [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Hospital jao, aur ho sake toh kisi ko saath le jao.

World Health Organization saaf kehta hai ki suicide roke ja sakte hain [[who-suicide]]. Exam dobara diya ja sakta hai, course badla ja sakta hai, hostel chhoda ja sakta hai. Raat ke do baje inmein se kuch bhi sach nahi lagta, aur isiliye pehla kadam har baar ek hi hai: kisi ko batao, aur use apne paas rukne do.

supriyo-same-sex-marriage-verdict-2023.en:
On 17 October 2023, a five-judge bench of the Supreme Court gave its verdict in *Supriyo v. Union of India*, the marriage-equality case. Queer couples had come to court asking to be recognised as families. They left with no right to marry, no right to a civil union, no right to adopt together, and the promise of a government committee. On two of those questions the margin was a single judge [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. This case file sets out what was asked, who held what, and what it means three years on.

## The petitions and the questions before the court

The verdict came five years after *Navtej Singh Johar*, in which the Supreme Court unanimously decriminalised consensual sex between adults of the same sex on 6 September 2018 [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Once queer relationships were no longer a crime, the next question was whether the state would recognise them. The petitions asked the court, chiefly, to let queer couples marry under India's existing marriage laws.

The bench was Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud and Justices S.K. Kaul, S.R. Bhat, Hima Kohli and P.S. Narasimha [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. It wrote four opinions: one each by the Chief Justice, Justice Kaul and Justice Narasimha, and one by Justice Bhat for himself and Justice Kohli.

## Unanimous: no fundamental right to marry

All five judges held that there is no fundamental right to marry [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. All five also declined to recognise same-sex marriage themselves. Whether queer couples can marry, they said, is for Parliament to decide.

The first holding is wider than it sounds. It is not a rule about queer people. It says the Constitution itself does not guarantee marriage to anyone; marriage rights come from laws that legislatures make. For a straight couple that changes nothing, because those laws already include them. For a queer couple it closes the door.

## Split 3:2: civil unions and adoption

On civil unions, the bench split. Chief Justice Chandrachud and Justice Kaul held that queer couples have a right to enter a union. Justices Bhat, Kohli and Narasimha held that no such right exists [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. The same 3:2 majority read the adoption rules as allowing joint adoption only by married couples, which shuts queer couples out.

| Question | Outcome | Vote |
|---|---|---|
| Is there a fundamental right to marry? | No | Unanimous |
| Will the court itself recognise same-sex marriage? | No, left to Parliament | Unanimous |
| Do queer couples have a right to a civil union? | No | 3:2 |
| Can queer couples adopt jointly? | No | 3:2 |
| Can a trans person in a heterosexual relationship marry? | Yes | Chief Justice, with Justice Bhat concurring |

On civil unions and adoption, one judge's vote was the whole distance between some recognition and none.

## What did change: transgender marriage and the committee

One door opened. The court held that a transgender person in a heterosexual relationship is entitled to marry under existing marriage laws [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. A trans woman and a man, or a trans man and a woman, can marry as any heterosexual couple can.

But the paperwork that records a trans person's gender in law has become harder to get. Since 25 May 2026, after an amendment to the transgender law, the right to a self-perceived gender identity has been deleted, and a District Magistrate issues a transgender certificate only after examining a medical board's recommendation [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. The amendment is under challenge in the Supreme Court.

The other change was a committee. During the hearing, the Solicitor General assured the court that the government would form one, and the judgment records that assurance. On 16 April 2024 the Centre set up a six-member committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary to recommend measures against discrimination, violence and involuntary medical treatment of queer persons [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. Its terms of reference do not mention legal recognition of couples. We could find no published report from it.

## After the review: where couples stand in 2026

On 9 January 2025, a five-judge bench headed by Justice B.R. Gavai dismissed the review petitions, finding no error apparent in the 2023 judgment [[barandbench-supriyo-review-dismissed-2025]]. The 2023 judgment stands. The route that remains is the one the court pointed to: Parliament. We could find no law recognising queer couples passed since.

Consider two women in Hyderabad who have lived together for eight years. In November 2026 they cannot marry each other under Indian law. They cannot register a civil union, because none exists. They cannot adopt a child together. In law they are two unrelated adults, and what protects them is what any two adults can arrange: wills, nominations on bank accounts and insurance, and documents that name each other.

This is general information, not legal advice. The judgment did not make anyone's relationship illegal. It decided that recognising it is not the court's job, and in the three years since, those whose job it is have not done it.
supriyo-same-sex-marriage-verdict-2023.hg:
17 October 2023 ko Supreme Court ki paanch judges ki bench ne *Supriyo v. Union of India*, yaani marriage-equality case, mein apna faisla sunaya. Queer couples court mein is ummeed se aaye the ki unhe family ke roop mein maana jaayega. Woh wapas gaye bina shaadi ke haq ke, bina civil union ke haq ke, bina saath mein adopt karne ke haq ke, aur haath mein bas ek sarkari committee ka vaada lekar. Inme se do sawaalon par faasla sirf ek judge ka tha [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. Yeh case file batati hai ki court se kya maanga gaya, kis judge ne kya kaha, aur teen saal baad iska matlab kya hai.

## Petitions aur court ke saamne sawaal

Yeh faisla *Navtej Singh Johar* ke paanch saal baad aaya, jisme 6 September 2018 ko Supreme Court ne unanimously same-sex adults ke beech consent wale sex ko decriminalise kiya tha [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Jab queer relationships crime nahi rahe, toh agla sawaal tha ki kya state unhe recognise karegi. Petitions mein court se khaas taur par yeh maanga gaya ki queer couples ko India ke maujooda marriage laws ke under shaadi karne diya jaaye.

Bench mein the Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud aur Justices S.K. Kaul, S.R. Bhat, Hima Kohli aur P.S. Narasimha [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. Chaar opinions likhe gaye: ek-ek Chief Justice, Justice Kaul aur Justice Narasimha ne, aur ek Justice Bhat ne apne aur Justice Kohli ki taraf se.

## Unanimous: shaadi ka koi fundamental right nahi

Paanchon judges ne kaha ki shaadi ka koi fundamental right nahi hai [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. Paanchon ne khud same-sex marriage ko recognise karne se bhi mana kiya. Unke hisaab se queer couples shaadi kar sakte hain ya nahi, yeh Parliament ko tay karna hai.

Pehla faisla jitna lagta hai usse bada hai. Yeh queer logon ke baare mein koi rule nahi hai. Yeh kehta hai ki Constitution khud kisi ko bhi shaadi ki guarantee nahi deta; shaadi ke haq un laws se aate hain jo legislatures banati hain. Straight couple ke liye isse kuch nahi badalta, kyunki woh laws unhe pehle se shaamil karte hain. Queer couple ke liye isse darwaaza band ho jaata hai.

## 3:2 ka split: civil unions aur adoption

Civil unions par bench bat gayi. Chief Justice Chandrachud aur Justice Kaul ne kaha ki queer couples ko union banane ka haq hai. Justices Bhat, Kohli aur Narasimha ne kaha ki aisa koi haq nahi hai [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. Usi 3:2 majority ne adoption rules ko aise padha ki joint adoption sirf married couples kar sakte hain, aur isse queer couples bahar ho gaye.

| Sawaal | Faisla | Vote |
|---|---|---|
| Kya shaadi ka fundamental right hai? | Nahi | Unanimous |
| Kya court khud same-sex marriage ko recognise karega? | Nahi, Parliament par chhoda | Unanimous |
| Kya queer couples ko civil union ka haq hai? | Nahi | 3:2 |
| Kya queer couples saath mein adopt kar sakte hain? | Nahi | 3:2 |
| Kya heterosexual relationship mein ek trans insaan shaadi kar sakta hai? | Haan | Chief Justice, Justice Bhat ki sahmati ke saath |

Civil unions aur adoption par, thodi recognition aur bilkul kuch nahi ke beech ka poora faasla ek judge ka vote tha.

## Kya badla: transgender marriage aur committee

Ek darwaaza khula. Court ne kaha ki heterosexual relationship mein ek transgender insaan ko maujooda marriage laws ke under shaadi karne ka haq hai [[scobserver-supriyo-judgment-summary-2023]]. Ek trans woman aur ek man, ya ek trans man aur ek woman, waise hi shaadi kar sakte hain jaise koi bhi heterosexual couple.

Lekin jo papers law mein ek trans insaan ka gender record karte hain, woh milna ab mushkil ho gaya hai. 25 May 2026 se, transgender law mein amendment ke baad, apni gender identity khud tay karne ka haq hata diya gaya hai, aur District Magistrate transgender certificate tabhi deta hai jab woh medical board ki recommendation dekh le [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Is amendment ko Supreme Court mein challenge kiya gaya hai.

Doosra badlav tha ek committee. Hearing ke dauraan Solicitor General ne court ko bharosa diya tha ki sarkar ek committee banayegi, aur judgment mein yeh assurance record hai. 16 April 2024 ko Centre ne Cabinet Secretary ki chairmanship mein chhe members ki committee banayi, jise queer logon ke saath discrimination, violence aur zabardasti medical treatment rokne ke upaay suggest karne the [[gazette-queer-committee-order-2024]]. Uske terms of reference mein couples ki legal recognition ka zikr hi nahi hai. Humein iski koi published report nahi mili.

## Review ke baad: 2026 mein couples kahan khade hain

9 January 2025 ko Justice B.R. Gavai ki adhyakshata wali paanch judges ki bench ne review petitions dismiss kar di, kyunki 2023 ke judgment mein koi galti saaf nazar nahi aayi [[barandbench-supriyo-review-dismissed-2025]]. 2023 ka judgment kaayam hai. Ab bacha raasta wahi hai jiski taraf court ne ishaara kiya tha: Parliament. Humein tab se queer couples ko recognise karne wala koi law pass hua nahi mila.

Socho, Hyderabad mein do auratein hain jo aath saal se saath reh rahi hain. November 2026 mein woh Indian law ke under ek-doosre se shaadi nahi kar sakti. Civil union register nahi kar sakti, kyunki aisa kuch hai hi nahi. Saath mein bachcha adopt nahi kar sakti. Law ki nazar mein woh do anjaan adults hain, aur unhe wahi protection milti hai jo koi bhi do adults khud arrange kar sakte hain: will, bank accounts aur insurance mein nomination, aur aise documents jinme ek-doosre ka naam ho.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Is judgment ne kisi ka relationship illegal nahi banaya. Isne bas yeh tay kiya ki use recognise karna court ka kaam nahi hai, aur teen saal mein jinka yeh kaam hai, unhone yeh nahi kiya.

teaching-consent-to-teenagers-guide.en:
Imagine a Class 9 classroom in Indore. A boy asks, half joking, whether girls "say no when they mean yes". The teacher can laugh along, change the subject, or answer. Too often, the subject changes.

The cost of that silence shows in police data. In 2024, in 96.6% of the POCSO penetrative sexual assault cases registered in India, 42,634 of 44,126, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. We have reported why "stranger danger" is the wrong lesson. This guide is about the right one: consent, taught by the adults children see every day, for parents and teachers of 13-to-17-year-olds.

## What the Supreme Court recommended in 2024

On 23 September 2024, ruling on child sexual abuse material, the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education that gives young people "a clear understanding of consent and the impact of exploitation". It also suggested the Union government set up an expert committee on health and sex education and POCSO awareness for children "from an early age" [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. These were suggestions, not binding orders.

Under the School Health and Wellness Programme, whose curriculum was launched on 12 February 2020, two teachers in every government and government-aided school are to be trained as Health and Wellness Ambassadors and teach 11 health themes, one hour a week for 24 weeks a year [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools are not covered. If your child's school skips that hour, the lesson falls to you.

## Does talking about consent make teenagers have sex? The evidence

This fear has been tested. The UN's 2018 guidance on sexuality education draws mainly on two evidence reviews: one of 87 studies, and a 2016 Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised trials. Its conclusion: sexuality education, in or out of school, does not increase sexual activity or sexual risk-taking [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Curriculum-based programmes are linked to later first sex, fewer partners and more condom and contraceptive use, while abstinence-only programmes do not delay first sex [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. After a 2007 backlash, states that banned or refused to run the school Adolescence Education Programme bet on the opposite fear; counts range from six to 12 states [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. The evidence does not back it.

The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse found that abuse reported by children gained momentum from age 10 and peaked at 12 to 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. In 2024, 16,801 child victims of POCSO penetrative assault were aged 12-16 and 23,497 were 16-18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], though NCRB does not separate teenage relationships from abuse in those counts. Thirteen is not too early. This is not only about daughters: boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse in the 2007 study [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Five consent conversations to have before 18

**1. A clear yes, freely given.** Consent is a clear yes that can be taken back at any time. Silence, "maybe" or a yes squeezed out by pressure is not a yes. This applies to a hug from an uncle as much as to a date.

**2. No secrets about bodies.** Grooming starts with trust: special attention to one child, gifts, playing the sympathetic listener, offers to help the family, contact through the internet [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Online, they often win the trust of the child or a parent before pushing for images [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. The rule to teach: anyone who asks you to keep a secret about your body or your photos is breaking the rules, not you.

**3. What 18 means in law.** Anyone under 18 is a child under POCSO, boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and since 2013 sex with a girl under 18 is rape whether or not she agreed [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Say it as information, not a threat: the law does not accept a "yes" from anyone under 18. (This guide gives general information, not legal advice.)

**4. Photos.** Creating, downloading or exchanging sexual images of anyone under 18 is a crime under Section 67B of the IT Act [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Forwarding a classmate's photo is not a joke. If a teenager's own image has leaked, Take It Down, a free and anonymous service available in Hindi, helps remove nude images taken before 18 [[ncmec-take-it-down]].

**5. Pressure.** "If you loved me, you would" is pressure, not romance. Teach the walk-away line: "If you have to push, the answer is no." Teach sons that hearing no is not an insult.

## Scripts for awkward moments at home and in class

- A student says girls "mean yes": "If you can't tell, you stop and ask. If she says no, that is the answer."
- A relative insists on a hug: "She can say namaste. Nobody has to hug anyone."
- You find something worrying on their phone: "I'm not angry with you. Tell me what happened, and we'll sort it out together."
- Your son asks why he must ask first: "Because her body is hers, the same way yours is yours."

What children see counts as much as what they hear. A 2014 ICRW-UNFPA study in seven states found that men raised in families where fathers did household chores were two times more likely to hold gender-equitable attitudes [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

## If a teenager tells you something happened

Stay calm. Believe them. Thank them for telling you. Do not ask why they went there or why they did not say no. Most never tell anyone: in the 2007 study, only 26.8% of young adults who had been sexually assaulted in childhood had ever told anyone [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Do not promise to keep it secret. Under POCSO Sections 19 and 21, any adult who knows of a child sexual offence must report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit. Failing to report can bring up to six months in jail, and heads of institutions who fail to report offences by their staff face up to one year [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. The duty does not apply to children. Say instead: "I can't keep this a secret, but I will be with you at every step."

Watch for changes. Behavioural signs, such as sleep problems, unusual fear of a person or sudden mood changes, are more common than physical ones [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Call the Child Helpline 1098, which is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], or visit an Adolescent Friendly Health Centre at a government health centre or district hospital for private counselling [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].
teaching-consent-to-teenagers-guide.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek Class 9. Ek ladka aadhe mazaak mein poochta hai, "Ladkiyan 'na' bolti hain par matlab 'haan' hota hai na?" Teacher ke paas teen raaste hain: saath mein hans dein, topic badal dein, ya jawab dein. Aksar topic badal diya jaata hai.

Is chuppi ki keemat police data mein dikhti hai. 2024 mein India mein POCSO ke penetrative sexual assault cases mein se 96.6% mein, yaani 44,126 mein se 42,634 cases mein, accused koi aisa tha jise bachcha jaanta tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Hum pehle bata chuke hain ki "stranger danger" wala lesson galat kyun hai. Yeh guide sahi lesson ke baare mein hai: consent, jo wahi bade sikhayein jinhein bachche roz dekhte hain. Yeh 13 se 17 saal ke bachchon ke parents aur teachers ke liye hai.

## 2024 mein Supreme Court ne kya suggest kiya

23 September 2024 ko, child sexual abuse material par ek faisle mein, Supreme Court ne comprehensive sex education ki recommendation di, jo young people ko "a clear understanding of consent and the impact of exploitation" de. Court ne yeh bhi suggest kiya ki Union government health aur sex education aur POCSO awareness par ek expert committee banaye, bachchon ke liye "from an early age" [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Yeh suggestions the, binding orders nahi.

School Health and Wellness Programme, jiska curriculum 12 February 2020 ko launch hua, ke under har government aur government-aided school ke do teachers ko Health and Wellness Ambassadors banaya jaana hai, jo saal mein 24 hafte, har hafte ek ghanta, 11 health themes padhayenge [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools ismein cover nahi hote. Agar tumhare bachche ka school yeh ghanta skip karta hai, toh yeh lesson tumhe dena hoga.

## Kya consent ki baat se teenagers sex karne lagte hain? Evidence kya kehta hai

Yeh darr test ho chuka hai. Sexuality education par UN ki 2018 guidance mainly do evidence reviews par tiki hai: ek 87 studies ka, aur ek 2016 ka Oxford review jismein 22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised trials the. Guidance ka conclusion: sexuality education, school mein ho ya bahar, sexual activity ya sexual risk-taking nahi badhati [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Curriculum-based programmes se pehla sex der se hone, kam partners aur zyada condom aur contraception use mein madad milti hai, jabki abstinence-only programmes pehle sex ko delay nahi kar paate [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. 2007 ke backlash ke baad jin states ne school ka Adolescence Education Programme ban kiya ya chalane se mana kiya, unhone isi ulte darr par daav lagaya tha; alag-alag counts mein yeh sankhya 6 se 12 states tak hai [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Evidence us darr ko support nahi karta.

Timing bhi matter karti hai. Sarkar ki 2007 Study on Child Abuse mein bachchon ne jo abuse bataya, woh 10 saal ki umar se tezi pakadta hai aur 12 se 15 saal mein peak par hota hai [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. 2024 mein POCSO penetrative assault cases mein 16,801 bachche 12-16 saal ke the aur 23,497 bachche 16-18 saal ke [[ncrb-cii-2024]], halanki NCRB in counts mein teenage relationships aur abuse ko alag nahi karta. 13 saal jaldi nahi hai. Aur yeh sirf betiyon ki baat nahi: 2007 study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## 18 se pehle paanch consent conversations

**1. Saaf haan, apni marzi se.** Consent ek saaf haan hai jo kabhi bhi wapas li ja sakti hai. Chuppi, "shayad" ya pressure se nikalwayi gayi haan, haan nahi hai. Yeh baat kisi uncle ke hug par bhi utni hi laagu hoti hai jitni kisi date par.

**2. Body ke baare mein koi secret nahi.** Grooming trust se shuru hoti hai: kisi ek bachche par khaas attention, gifts, sympathetic listener banna, family ki madad offer karna, internet se contact [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Online bhi abusers aksar pehle bachche ya parent ka trust jeette hain, phir images maangte hain [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Yeh rule sikhao: jo bhi tumse tumhari body ya photos ke baare mein secret rakhne ko kahe, galti uski hai, tumhari nahi.

**3. Law mein 18 ka matlab.** POCSO mein 18 se kam umar ka har insaan child hai, ladka ho ya ladki [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur 2013 se 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex rape hai, chahe usne haan kaha ho ya nahi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Ise dhamki ki tarah nahi, information ki tarah batao: 18 se kam umar ke kisi ki "haan" law nahi maanta. (Yeh guide general information hai, legal advice nahi.)

**4. Photos.** 18 se kam umar ke kisi ki sexual images banana, download karna ya exchange karna IT Act ke Section 67B ke under crime hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Kisi classmate ki photo forward karna mazaak nahi hai. Agar kisi teenager ki apni image leak ho gayi hai, toh Take It Down, ek free aur anonymous service jo Hindi mein bhi hai, 18 se pehle li gayi nude images hatwane mein madad karti hai [[ncmec-take-it-down]].

**5. Pressure.** "Agar mujhse pyaar hai toh maan jao" pressure hai, romance nahi. Walk-away line sikhao: "Agar push karna pade, toh jawab na hi hai." Beton ko sikhao ki na sunna insult nahi hai.

## Ghar aur class ke awkward moments ke liye scripts

- Koi student kahe ki ladkiyon ki na ka "matlab haan" hota hai: "Agar samajh na aaye, toh ruko aur poocho. Agar usne na kaha, toh wahi jawab hai."
- Koi relative hug ki zid kare: "Woh namaste kar sakti hai. Kisi ko bhi hug karna zaroori nahi."
- Bachche ke phone mein kuch pareshaan karne wala dikhe: "Main tumse naraz nahi hoon. Batao kya hua, hum milkar sort kar lenge."
- Beta pooche ki pehle poochna kyun zaroori hai: "Kyunki uski body uski hai, jaise tumhari body tumhari hai."

Bachche jo dekhte hain, uska asar utna hi hota hai jitna jo sunte hain uska. Saat states mein 2014 ki ICRW-UNFPA study ne paaya ki jin aadmiyon ke papa ghar ke kaam karte the, unmein gender-equitable soch hone ke chances do guna the [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

## Agar koi teenager bataye ki uske saath kuch hua

Shaant raho. Bharosa karo. Batane ke liye thank you bolo. Yeh mat poocho ki "wahan gaye kyun the" ya "na kyun nahi kaha". Zyada tar log kabhi kisi ko nahi batate: 2007 study mein bachpan mein sexual assault jhel chuke young adults mein se sirf 26.8% ne kabhi kisi ko bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Secret rakhne ka promise mat karo. POCSO Sections 19 aur 21 ke under, jis bhi adult ko bachche ke saath sexual offence ki jaankari hai, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko report karna zaroori hai. Report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ho sakti hai, aur jo institution heads apne staff ke offences report nahi karte, unhe 1 saal tak [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Yeh duty bachchon par laagu nahi hoti. Iske bajaye kaho: "Yeh baat secret nahi rahegi, par har step par main tumhare saath hoon."

Badlaavon par nazar rakho. Behaviour ke signs, jaise neend ki problem, kisi khaas insaan se ajeeb darr ya achanak mood swings, physical signs se zyada common hain [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Child Helpline 1098 par call karo, jo 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], ya kisi government health centre ya district hospital ke Adolescent Friendly Health Centre jao, jahan private counselling milti hai [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

transgender-amendment-act-2026-explained.en:
On 15 April 2014, in NALSA v. Union of India, the Supreme Court recognised transgender persons as a "third gender" and upheld their right to self-identify their gender [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Parliament later wrote that idea into Section 4(2) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, which gave every person recognised as transgender "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. In March 2026 Parliament deleted that sub-section. Who counts as transgender now runs through a medical board. This explainer goes through the amendment clause by clause. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Twelve days in March: how the amendment passed

The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, a bill of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 13 March 2026. The Lok Sabha passed it on 24 March and the Rajya Sabha on 25 March, within 12 days of its introduction [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]].

The President gave assent on 30 March 2026, making it Act No. 3 of 2026. The Gazette text said the Act would start on a date the Centre notified, and a petition before the Supreme Court cites the notification that brought it into force from 25 May 2026 [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Compare the pace. The right took a Supreme Court judgment in 2014 and then a law that came into force only on 10 January 2020 [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Removing it took less than a fortnight of Parliament's time.

## Clause by clause: self-identification, medical boards, punishments

**The right to self-identify is deleted.** The amendment omits Section 4(2) of the 2019 Act, the sub-section on self-perceived gender identity [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Nothing is put in its place.

**A medical board enters.** A new clause defines an "authority": a medical board headed by a Chief Medical Officer or a Deputy Chief Medical Officer. The District Magistrate still issues the transgender certificate, but now only "after examining the recommendation of the authority" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Under NALSA the starting point was what a person says about themselves. Now it is what a board recommends about them.

**The punishments are rewritten.** A new offence, kidnapping an adult and causing grievous hurt to force them to assume a transgender identity, carries rigorous imprisonment of 10 years to life. Sexual abuse of a transgender person stays at six months to two years, the same range as in 2019 [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Our investigation into that punishment gap covers it in detail.

## Who is in and who is out

The fourth change is the definition itself. A "transgender person" now means a person with "such socio-cultural identities as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta, or eunuch" (the Act's own word), a person with intersex variations, or a person forced to assume a transgender identity [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

It ends with a proviso. The term "shall not include, nor shall ever have been so included, persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. PRS Legislative Research notes that trans men, trans women and genderqueer persons, all named in the 2019 definition, are dropped [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]].

> The law now recognises a transgender person through a community, a body or a crime done to them. It no longer starts from their own word.

Consider a hypothetical. A 23-year-old trans man in Indore works at a courier office. He has never lived in a hijra household and has no intersex variation. The 2019 Act named people like him. The 2026 text does not, and the proviso points away from him. Whether a medical board and a District Magistrate would still certify him is not something the text answers, and there is no verified data yet on how boards are deciding.

## What happens to certificates already issued

Certificates and identity cards have been issued online through the National Portal for Transgender Persons since 25 November 2020 [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. A petition filed in the Supreme Court on 15 June 2026 cites ministry data showing that 33,189 certificates had been issued nationwide, about 7% of the Census 2011 count [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. That census counted 4,87,803 people in the "other" gender category, a figure widely seen as an undercount [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

For these cardholders there is an answer, for now. On 17 August 2026 a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana recorded the Union government's statement that identity cards issued before the Amendment Act will continue to operate, subject to the outcome of the case [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

Read that carefully. It covers cards already issued, it lasts while the case is pending, and it depends on how the case ends. As reported, it is not a promise about new applications, which are decided under the amended law.

## The Supreme Court challenge

The petitions before the court include those of Akkai Padmashali and Kalki Subramaniam. At the 17 August hearing the court asked the Union to file a reply and listed the matter after four weeks. As of November 2026, no later hearing report had appeared on the Supreme Court Observer's case page [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

The question is easy to state. In NALSA the court upheld self-identification and extended to transgender persons the protection of Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 and 21 of the Constitution [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Parliament has now written the opposite test into the statute. The court has to decide whether a medical board's recommendation can replace a right it upheld twelve years ago.

Until it rules, three things are true at once: the amendment is in force, old cards work, and the definition that decides new applications is under challenge. If this affects you, keep your documents safe and get advice before you apply. Free legal aid is available through the legal services authorities [[nalsa]]. Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline on 14416, offers counselling to anyone, including transgender persons [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
transgender-amendment-act-2026-explained.hg:
15 April 2014 ko NALSA v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne transgender persons ko "third gender" maana aur unka yeh right upheld kiya ki woh apna gender khud identify karein [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Baad mein Parliament ne yahi baat Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 ke Section 4(2) mein likhi, jo transgender ke roop mein recognised har insaan ko "a right to self-perceived gender identity" deta tha [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. March 2026 mein Parliament ne yeh sub-section hata diya. Ab kaun transgender maana jaayega, yeh sawaal ek medical board se hokar guzarta hai. Yeh explainer amendment ko clause by clause samjhata hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## March ke baarah din: amendment kaise pass hua

Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, jo Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment ka bill tha, 13 March 2026 ko Lok Sabha mein introduce hua. Lok Sabha ne ise 24 March ko pass kiya aur Rajya Sabha ne 25 March ko, yaani introduce hone ke 12 din ke andar [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]].

President ne 30 March 2026 ko assent diya, aur yeh Act No. 3 of 2026 ban gaya. Gazette text mein likha tha ki Act us date se shuru hoga jo Centre notify karega, aur Supreme Court ke saamne ek petition us notification ko cite karti hai jisne ise 25 May 2026 se lagu kiya [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Ab raftaar compare kijiye. Is right ko paane mein 2014 ka ek Supreme Court judgment laga, aur phir ek law jo 10 January 2020 ko jaakar lagu hua [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Ise hatane mein Parliament ke do hafte bhi nahi lage.

## Clause by clause: self-identification, medical board, punishments

**Self-identify karne ka right delete ho gaya.** Amendment 2019 Act ka Section 4(2) hata deta hai, yaani self-perceived gender identity wala sub-section [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Uski jagah kuch nahi rakha gaya.

**Medical board ki entry.** Ek naya clause "authority" ko define karta hai: ek medical board, jiska head Chief Medical Officer ya Deputy Chief Medical Officer hoga. Transgender certificate ab bhi District Magistrate hi issue karta hai, lekin ab sirf "after examining the recommendation of the authority" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. NALSA ke hisaab se shuruaat is baat se hoti thi ki insaan apne baare mein khud kya kehta hai. Ab shuruaat is baat se hoti hai ki board uske baare mein kya recommend karta hai.

**Punishments bhi dobara likhi gayi hain.** Ek naya offence aaya hai: kisi adult ko kidnap karke aur grievous hurt pahunchakar use transgender identity apnane par majboor karna, jiski saza 10 saal se life tak ki rigorous imprisonment hai. Transgender insaan ke sexual abuse ki saza chhe mahine se do saal par hi rahi, wahi range jo 2019 mein thi [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Is punishment gap par hamari investigation ise detail mein dekhti hai.

## Kaun andar hai aur kaun bahar

Chautha change khud definition hai. Ab "transgender person" ka matlab hai aisa insaan jiski "such socio-cultural identities as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta, or eunuch" ho (yeh Act ka apna shabd hai), intersex variations wala insaan, ya woh insaan jise transgender identity apnane par majboor kiya gaya ho [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Definition ek proviso par khatam hoti hai. Yeh term "shall not include, nor shall ever have been so included, persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. PRS Legislative Research note karta hai ki trans men, trans women aur genderqueer persons, jo 2019 ki definition mein naam se the, ab hata diye gaye hain [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]].

> Law ab transgender insaan ko ek community, ek body ya uske saath hue ek crime ke zariye pehchaanta hai. Uski apni baat se shuruaat ab nahi hoti.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Indore ka ek 23 saal ka trans man courier office mein kaam karta hai. Woh kabhi kisi hijra household mein nahi raha aur uski koi intersex variation nahi hai. 2019 ka Act uske jaise logon ka naam leta tha. 2026 ka text nahi leta, aur proviso use bahar ki taraf dhakelta hai. Koi medical board aur District Magistrate use phir bhi certify karenge ya nahi, iska jawab text nahi deta, aur boards kaise decide kar rahe hain is par abhi koi verified data nahi hai.

## Jo certificates pehle se issue ho chuke hain, unka kya hoga

Certificates aur identity cards 25 November 2020 se National Portal for Transgender Persons ke zariye online issue ho rahe hain [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. 15 June 2026 ko Supreme Court mein file hui ek petition ministry data cite karti hai, jiske hisaab se desh bhar mein 33,189 certificates issue hue the, yaani Census 2011 ke count ka kareeb 7% [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. Us census ne "other" gender category mein 4,87,803 log gine the, aur is figure ko aam taur par undercount maana jaata hai [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

In cardholders ke liye filhaal ek jawab hai. 17 August 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur V. Mohana ki bench ne Union government ka yeh statement record kiya ki Amendment Act se pehle issue hue identity cards chalte rahenge, aur yeh case ke outcome par depend karega [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

Ise dhyan se padhiye. Yeh pehle se issue hue cards ko cover karta hai, tab tak chalta hai jab tak case pending hai, aur is par depend karta hai ki case kaise khatam hota hai. Jaisa report hua hai, yeh nayi applications ke baare mein koi promise nahi hai; woh amended law ke tahat decide hoti hain.

## Supreme Court mein challenge

Court ke saamne jo petitions hain, unme Akkai Padmashali aur Kalki Subramaniam ki petitions shamil hain. 17 August ki hearing mein court ne Union se reply file karne ko kaha aur matter chaar hafte baad list kiya. November 2026 tak Supreme Court Observer ke case page par iske baad ki koi hearing report nahi aayi thi [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

Sawaal seedha hai. NALSA mein court ne self-identification ko upheld kiya tha aur transgender persons ko Constitution ke Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 aur 21 ki protection di thi [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Parliament ne ab statute mein iska ulta test likh diya hai. Court ko decide karna hai ki kya ek medical board ki recommendation us right ki jagah le sakti hai jise usne baarah saal pehle upheld kiya tha.

Jab tak court faisla nahi deta, teen baatein ek saath sach hain: amendment lagu hai, purane cards chal rahe hain, aur jo definition nayi applications decide karti hai woh khud challenge mein hai. Agar yeh aap par asar daalta hai, toh apne documents sambhal kar rakhiye aur apply karne se pehle advice lijiye. Free legal aid legal services authorities ke zariye milti hai [[nalsa]]. Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free, 24x7 helpline, 14416 par kisi ko bhi counselling deti hai, transgender persons ko bhi [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

transgender-certificates-paperwork-wall.en:
On paper, the route is short. Since 25 November 2020 a transgender person in India has been able to apply online, through the National Portal for Transgender Persons, for a certificate and an identity card [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. By June 2026, according to ministry data cited in a writ petition before the Supreme Court, only 33,189 certificates had been issued in the whole country [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. Census 2011 counted 4,87,803 people in its "other" gender category [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. That is about 7 certificates for every 100 people.

## What the certificate is for

On 15 April 2014, in NALSA v. Union of India, the Supreme Court recognised transgender persons as a "third gender" and upheld their right to self-identify their gender [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, in force from 10 January 2020, turned that right into a procedure: an application, and a certificate issued by the District Magistrate. Section 4(2) of the Act gave every person recognised as transgender "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

The certificate is the state's written acknowledgement of who a person is, and it is what the next desk asks for. Consider a hypothetical: a 22-year-old trans woman in a district town in Maharashtra, whose school marksheets and bank account carry a name and gender she no longer uses. A college form, a landlord, a hospital registration counter: each wants a document that matches the person standing there. Without the certificate she explains herself from the beginning at every counter. With it, she has one paper that says the state already knows.

So the count measures something simple: how many people have been able to turn a right from a judgment into a paper they can carry.

## 24,015, then 33,189: the count since 2020

The Rules under the Act were notified on 25 September 2020, and the portal was launched two months later [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. By December 2024 it had issued 24,015 certificates, about 5% of the Census figure, according to an annexure to a Parliament reply. The same annexure said the portal had drawn more than 62 lakh visitors [[pib-mosje-transgender-parliament-reply-2024]]. Visitors are not applicants, but the distance between those two numbers is hard to miss.

By June 2026 the figure was 33,189, about 7% [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. A caution: we quote it from the petition, filed on 15 June 2026, which cites a ministry release. We could not locate the release itself.

Read together, the two figures show the counter moving by about nine thousand certificates in a year and a half. After about five and a half years of the portal, coverage stands at roughly 7 in 100.

Refused applications are part of this story too. We could not confirm a national count of rejections against a second source, so we give no figure here.

## Why the 2011 count is too low

The 7% rests on a weak denominator, and the weakness runs mostly one way. Census 2011 did not specifically enumerate transgender persons. It offered an "other" option, 4,87,803 people chose it, and the government still uses that figure as the transgender population [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Many transgender people recorded themselves as male or female, which is why the figure is widely seen as an undercount. "Other" also took in anyone who chose it, not only transgender persons. And the count is fifteen years old.

If the real population is larger than 4.87 lakh, the real share holding a certificate is smaller than 7%.

## The offices that were promised

The certificate is not the only promise running late. The 2020 Rules required every state to set up a Transgender Protection Cell. By November 2025 only 20 of India's 36 states and union territories had done so, and 25 had set up Transgender Welfare Boards [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Shelter is thinner still. In November 2025 there were 21 Garima Greh shelter homes for destitute transgender persons, across 17 states [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. In August 2025, 429 people were living in the shelters the ministry then supported [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

A person stuck at the application stage is, in many states, stuck alone.

## What changes when a medical board takes over

In March 2026 Parliament passed an amendment to the Act within 12 days of its introduction [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. In force since 25 May 2026, it omits Section 4(2), the right to self-perceived gender identity. A District Magistrate now issues a certificate only after examining the recommendation of an "authority": a medical board headed by a Chief Medical Officer or Deputy Chief Medical Officer [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Under self-identification, the system reached about 7 in 100. The amendment adds a step, and the step is a panel of doctors. NALSA's principle was that a person names their own gender; the new route asks doctors to recommend it first. What a board will examine, and how long it will take, can be judged only once boards are working. But an extra gate has rarely made a queue shorter.

The amendment is under challenge. On 17 August 2026 a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant heard the petitions, and the Union told the court that identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act would continue to operate while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

This is general information, not legal advice. If you hold a certificate or card, keep the original and copies safe. If you are applying, keep a record of every step: application number, dates, each reply. Free legal aid is available through legal services authorities [[nalsa]]. And if the wait is wearing you down, Tele-MANAS offers free counselling to anyone, including transgender persons, on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
transgender-certificates-paperwork-wall.hg:
Kaagaz par raasta chhota hai. 25 November 2020 se India mein koi bhi transgender insaan National Portal for Transgender Persons par online apply karke certificate aur identity card le sakta hai [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. June 2026 tak, Supreme Court mein file hui ek writ petition mein cite kiye gaye ministry data ke hisaab se, poore desh mein sirf 33,189 certificates issue hue the [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. Census 2011 ne apni "other" gender category mein 4,87,803 log gine the [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Yaani har 100 logon par kareeb 7 certificates.

## Certificate kis kaam ka hai

15 April 2014 ko NALSA v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne transgender persons ko "third gender" maana aur apna gender khud identify karne ka unka right upheld kiya [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, jo 10 January 2020 se lagu hai, ne is right ko ek procedure mein badal diya: ek application, aur District Magistrate ka issue kiya hua certificate. Act ke Section 4(2) ne transgender maane gaye har insaan ko "a right to self-perceived gender identity" diya [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]].

Certificate state ki likhit acknowledgement hai ki yeh insaan kaun hai, aur agla counter yahi maangta hai. Ek hypothetical lijiye: Maharashtra ke ek district town ki 22 saal ki trans woman, jiski school marksheets aur bank account par woh naam aur gender likha hai jo woh ab use nahi karti. College ka form, makaan-malik, hospital ka registration counter: har koi aisa document chahta hai jo saamne khade insaan se match kare. Certificate ke bina woh har counter par apni baat shuru se samjhati hai. Certificate ho, toh uske paas ek kaagaz hai jo kehta hai ki state pehle se jaanta hai.

Isliye yeh ginti ek seedhi cheez naapti hai: kitne log ek judgment se mile right ko aise kaagaz mein badal paaye jo woh saath lekar chal sakein.

## 24,015, phir 33,189: 2020 se ab tak ki ginti

Act ke Rules 25 September 2020 ko notify hue, aur portal do mahine baad launch hua [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Parliament ke ek reply ke annexure ke hisaab se, December 2024 tak portal ne 24,015 certificates issue kiye the, Census figure ka kareeb 5%. Usi annexure mein likha tha ki portal par 62 lakh se zyada visitors aa chuke hain [[pib-mosje-transgender-parliament-reply-2024]]. Visitors applicants nahi hote, lekin in do numbers ke beech ka fasla nazar-andaaz karna mushkil hai.

June 2026 tak yeh figure 33,189 tha, kareeb 7% [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]]. Ek caution: hum yeh number us petition se le rahe hain jo 15 June 2026 ko file hui aur jo ministry ki ek release cite karti hai. Woh release khud hamein nahi mili.

Dono figures saath padhiye toh counter dedh saal mein kareeb nau hazaar certificates aage badha. Portal ke kareeb saadhe paanch saal baad coverage lagbhag 100 mein 7 par hai.

Refuse hui applications bhi is kahani ka hissa hain. Rejections ki national ginti ko hum kisi doosre source se confirm nahi kar paaye, isliye yahan koi figure nahi de rahe.

## 2011 ki ginti kam kyun hai

Yeh 7% ek kamzor denominator par tika hai, aur kamzori zyada tar ek hi taraf jaati hai. Census 2011 ne transgender persons ko alag se nahi gina tha. Usne "other" ka option diya, 4,87,803 logon ne use chuna, aur sarkar aaj bhi isi figure ko transgender population maanti hai [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Kai transgender logon ne khud ko male ya female likhwaya, isi wajah se is figure ko aam taur par undercount maana jaata hai. "Other" mein woh sab bhi aaye jinhone yeh option chuna, sirf transgender persons nahi. Aur yeh ginti pandrah saal purani hai.

Agar asli population 4.87 lakh se badi hai, toh certificate rakhne walon ka asli share 7% se chhota hai.

## Woh daftar jinka vaada hua tha

Der se chal raha vaada sirf certificate ka nahi hai. 2020 ke Rules ke hisaab se har state ko ek Transgender Protection Cell banana tha. November 2025 tak India ke 36 states aur union territories mein se sirf 20 ne aisa kiya tha, aur 25 ne Transgender Welfare Boards banaye the [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

Shelter ka haal aur patla hai. November 2025 mein destitute transgender persons ke liye 21 Garima Greh shelter homes the, 17 states mein [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. August 2025 mein, ministry jin shelters ko tab support kar rahi thi, unme 429 log reh rahe the [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Jo insaan application ke stage par atka hai, woh kai states mein akela atka hai.

## Medical board ke aane se kya badalta hai

March 2026 mein Parliament ne is Act ka ek amendment introduce hone ke 12 din ke andar pass kar diya [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. 25 May 2026 se lagu yeh amendment Section 4(2) ko, yaani self-perceived gender identity ke right ko, hata deta hai. Ab District Magistrate certificate tabhi issue karta hai jab woh ek "authority" ki recommendation examine kar le: ek medical board, jiska head Chief Medical Officer ya Deputy Chief Medical Officer hota hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Self-identification ke rehte system 100 mein kareeb 7 tak pahuncha. Amendment ek step aur jodta hai, aur woh step doctors ka ek panel hai. NALSA ka principle tha ki insaan apna gender khud batata hai; naya raasta kehta hai ki pehle doctors recommend karein. Board kya examine karega aur kitna time lega, yeh tabhi pata chalega jab boards kaam karne lagenge. Lekin ek extra gate ne shayad hi kabhi koi line chhoti ki ho.

Amendment ko challenge kiya gaya hai. 17 August 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ki lead wali Supreme Court bench ne petitions suni, aur Union ne court ko bataya ki 2019 Act ke tahat pehle se issue hue identity cards case pending rehne tak chalte rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar aapke paas certificate ya card hai, toh original aur copies sambhaal kar rakhiye. Agar aap apply kar rahe hain, toh har step ka record rakhiye: application number, dates, har reply. Legal services authorities se free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]]. Aur agar yeh intezaar aapko thaka raha hai, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 par kisi ko bhi, transgender persons ko bhi, free counselling deta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

transgender-id-after-2026-amendment-ques.en:
Since 25 May 2026, India's transgender law no longer carries a right to self-perceived gender identity, and a new certificate needs a medical board's recommendation [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. If you hold a card, or need one, your questions are practical. These are ten of them, answered with what can be verified and marked clearly where it cannot. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Certificates and cards already issued: what the Union promised

**1. I already have a transgender certificate and ID card. Are they still valid?**

Yes, for now. On 17 August 2026, hearing challenges to the amendment, a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant recorded the Union government's statement that identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act will continue to operate while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

**2. Is that permanent?**

No. The assurance is tied to the case: it holds while the challenge is pending and depends on how it ends. The court asked the Union to file a reply and listed the matter after four weeks. As of November 2026, no later hearing report had appeared on the Supreme Court Observer's case page [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. If a bank, college or office says your card is "cancelled", that is not what the Union told the court.

## Applying now: the amendment is already in force

**3. Has the new law actually started?**

Yes. The President gave assent on 30 March 2026. The Act said it would begin on a date the Centre notified, and a petition before the Supreme Court cites the notification that brought it into force from 25 May 2026 [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. An application made today is decided under the amended law.

**4. I never applied. Should I apply now or wait for the court?**

Nobody can honestly answer that for you. The Union's assurance, as reported, covers cards already issued; we have no verified information that it protects an application made today. The court has not ruled, and there is no date for a ruling that we can verify. If your application would rest on self-identification alone, get advice before you file. Free legal aid is available through the legal services authorities [[nalsa]].

## Medical boards: what the law says they do

**5. Who decides my application now?**

The District Magistrate still issues the certificate, but only after examining the recommendation of an "authority": a medical board headed by a Chief Medical Officer or a Deputy Chief Medical Officer. Section 4(2), which guaranteed the right to self-perceived gender identity, has been deleted [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. In 2014 the Supreme Court had upheld the right to self-identify gender in NALSA v. Union of India [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. That reversal is the heart of the court challenge.

**6. What will the board do? Will I be physically examined?**

We do not know, and we will not guess. What is verified is who heads the board and that the District Magistrate must examine its recommendation. What we could not verify is what a board will ask, which documents it wants, or how it will assess a person. Before any appointment, ask the District Magistrate's office in writing what the procedure is, and take someone you trust if you can.

## Rejected? Who is at risk and what to do next

**7. Who is most likely to be refused?**

Look at the new definition. It covers people with socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta, eunuchs (the Act's own word), intersex persons and people forced into a transgender identity. It says the term does not include "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. PRS Legislative Research notes that trans men, trans women and genderqueer persons, named in the 2019 definition, are dropped [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. A trans man or trans woman outside those communities is the applicant the text no longer names. How boards will treat such applications in practice is not yet known.

**8. My application was rejected. What now?**

We have no verified national figure for rejections, or for the reasons behind them, that we can print. So work on your own case. Ask for the decision and the reason in writing. Find out whether the problem is a document you can correct or the definition itself. Keep every receipt and screenshot from the National Portal, which issues certificates and identity cards online [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Then take the papers to a legal aid lawyer [[nalsa]].

If you have no certificate, you are far from alone. Ministry data cited in a Supreme Court petition filed in June 2026 shows only 33,189 certificates issued nationwide, about 7% of the Census 2011 count [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]].

## Shelters, protection cells and help if you are in danger

**9. My family has thrown me out. Where can I go?**

The government's shelter homes for destitute transgender persons are called Garima Greh, run under the SMILE scheme. As of November 2025 there were 21, in 17 states [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]], so fewer than half of India's 36 states and union territories had one. In August 2025, 429 people were living in the shelters the ministry supported [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Call before you travel, and ask what documents the shelter needs.

**10. Someone is threatening or hurting me. Who do I call?**

In immediate danger, call 112 [[mha-erss]]. Any police station must record information about a cognizable offence wherever it happened (a Zero FIR) and give you a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The 2020 rules required every state to set up a Transgender Protection Cell, but by November 2025 only 20 states and union territories had one [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Ask whether yours does.

If the fear and the paperwork are wearing you down, Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline on 14416, offers counselling to anyone, including transgender persons [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. A card is paperwork. Whether the law can take your own word out of that paperwork is now for the Supreme Court to decide.
transgender-id-after-2026-amendment-ques.hg:
25 May 2026 se India ke transgender law mein self-perceived gender identity ka right nahi raha, aur naye certificate ke liye ab ek medical board ki recommendation chahiye [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Agar aapke paas card hai, ya aapko card chahiye, toh aapke sawaal practical hain. Yeh aise hi dus sawaal hain. Jawab mein wahi hai jo verify ho sakta hai, aur jahan verify nahi ho saka wahan saaf likha hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Pehle se issue hue certificates aur cards: Union ne kya promise kiya

**1. Mere paas pehle se transgender certificate aur ID card hai. Kya woh abhi bhi valid hain?**

Haan, filhaal. 17 August 2026 ko amendment ke khilaaf challenges sunte hue, Chief Justice Surya Kant ki lead wali Supreme Court bench ne Union government ka yeh statement record kiya ki 2019 Act ke tahat pehle se issue hue identity cards case pending rehne tak chalte rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

**2. Kya yeh permanent hai?**

Nahi. Yeh assurance case se juda hai: jab tak challenge pending hai tab tak hai, aur is par depend karta hai ki case kaise khatam hota hai. Court ne Union se reply file karne ko kaha aur matter chaar hafte baad list kiya. November 2026 tak Supreme Court Observer ke case page par iske baad ki koi hearing report nahi aayi thi [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. Agar koi bank, college ya office kahe ki aapka card "cancel" ho gaya hai, toh Union ne court ko yeh nahi kaha hai.

## Abhi apply karna: amendment pehle se lagu hai

**3. Kya naya law sach mein shuru ho chuka hai?**

Haan. President ne 30 March 2026 ko assent diya. Act mein likha tha ki woh us date se shuru hoga jo Centre notify karega, aur Supreme Court ke saamne ek petition us notification ko cite karti hai jisne ise 25 May 2026 se lagu kiya [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Aaj ki gayi application amended law ke tahat decide hogi.

**4. Maine kabhi apply nahi kiya. Abhi apply karun ya court ka wait karun?**

Iska imaandaar jawab aapke liye koi nahi de sakta. Union ka assurance, jaisa report hua hai, pehle se issue hue cards ko cover karta hai; hamare paas koi verified information nahi hai ki woh aaj ki gayi application ko bhi protect karta hai. Court ne abhi faisla nahi diya hai, aur faisle ki koi aisi date nahi hai jo hum verify kar sakein. Agar aapki application sirf self-identification par tiki hogi, toh file karne se pehle advice lijiye. Free legal aid legal services authorities ke zariye milti hai [[nalsa]].

## Medical boards: law ke hisaab se woh kya karte hain

**5. Ab meri application kaun decide karta hai?**

Certificate ab bhi District Magistrate hi issue karta hai, lekin sirf ek "authority" ki recommendation examine karne ke baad: yeh ek medical board hai jiska head Chief Medical Officer ya Deputy Chief Medical Officer hota hai. Section 4(2), jo self-perceived gender identity ka right guarantee karta tha, delete kar diya gaya hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. 2014 mein Supreme Court ne NALSA v. Union of India mein apna gender khud identify karne ka right upheld kiya tha [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Yahi palatna court challenge ka asli mudda hai.

**6. Board kya karega? Kya mera physical examination hoga?**

Hume nahi pata, aur hum andaza nahi lagayenge. Jo verified hai woh yeh hai ki board ka head kaun hota hai aur District Magistrate ko uski recommendation examine karni hoti hai. Jo hum verify nahi kar sake woh yeh hai ki board kya poochhega, kaunse documents maangega, ya kisi insaan ko kaise assess karega. Kisi bhi appointment se pehle District Magistrate ke office se likhit mein poochhiye ki procedure kya hai, aur ho sake toh kisi bharosemand insaan ko saath le jaiye.

## Application reject ho gayi? Kise risk hai aur aage kya karein

**7. Sabse zyada kiske refuse hone ka chance hai?**

Nayi definition dekhiye. Isme woh log aate hain jinki socio-cultural identities kinner, hijra, aravani aur jogta jaisi hain, eunuchs (yeh Act ka apna shabd hai), intersex persons aur woh log jinhe transgender identity apnane par majboor kiya gaya. Definition kehti hai ki is term mein "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" shamil nahi hain [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. PRS Legislative Research note karta hai ki trans men, trans women aur genderqueer persons, jo 2019 ki definition mein naam se the, ab hata diye gaye hain [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. In communities ke bahar ka trans man ya trans woman woh applicant hai jiska naam text ab nahi leta. Boards aisi applications ke saath practice mein kya karenge, yeh abhi pata nahi hai.

**8. Meri application reject ho gayi. Ab kya?**

Rejections ka, ya unki wajahon ka, koi verified national figure hamare paas nahi hai jo hum chhaap sakein. Isliye apne case par kaam kijiye. Decision aur uski wajah likhit mein maangiye. Pata kijiye ki problem koi document hai jo aap theek kar sakte hain, ya khud definition hai. National Portal, jo certificates aur identity cards online issue karta hai, uski har receipt aur screenshot sambhal kar rakhiye [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Phir yeh papers legal aid lawyer ke paas le jaiye [[nalsa]].

Agar aapke paas certificate nahi hai, toh aap bilkul akele nahi hain. June 2026 mein file hui ek Supreme Court petition mein cite kiya gaya ministry data dikhata hai ki desh bhar mein sirf 33,189 certificates issue hue, yaani Census 2011 ke count ka kareeb 7% [[sc-kalki-subramaniam-petition-2026]].

## Shelters, protection cells aur khatre mein madad

**9. Family ne mujhe ghar se nikaal diya hai. Ab main kahan jaun?**

Destitute transgender persons ke liye sarkar ke shelter homes ko Garima Greh kehte hain, jo SMILE scheme ke tahat chalte hain. November 2025 tak aise 21 shelters the, 17 states mein [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]], yaani India ke 36 states aur union territories mein se aadhe se bhi kam mein ek tha. August 2025 mein ministry ke support wale shelters mein 429 log reh rahe the [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Travel karne se pehle call kijiye, aur poochhiye ki shelter ko kaunse documents chahiye.

**10. Koi mujhe dhamka raha hai ya hurt kar raha hai. Kise call karun?**

Agar khatra abhi hai, toh 112 par call kijiye [[mha-erss]].
